payload.author: giezi
payload.body:
### Problem or use case

Provide a supported way to run the Orca runtime and orca CLI on a headless Linux server (no display, no GPU, no desktop) — without the Electron GUI.

This is the missing server-side counterpart to the existing "Remote Orca Servers" (BETA) feature. That feature already ships the client side: switching the active runtime from "Local desktop" to a paired remote runtime, saving servers (Add Server), and sharing revocable access grants.

But today the only thing a client can point at is another desktop instance with a GUI. There is no way to run that remote runtime headless on a server. Completing this makes "Remote Orca Servers" actually useful — you can run the runtime on a VPS / build box / container and pair into it.

The runtime is bundled inside the Electron desktop app. orca serve and the orca CLI therefore inherit Electron's hard dependency on a display server, which makes them unusable on a bare server.

Common scenarios where you want the runtime on the server, not driven from workstation, like Always-on orchestration — run orca automations / the coordinator loop 24/7 on a VPS, independent of any desktop being open.

### Proposed solution

Make orca serve deliver on what the help text already promises — a runtime that runs headless with no display dependency:

- Headless runtime / entrypoint — orca serve --headless (or a dedicated orca-server binary) that boots with no Electron window dependency and no xvfb. Ideally the runtime is factored out of the renderer so it can run on Node alone.

- Standalone CLI install — a way to install just the orca CLI on a host without the desktop app, pointed at a runtime via pairing code / environment (the flags already exist).

- Pairing into headless — a headless runtime can issue a pairing grant that a desktop client adds via Remote Orca Servers → Add Server and selects as its Active Server. This completes the existing BETA feature.

### Alternatives or additional context

Thanks for the awesome project! 🙌
payload.title: [Feature]: First-class headless / server mode for the Orca runtime

payload.body:
## Bug

On Windows, Orca orchestration can create and dispatch multiple worker agents successfully, but the workers do not appear in the Orca UI sidebar as child agents under the main/orchestrator agent. The same orchestration flow does show the subagents in the sidebar on macOS.

## Environment

- OS: Windows
- Orca repo: stablyai/orca
- Flow: `orca orchestration dispatch --inject` to multiple Codex worker terminals

## Observed

- Worker terminals are created and remain reachable through the Orca CLI.
- Orchestration tasks are dispatched and can complete.
- Agent hook status is recorded for the workers.
- The Windows sidebar does not show the dispatched workers as nested/child agents under the orchestrator.

## Expected

Windows should match macOS behavior: CLI-dispatched orchestration workers should appear in the sidebar as child/subagent rows under the orchestrator/main agent.

## Likely area

This appears to be a Windows-specific sidebar attribution/recovery bug for CLI-created background worker terminals, not a dispatch failure. The worker state exists in the runtime/orchestration/hook layers, but the renderer/sidebar does not recover or preserve the child-agent lineage reliably.
payload.title: Bug: Windows orchestration workers do not appear as sidebar child agents

### Operating system

Windows

### Orca version

1.4.32.0 / 1.4.33 (crash), 1.4.34 (crash), 1.4.35 (crash); last known good: 1.4.3 

### Details

### Operating system

Windows

### Orca version

1.4.32.0 / 1.4.33.0 (crash) / 1.4.34.0 (crash) / 1.4.35.0 (crash); last known good: 1.4.3

### Details

## Describe the bug
Orca crashes a few seconds after launch, every time. The window appears briefly, then closes. Reproducible 100% of the time. Reinstalling and wiping %APPDATA%\orca does not help.

**This is a regression:** version **1.4.3 runs fine and stable**, but **1.4.32, 1.4.33 1.4.34 1.4.35 crash** on the same machine.

## Environment
- Affected versions: 1.4.35.0, 1.4.34.0, 1.4.33.0 (crash). Last known good: **1.4.3** (stable)
- OS: Windows 11 Pro, build 26200 (verbld=26200, ubr 8457)
- RAM: 64 GB

## Crash signature (Windows Event Viewer / WER)
- Faulting module: ntdll.dll (10.0.26100.8328)
- Exception code: 0xc0000374 (heap corruption)
- Faulting offset: identical on every crash (0x117175)
- WER bucket: ca73297130f9a1744468adeee883d1a4

## What I've ruled out
- **Not GPU-related:** crashes the same with --disable-gpu, --disable-gpu-compositing, --no-sandbox, --disable-software-rasterizer.
- **Not a corrupt config:** wiped %APPDATA%\orca and %APPDATA%\orca\daemon, fresh reinstall — same crash.
- **Not an injected 3rd-party DLL:** the WER loaded-module list is clean — only Windows DLLs plus Orca's own native modules. No AV/overlay DLLs present.

## Likely culprit
The only non-Windows modules loaded at crash time are Orca's native addons:
- resources\app.asar.unpacked\node_modules\node-pty\build\Release\conpty.node
- resources\app.asar.unpacked\node_modules\cpu-features\build\Release\cpufeatures.node

The crash coincides with PTY/daemon init. Earlier launches logged:
Failed to start daemon PTY provider, falling back to local: Daemon exited during startup with code 1

Looks like a node-pty / ConPTY heap corruption during startup on recent Windows 11 builds (26200), introduced between 1.4.3 and 1.4.32.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Install Orca 1.4.32 or 1.4.33 on Windows 11 build 26200
2. Launch
3. App opens, then crashes within seconds with c0000374

## Workaround
Downgrading to 1.4.3 resolves it.

I can provide the full WER report, the .dmp, or stderr logs if useful.
payload.title: [Bug]: [Windows] Crash on startup since 1.4.32 — heap corruption (c0000374) in ntdll during native module init (regression, 1.4.3 works)

payload.author: noname-oni
payload.body:
Operating system: macOS

Orca version: 1.4.35

Details:

Short summary:
When using Pi inside an Orca-managed terminal/session, Orca sets `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` to a per-session overlay directory. As a result, running `pi install <extension>` appears to succeed, but the extension is installed into Orca’s temporary overlay rather than the user’s persistent `~/.pi/agent` config. After the Orca session/terminal is recreated, the installed extension is gone or not loaded as expected.

What happened?
In an Orca-managed terminal, the environment contains values like:

```bash
PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR="$HOME/Library/Application Support/orca/pi-agent-overlays/<pty-or-session-id>"
ORCA_PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR="$HOME/Library/Application Support/orca/pi-agent-overlays/<pty-or-session-id>"
ORCA_OMP_CODING_AGENT_DIR="$HOME/Library/Application Support/orca/omp-agent-overlays/<pty-or-session-id>"
```

Pi correctly respects `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`, so `pi install ...` writes into the Orca overlay. This creates a conflict between Orca’s injected Pi integration overlay and normal Pi CLI configuration commands.

The overlay includes Orca-managed extensions such as:

```text
orca-prefill.ts
orca-agent-status.ts
orca-titlebar-spinner.ts
```

Some files in the overlay appear to be symlinked back to the real Pi config, e.g. `settings.json`, `auth.json`, and `npm`, but `extensions/` is a real overlay directory. That means extension installs can land in the overlay and behave as if they are session-local.

How can we reproduce it?
1. Enable Orca agent hooks. In my case:
   ```bash
   orca agent hooks status
   ```
   reports:
   ```json
   {
     "enabled": true
   }
   ```

2. Open an Orca-managed terminal/session.

3. Check the Pi config environment:
   ```bash
   env | grep -E '^(PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR|ORCA_PI|ORCA_OMP)'
   ```

4. Observe that `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` points to an Orca overlay path, not `~/.pi/agent`.

5. Run:
   ```bash
   pi install <some-extension>
   ```

6. Pi reports the extension as installed, but it is installed relative to Orca’s overlay. After restarting/recreating the Orca terminal/session, the extension is not persistently available from the user’s normal Pi config.

Expected behavior:
Normal Pi CLI management commands like `pi install`, `pi remove`, `pi update`, and possibly `pi config` should not accidentally mutate an ephemeral Orca overlay unless the user explicitly asks for that.

Possible fixes / workarounds Orca could implement:
- Do not expose the overlay as `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` for arbitrary shell commands; only set it when launching the Pi TUI itself.
- Provide a wrapper/shim so `pi install`, `pi remove`, `pi update`, and `pi config` run against the original source dir, e.g. `~/.pi/agent`, while `pi` interactive sessions use the overlay.
- In the overlay, make user extension installs persist by linking or forwarding `extensions/` entries back to the source config, while still injecting Orca’s own extensions.
- Expose an `ORCA_PI_SOURCE_AGENT_DIR` and teach the shell wrapper to restore `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` to the source dir for non-interactive Pi config-management commands.
- At minimum, detect `pi install` in an Orca-managed terminal and warn that the install is targeting a temporary Orca overlay.

Current manual workaround:
Run installs with the real Pi config dir explicitly:

```bash
PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR="$HOME/.pi/agent" pi install <source>
```

or unset the Orca overlay environment variables:

```bash
env -u PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR \
    -u ORCA_PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR \
    -u ORCA_PI_SOURCE_AGENT_DIR \
    -u ORCA_OMP_CODING_AGENT_DIR \
    -u ORCA_OMP_SOURCE_AGENT_DIR \
    pi install <source>
```

Then restart the Orca Pi session so Orca rematerializes its overlay from the persistent config.

Anything else that might help:
This looks like an integration conflict rather than a Pi bug: Pi is behaving correctly by respecting `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`, but Orca’s overlay changes the meaning of normal Pi CLI management commands inside
payload.title: [Bug]: Pi extensions installed inside Orca overlay instead of persistent Pi config

payload.author: LesleyMurfin
payload.body:
### Operating system

Windows 10/11

### Orca version

v1.4.35+

### Details

`resolveCommandPath()` in `cli-installer.ts` returns:
```
%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Orca\bin\orca.cmd
```

But the actual CLI on disk after an Orca update is at:
```
%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Orca\resources\bin\orca.cmd
```

The `bin\orca.cmd` shim is wiped on updates. Users who rely on the shim path (or WSL bridge scripts pointing at it) lose CLI access after updating Orca.

**Evidence**: The WSL bridge script installed by Orca documents this explicitly in a comment:
> "After Orca updates, the `bin/orca.cmd` shim is wiped — point directly at the canonical CLI inside resources/"

This means `resolveCommandPath()` for win32 points at a path that becomes stale after every update.

### Suggested fix

Update `DEFAULT_WIN_COMMAND_PATH` (or equivalent) to use `resources\bin\orca.cmd` as the canonical path, or implement update-resilient path resolution that checks both locations.

**Related**: #3557 (macOS arm64 path issue — same class of hardcoded path bug)
payload.title: [Bug]: Windows CLI detection uses bin/orca.cmd but real path is resources/bin/orca.cmd after updates

payload.author: LesleyMurfin
payload.body:
### Context

Companion to #3557 (arm64 silent install failure). The Settings → CLI section has only a binary installed/not-installed display — when the install fails for any reason (missing directory, permission error, unsupported platform), nothing is shown to the user. The button appears to do nothing.

### Proposed change

Add an error state to the CLI Settings panel that:
- Shows the specific failure reason when Install is clicked and fails (e.g. "Failed to create /usr/local/bin — try running with administrator privileges" or "Directory /usr/local/bin does not exist on this system")
- Distinguishes between "not yet installed" and "install failed"

This is independent of the arm64 path fix in #3557 and would have surfaced that bug immediately during development.

### Why

Silent failure is indistinguishable from a hung operation. Any install failure should produce a user-visible error, not a silent no-op.

Discovered during investigation of #3557.
payload.title: [Feature]: Surface CLI install error in Settings UI when registration fails

payload.author: Jeet-Chugh
payload.body:
### Problem or use case

When I create a worktree from a Linear issue, Orca already stores the link (`WorktreeMeta.linkedLinearIssue`) and seeds the branch/prompt from the issue. But once I start working, the **worktree board** (the kanban with `Todo / In progress / In review / Done` lanes) and the **Linear issue's status** drift apart.

Today, dragging a worktree card between board lanes only writes `workspaceStatus` to local Orca metadata — it does **not** touch the linked Linear issue. So I end up updating the status twice: once on Orca's board, and again in Linear (or via Linear's own board). For a Linear-driven workflow this is exactly the kind of bookkeeping the tool should remove. The worktree *is* the unit of work for that issue, so its board column is the most natural, lowest-friction place to express "this issue is now in progress / in review / done."

**Summary:** When a worktree is linked to a Linear issue, moving that worktree between Orca board statuses should automatically transition the underlying Linear issue's workflow state.

### Proposed solution

When a worktree has a non-null `linkedLinearIssue` and the user drags it between board lanes, also push the corresponding state to Linear:

- `todo` → Linear `unstarted` (or `backlog`) state
- `in-progress` → Linear `started` state
- `in-review` → Linear `started` "In Review"–type state (fall back to the team's review state by name, else nearest `started`)
- `completed` → Linear `completed` / `Done` state

The good news is that nearly all the machinery already exists in the repo — this is mostly a matter of wiring two existing systems together:

1. **The drop handler that needs to gain the behavior:** `buildWorkspaceKanbanSidebarDropUpdates()` in `src/renderer/src/components/sidebar/workspace-kanban-sidebar-drop.ts` currently produces only `{ workspaceStatus: args.status }` updates to `WorktreeMeta`. It has no notion of the linked Linear issue.

2. **The exact sync already exists for the other board:** the standalone Linear issue board in `src/renderer/src/components/TaskPage.tsx` already does this — on drag it resolves the team's workflow states and calls `linearUpdateIssue(settings, issue.id, { stateId: workflowState.id }, issue.workspaceId)` (via `runtime-linear-client.ts`), using the helper `findLinearWorkflowStateForStatus(states, targetState)`. The same pattern can be reused from the worktree board's drop path, keyed off `worktree.linkedLinearIssue` instead of a Linear-issue card.

3. **The link and the API are already there:** `WorktreeMeta.linkedLinearIssue` (in `src/shared/types.ts`), `linearTeamStates` / `linearUpdateIssue` in the runtime Linear client, and the default statuses (`DEFAULT_WORKSPACE_STATUSES` in `src/shared/workspace-status-defaults.ts`) line up one-to-one with the four Linear state groups.

Suggested scope/behaviors:

- **Opt-in toggle** (e.g. in the workspace board / Linear settings): "Sync worktree board status to linked Linear issue." Default off to avoid surprising state writes.
- **Status → workflow-state mapping** that resolves against the issue's *team* states (teams can have custom states), reusing/extending `findLinearWorkflowStateForStatus`. Since Orca's board statuses are user-customizable (`WorkspaceStatusDefinition`), an optional explicit mapping field per workspace status (e.g. a target Linear state `type`/name) would make this robust for custom columns.
- **Optimistic update with rollback + toast on failure**, mirroring the existing Linear-board behavior (`patchLinearIssue` + revert on `result.ok === false`).
- **No-op when** the worktree has no `linkedLinearIssue`, the move doesn't change status, or no matching workflow state is found for the team (surface a toast like the existing board does).
- Only the worktree→Linear (push) direction is in scope here; the reverse is covered separately (see below).

### Alternatives or additional context

- **Workaround today:** manually update the issue in Linear, or use Orca's separat
payload.title: [Feature]: Sync worktree board status to linked Linear issue state (drag worktree → update Linear)

payload.author: LesleyMurfin
payload.body:
### Operating system

macOS (Apple Silicon / arm64)

### Orca version

v1.4.35

### Details

On Apple Silicon Macs, `/usr/local/bin` is never created by default because Homebrew moved to `/opt/homebrew`. The `/usr/local` directory exists but is owned by `root:wheel` with no `bin/` subdirectory.

**Settings → CLI → Install fails silently:** it tries to symlink to `/usr/local/bin/orca` but the parent directory doesn't exist. The "not installed" state persists with no error shown anywhere — not in the Settings UI, not in `~/Library/Application Support/orca/logs/main.trace.ndjson`, and not in the macOS unified log for the Orca process.

The CLI works fine when manually symlinked to `~/.local/bin` (which is on PATH via the user's shell config), but Orca's Settings check only looks at `/usr/local/bin` and never detects it.

**How to reproduce:**
1. Fresh Apple Silicon Mac (arm64) with Orca installed
2. Open Settings → CLI
3. Observe "not installed" state
4. Click Install — no error message appears, state does not change
5. Confirm: `ls /usr/local/bin` → "No such file or directory"

**Workaround:**
```bash
sudo mkdir -p /usr/local/bin
sudo ln -sf /Applications/Orca.app/Contents/Resources/bin/orca /usr/local/bin/orca
```

**Suggested fix:**
- Check whether `/usr/local/bin` exists before trying to install there; create it or fall back gracefully
- On `arm64`, prefer `~/.local/bin` as the install target (user-writable, XDG standard, no `sudo` required) or detect and use `$(brew --prefix)/bin`
- Surface any install failure with a user-facing error message in the Settings UI

**Related:** #2144 is the same class of bug on Windows — Orca's hardcoded path probe list misses user-level PATH entries.
payload.title: [Bug]: CLI install fails silently on Apple Silicon (arm64) — /usr/local/bin does not exist

payload.author: ozekishigeo
payload.body:
### Operating system

macOS

### Orca version

v1.4.35 (Homebrew cask `stablyai/orca/orca`)

### Details

#### Short summary
On a clean macOS 26.3.1 (Tahoe, Apple Silicon M3) machine with no prior Orca install, launching Orca v1.4.35 results in the process exiting silently ~400ms after start, before any window is shown and before the userData directory is created. Re-launching produces identical behavior.

#### What happened
- `brew install --cask stablyai/orca/orca` succeeded (v1.4.35)
- `open -a Orca` (and equivalents) → app enters `running-active`, transitions through `NotVisible`, then exits cleanly (no crash report)
- No window ever appears
- No userData directory created at `~/Library/Application Support/orca` (lowercase per `package.json`) nor `Orca`
- No `~/Library/Logs/Orca` written
- Only stderr output during the entire app lifetime:
  ```
  [ERROR:electron/shell/common/mac/codesign_util.cc:79] task_name_for_pid: (os/kern) failure (5)
  ```
- No other Orca / `Orca Helper` / daemon process exists before launch (verified via `pgrep -fl -i orca` and `ps aux`)
- Code signature is valid and notarized:
  ```
  spctl: source=Notarized Developer ID
  origin=Developer ID Application: Lovecast LLC (6CX3WHS9HZ)
  ```

#### Root cause (from inspecting the bundled `out/main/index.js`)
The early exit path at `out/main/index.js:103342-103350` is being hit:

```js
const hasSingleInstanceLock = utils.is.dev && !isServeMode
  ? true
  : acquireSingleInstanceLock(electron.app, focusExistingWindow);
if (!hasSingleInstanceLock) {
  if (utils.is.dev) { console.log("[single-instance] ...") }
  electron.app.quit();
}
```

`acquireSingleInstanceLock` (line 93774) simply wraps `app.requestSingleInstanceLock()`. On this macOS 26.3.1 + Electron 41.5.0 combination, the call returns `false` even though no other Orca instance exists. Production builds emit no log in this branch, which is why the failure looks completely silent.

This may be related to known Electron + Tahoe (macOS 26) Cocoa interop regressions, but the specific `requestSingleInstanceLock`-returning-false case doesn't seem to be tracked yet.

#### Reproduction
1. macOS 26.3.1 (build 25D771280a) on Apple Silicon, fully clean of any prior Orca state
2. `brew install --cask stablyai/orca/orca` (gets v1.4.35)
3. `open -a Orca`
4. Window never appears; `pgrep orca` shows nothing within ~1s
5. Verify with: `ELECTRON_ENABLE_LOGGING=1 open -W --stdout /tmp/o.out --stderr /tmp/o.err -a Orca` — `/tmp/o.err` will contain only the `codesign_util` warning

#### Suggested next step for triage
In the production build, log a single line on the `app.quit()` path in `index.js:103349` even when not in dev, so users hitting this don't see a silent exit. Beyond that, the underlying issue is most likely on the Electron 41 / macOS 26 side and may need an Electron upgrade.

#### Environment
- macOS 26.3.1 (build 25D771280a, beta marker `(a)`)
- Apple M3
- Orca 1.4.35
- Bundled: Electron 41.5.0, Chromium 146.0.7680.216
- Code signed by Lovecast LLC (6CX3WHS9HZ), notarized
payload.title: [Bug]: v1.4.35 quits ~400ms after launch on macOS 26.3.1 (Tahoe) — single-instance lock acquisition fails on first run

### Operating system

macOS

### Orca version

1.4.34

### Details

[mouse_probe.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28412383/mouse_probe.py)

**Short summary:**
  Touch gestures are sent as mouse-wheel events instead of clicks, so mouse-driven TUIs can't register taps.

  **What happened?**
  When a terminal app enables SGR mouse tracking (`\x1b[?1000h` / `\x1b[?1006h`), tapping/dragging in Orca Mobile is delivered
  as mouse-wheel events (button code 64 = wheel-up, 65 = wheel-down), never as a left-click (code 0). Because mouse-clickable
  TUIs (e.g. Textual buttons) fire on a left button press+release, the buttons never respond. Only scrolling works; keyboard
  input works fine.

  Setup: iPhone 16 Pro Max → Orca Mobile → remote session → program. No tmux involved (direct connection).

  **How can we reproduce it?**
  1. Run a small program that enables SGR mouse mode (`\x1b[?1000h\x1b[?1006h`) and prints raw stdin bytes.
  2. Tap or drag anywhere on the screen.
  3. Observe that only wheel codes arrive — e.g. `\x1b[<64;38;20M`, `\x1b[<65;36;29M` — and no left-click sequence (`\x1b[<0;…M`
  press / `\x1b[<0;…m` release) is ever emitted.

  **Anything else that might help:**
  Expected: a tap should emit a left-button press + release, e.g. `\x1b[<0;38;20M` then `\x1b[<0;38;20m`. Ideally a "tap to
  click" / pointer mode (or a toggle for touch→click vs touch→scroll) so mouse-driven TUIs work.
payload.title: [Bug]: Touch gestures from mobile app send only mouse-wheel events instead of clicks (SGR mouse mode)

payload.author: mubeda
payload.body:
### Operating system

Windows 11

### Orca version

1.4.33.0

### Details

### Summary
On Windows, closing the Orca window does not fully terminate the app. The main
process and/or spawned child processes (the codex CLI, Node helpers, terminal/PTY
processes) keep running in the background. Relaunching while a stale instance is
alive leads to overlapping state writes (see the primary issue) and, in some cases,
a new window that doesn't behave as a clean start.

### Steps to reproduce

Run a Codex agent / start a task in Orca on Windows.
Close the Orca window with the X.
Open Task Manager (or Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "Name LIKE '%orca%' OR Name='codex.exe'").
### 
Actual behavior
One or more Orca / codex / Node / PTY processes remain running after the window
is closed. They are not cleaned up and must be killed manually (taskkill /T) to get
a fully clean relaunch.
Expected behavior

Closing/quitting Orca should terminate the full process tree it owns (main +
spawned agent/terminal children), or
If background runs are intentionally kept alive, provide a clear "Quit Orca" action
and an indicator that background agent processes are still running, plus a reliable
way to stop them all.

### Notes
This is consistent with a documented Codex-on-Windows lifecycle problem: the UI window
closes but background processes remain, blocking relaunch, recoverable only by killing
the leftover processes in Task Manager.

Because Orca manages the Codex runtime (codex-runtime-home), this lifecycle bug is
likely the trigger for the duplicate-[hooks.state] corruption in the primary issue. 
Issue #3190
payload.title: [Bug]: Orca process (and spawned Codex/agent children) keeps running after window close, blocking clean relaunch

payload.author: mubeda
payload.body:
### Operating system

Windows 11

### Orca version

1.4.33.0

### Details

### SUMMARY 

On Windows, Orca's managed Codex config at
%APPDATA%\orca\codex-runtime-home\home\config.toml accumulates duplicate
[hooks.state."<abs-path-to-hooks.json>:<event>:<i>:<j>"] tables across
close/reopen cycles. Because duplicate keys/tables are invalid in TOML, the next
launch fails to parse the file and the agent will not start.
This looks like an append-instead-of-update serializer bug: hook-trust state
is re-written (appended) on shutdown rather than replaced in place, so the same
quoted-path key is emitted more than once. It is very likely compounded by the
process-lifecycle bug described in the optional second issue (a stale Orca/Codex
process surviving window close means two writers touch the same file).

### Steps to reproduce

Use Codex in Orca in a workspace that has a hooks.json with a SessionStart
(session_start) hook, so Orca persists hook-trust state.
Close the Orca window.
Reopen Orca (or relaunch the Codex agent in the same workspace).
Repeat the close→reopen cycle a few times.

Actual behavior
Codex fails to start and emits a TOML parse error pointing at a [hooks.state."…"]
table. Example (line number varies as duplicates accumulate; username redacted):
```
    |
145 | [hooks.state."C:\\Users\\<USER>\\AppData\\Roaming\\orca\\codex-runtime-home\\home\\hooks.json:session_start:0:0"]
    |              ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
```
Inspecting config.toml shows the same [hooks.state."…hooks.json:session_start:0:0"]
header present two or more times. Removing the duplicate header(s) and relaunching
resolves it immediately — until the next close→reopen cycle reintroduces the duplicate.
Expected behavior

Hook-trust state should be updated in place (one table per unique hook key),
never appended as a duplicate.
If a malformed/duplicate config.toml is encountered on startup, Orca should
surface a clear, recoverable error (and ideally self-heal the managed file it owns)
rather than failing the agent launch.

### Suspected root cause

The [hooks.state] serializer appends a new table per shutdown instead of
replacing the existing entry keyed by the absolute hooks.json path + event +
indices.
A stale Orca/Codex process surviving window close (see optional second issue)
causes overlapping writes to the same config.toml, increasing the chance of
duplication.
payload.title: [Bug]: Duplicate [hooks.state."…"] tables accumulate in codex-runtime-home/config.toml on every close→reopen, breaking Codex startup

payload.author: Fybex
payload.body:
### Problem or use case

Recently switched to Orca from [cmux](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux) and — loving the product so far — there are a few muscle-memory hotkeys I miss. (The focus here is the proposal below, not the comparison.)

**Correction to an earlier version of this issue:** workspace switching by number (`⌘1…9`) *already exists* in Orca — it shipped in #394 ("Cmd+1–9 worktree switching with hint overlay") and was later moved to main-process interception in #469. It's intentionally hardcoded (not in the customizable shortcuts catalog and not shown in Settings). So that ask is already covered. 🎉

What's still missing is the **tab-level** equivalent and **keyboard rename** for both tabs and workspaces:
- No way to jump to a tab by number within the current workspace.
- No keyboard shortcut to rename a tab or rename a workspace — rename is reachable via double-click / context menu, but not the keyboard.

### Proposed solution

Three additions:

- `⌃1…9` — jump to tab N within the current workspace (the `⌃` counterpart to the existing `⌘1…9` workspace jump). Like the workspace jump, this should survive terminal focus, so it likely belongs in the same main-process interception path rather than the rebindable catalog.
- `⌘R` — rename the active tab.
- `⌘⇧R` — rename the active workspace.

For reference, cmux ships all of these — see its [shortcut list](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/blob/main/web/data/cmux-shortcuts.ts) (`selectSurfaceByNumber`, `renameTab`, `renameWorkspace`).

### Alternatives or additional context

- **Cross-platform:** on Windows/Linux the existing workspace jump is already `Ctrl+1…9` (primary modifier), so a tab jump there can't reuse `Ctrl+1…9` — it'd need a different modifier (e.g. `Alt+1…9`). macOS is clean (`⌘` vs `⌃`).
- The two renames are app-context actions and fit the customizable catalog (#2581); `⌘R` / `⌘⇧R` overlap with `browser.reload` / `app.forceReload`, which can be resolved by scoping rename to app focus (as cmux does) and/or shipping the rename defaults unbound on platforms where they'd collide.
- Related: #2808 (keyboard shortcut to delete current workspace).
payload.title: [Feature]: Number-jump and inline-rename shortcuts for tabs & workspaces

payload.author: ryanmargono
payload.body:
## Problem or use case

Orca's primary interaction model today is worktree- and terminal-centric. For many agent workflows—especially quick prompts, follow-ups, and mobile check-ins—a dedicated chat surface would be a more natural primary UI than navigating terminals and file trees.

A chat-based UI would let users converse with agents in a familiar message thread, see streaming responses in one place, and send follow-ups without re-focusing a terminal pane.

## Proposed solution

Add a first-class chat-based UI in Orca as an alternative (or complementary) interaction surface for agent work:

- Message-thread view with streaming agent output
- Follow-up prompts in the same conversation context
- Clear linkage between a chat thread and its backing worktree/terminal/session
- Usable from desktop and mobile for lightweight agent steering

This would improve discoverability for users who think in terms of "talk to the agent" rather than "manage terminals and worktrees."

## Alternatives or additional context

**Reference OSS:** [Paseo](https://github.com/getpaseo/paseo) implements a chat-first interface for coding agents across Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, OpenCode, and Pi—with desktop, mobile, web, and CLI clients connecting to a local daemon. Worth studying for UX patterns around multi-provider agent chat, cross-device continuity, and voice/hands-free interaction.

- https://github.com/getpaseo/paseo
- https://paseo.sh/docs
payload.title: [Feature]: Chat-based UI

payload.author: plozmun
payload.body:
### Problem or use case

Orca already supports multiple forge/VCS hosting providers under `src/main/`:

* `src/main/github/`
* `src/main/gitlab/`
* `src/main/gitea/`

These providers already expose very similar capabilities:

* fetch PRs/MRs
* inspect CI status
* associate branches/worktrees with remote tasks
* resolve repository metadata

However, they currently appear to operate as independent implementations without a shared TypeScript contract binding them together.

That works well today, but it creates an implicit API surface that consumers must understand manually.

As more integrations appear, this becomes harder to maintain because:

* worktree/UI logic must branch on concrete provider types
* adding new providers requires reverse-engineering existing implementations
* compile-time guarantees are lost
* provider capabilities become inconsistent over time



### Proposed solution

Now that Orca already has multiple implementations, it may be a good moment to extract the shared behavior into a small additive interface.

Something along these lines:

```ts
// src/main/forge/ForgeProvider.ts

export interface PullRequest {
  id: string
  number: number
  title: string
  url: string
  state: 'open' | 'closed' | 'merged'
  headBranch: string
  baseBranch: string
}

export interface CiCheck {
  name: string
  status:
    | 'pending'
    | 'running'
    | 'success'
    | 'failure'
    | 'skipped'

  url?: string
}

export interface ForgeProvider {
  /** Whether this provider supports the given remote URL */
  handles(remoteUrl: string): boolean

  getPullRequestForBranch(
    branch: string
  ): Promise<PullRequest | null>

  createPullRequest(
    opts: CreatePrOptions
  ): Promise<PullRequest>

  listCiChecks(
    branch: string
  ): Promise<CiCheck[]>
}
```

Then:

* `GitHubProvider`
* `GitLabProvider`
* `GiteaProvider`

would simply implement the shared interface.

The important part is not the exact shape of the API, but making the currently implicit contract explicit and type-checked.

## Why this helps

### Easier provider additions

New providers become much easier to implement:

* Forgejo
* Bitbucket
* Azure DevOps
* self-hosted internal forges

A contributor can implement a known interface instead of tracing provider-specific behavior through the codebase.

### Cleaner UI/worktree orchestration

Consumers can operate against capabilities instead of concrete provider types.

This reduces branching logic and avoids provider-specific checks spreading through the UI layer.

### Safer evolution

Today, capability drift between providers is mostly a runtime concern.

A shared interface would move many of those inconsistencies to compile-time errors instead.

### Natural path toward issue tracker integrations

This pattern could later extend naturally to:

```ts
interface IssueTrackerProvider
```

for integrations such as:

* Linear (#370)
* Jira
* GitHub Issues
* GitLab Issues

without coupling task orchestration directly to a specific forge implementation.

## What this does NOT require

This could remain entirely incremental:

* no DI/container rewrite
* no plugin system
* no behavior changes
* no registry refactor
* no breaking API changes

Existing providers would simply formalize the contract they already mostly share today.



### Alternatives or additional context

_No response_
payload.title: [Feature]: Introduce a shared ForgeProvider interface for VCS hosting integrations

payload.author: thebizfixer
payload.body:
### Summary

When **Agent Orchestration** is enabled, unread orchestration mail is delivered on **terminal idle** by writing formatted text into the Orca-managed **PTY** and sending **Enter** after a short delay (~500ms). That is reasonable for coordinator-driven CLI agents, but it is disruptive when the recipient is a **Cursor Agent** tab inside Orca: the operator sees blocks like `--- Orchestration Messages (N) ---` in what feels like their "prompt," often right after they stop typing or when they submit — because delivery is tied to idle, not to an explicit "read mail" action.

This is easy to confuse with **Cursor IDE** chat injection; in our case the affected surface is an **Orca terminal running Cursor Agent**, not the separate Cursor desktop app.

### Environment

- **Orca version:** 24.15.0 (Windows desktop)
- **OS:** Windows 10
- **Agent:** Cursor Agent in an Orca terminal tab
- **Orchestration:** Experimental → Agent Orchestration (localStorage `orca.orchestration.enabled`)
- **Agent status hooks:** Separate toggle (`agentStatusHooksEnabled` / `orca agent hooks on|off`) — we understand this is **not** the same feature as orchestration mail, but both were enabled during debugging

### Steps to reproduce

1. Enable **Settings → Experimental → Agent Orchestration** (`orca.orchestration.enabled` = `"1"`).
2. Open a worktree terminal running **Cursor Agent** (CLI in Orca).
3. From another terminal or Hermes/coordinator, send orchestration mail to that terminal handle, e.g.  
   `orca orchestration send --to <cursor-terminal-handle> --subject "status" --body "…" --type status`
4. In the Cursor Agent tab, compose a long prompt or finish a turn and go idle.
5. Observe orchestration banner text injected into the PTY; after ~500ms, **Enter** is sent and the composed/injected text is **submitted** without an explicit user action.

### Expected behavior

One or more of (product choice):

- **No auto-Enter** for orchestration idle delivery (inject text only; user submits manually), and/or
- **Per-terminal opt-out** from push-on-idle (e.g. "do not deliver orchestration mail to this tab"), and/or
- **Do not target** terminals whose agent type is Cursor (or other IDE-embedded agents) for push-on-idle, and/or
- Clear UI copy that orchestration mail is delivered to **Orca terminal PTYs** and may auto-submit CLI prompts.

### Actual behavior

- Idle delivery injects `formatMessagesForInjection` output (banner `--- Orchestration Messages (N) ---` plus bodies).
- Enter is sent automatically after a delay (documented/intentional for dispatch inject in PR #1188; same path hurts interactive Cursor Agent use).
- Mail can appear to "interrupt" composition because delivery waits for **idle**, not for an explicit check.

### What we tried (workarounds)

- `orca agent hooks off` — removes Cursor `hooks.json` entries; **does not** stop orchestration mail injection.
- `orca orchestration reset --messages` — clears queue; does not change idle push behavior.
- Turn off **Agent Orchestration** in Settings (`orca.orchestration.enabled` = `"0"`) — stops the behavior.
- Avoid `orca orchestration send` to the operator's Cursor Agent handle; use git/PR handoff instead.

### Related upstream context

- Push-on-idle + split write + 500ms Enter: [PR #1188](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/pull/1188) (orchestration MVP).
- Replay fix for re-injecting delivered unread mail: [PR #2003](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/pull/2003) (adjacent, not the same ask).
- Feature request to inject into **active** session (opposite framing): [#2909](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/issues/2909).
- Hooks / PTY layering: [#1308](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/issues/1308).

We did **not** find an existing issue for "orchestration idle delivery auto-submits into Cursor Agent terminal."

### Suggested fix (engineering)

- Gate `deliverPendingMessagesForHandle` / post-inject Enter on agent type, terminal metadata flag, or user setting ("inject without submit").
- CLI: `orca or
payload.title: Agent Orchestration idle delivery auto-submits into Cursor Agent terminal; need per-terminal opt-out or inject-without-Enter

payload.author: erginbey
payload.body:
## Summary

Orca's Monaco editor currently opens .bat and .cmd files as plaintext — no syntax highlighting, no IntelliSense. Since Orca targets Windows developers (the README lists Windows as a supported platform), supporting Windows Batch files would complete the experience.

## Current State

- src/renderer/src/lib/language-detect.ts has no mapping for .bat or .cmd — they fall through to plaintext
- Monaco's built-in languages include shell (POSIX/Bash) which is close but semantically wrong for Batch syntax

## Requested

1. Syntax highlighting — register a custom Batch language using Monaco's Monarch tokenizer (similar to existing register-vue.ts, register-svelte.ts, register-astro.ts in src/renderer/src/lib/monaco-languages/)
2. Language configuration — auto-closing pairs, bracket matching, comment toggling for Batch
3. File extension mapping — add .bat -> batch and .cmd -> batch to language-detect.ts

## Batch Syntax Features a Tokenizer Should Cover

- Control keywords: @echo, setlocal, endlocal, if, else, for, in, do, call, exit, goto, set, cd, dir, copy, del, move, type, find, pause, shift, title, color, mode, pushd, popd, start, timeout, choice, where
- Variables: %VAR% (expansion), !VAR! (delayed expansion), %~dp0, %~f0
- Labels: :label, ::comment-label
- Operators: >, >>, <, |, &&, ||
- Escaping: ^^, ^|, ^&, ^<, ^>
- Strings: double-quoted
- Comments: REM (line-level)

## Implementation Reference

The existing custom language files follow this pattern:

monaco.languages.register({
  id: 'batch',
  extensions: ['.bat', '.cmd'],
  aliases: ['Batch', 'Windows Batch']
})
monaco.languages.setMonarchTokensProvider('batch', batchMonarchLanguage)
monaco.languages.setLanguageConfiguration('batch', batchLanguageConfiguration)

A Monarch tokenizer for Batch is roughly 100-150 lines. Happy to contribute a PR if that helps.
payload.title: feat: add syntax highlighting and IntelliSense for .bat/.cmd (Windows Batch) files

payload.author: DEV-Johnstocker
payload.body:
## Bug Description

When Orca opens a PowerShell (or cmd) terminal, it injects both `orca-terminal-attribution/posix` and `orca-terminal-attribution/win32` into PATH for git attribution. In a Windows terminal, the extensionless `posix/git` bash script is found by PATH resolution before the real `git.exe`, and since Windows has no native handler for extensionless shebang scripts, it pops up an **\"Open With\" dialog** showing the raw script content and asking the user to choose an application.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install Orca on Windows with default PowerShell terminal
2. Open any Orca terminal (not Git Bash — no Git Bash option is offered)
3. Run any git command (e.g. `git status`)
4. The \"Open With\" dialog appears showing the contents of `orca-terminal-attribution/posix/git`

## Root Cause

`posix/git` is a `#!/usr/bin/env bash` script with no file extension. Windows PATHEXT does not include extensionless files, but Windows still attempts to open the file via shell association when it's the first match on PATH — resulting in the dialog.

The `win32/` directory already has the correct `git.cmd` + `git-wrapper.ps1` wrappers for Windows terminals, but `posix/` is also being injected into PATH regardless of terminal type.

## Expected Behavior

The `posix/` directory should only be injected into PATH when the terminal shell is bash/zsh/sh (e.g. Git Bash, WSL). For PowerShell/cmd terminals, only `win32/` should be on PATH.

## Workaround

Adding a `git.cmd` to `posix/` that delegates to `win32/git-wrapper.ps1` resolves the issue immediately, since Windows PATHEXT prefers `.cmd` over extensionless files:

```batch
@echo off
setlocal
if not "%ORCA_ENABLE_GIT_ATTRIBUTION%"=="1" goto run
if "%ORCA_ATTRIBUTION_BYPASS%"=="1" goto run
call :orca_is_git_commit %*
if errorlevel 1 goto run
powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "%~dp0..\win32\git-wrapper.ps1" %*
exit /b %ERRORLEVEL%
:run
if defined ORCA_REAL_GIT (
  "%ORCA_REAL_GIT%" %*
) else (
  echo Orca attribution wrapper could not locate git on PATH. 1>&2
  exit /b 127
)
exit /b %ERRORLEVEL%
:orca_is_git_commit
... (same logic as win32/git.cmd)
```

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11 Home
- Shell: PowerShell (default)
- Orca version: latest

Made with [Orca](https://github.com/stablyai/orca) 🐋
payload.title: Windows: posix/git attribution wrapper triggers 'Open With' dialog in PowerShell terminals

payload.author: marnific
payload.body:
### Operating system

Windows

### Orca version

1.4.32.0 / 1.4.33.0 (crash); last known good: 1.4.3

### Details

## Describe the bug
Orca crashes a few seconds after launch, every time. The window appears briefly, then closes. Reproducible 100% of the time. Reinstalling and wiping %APPDATA%\orca does not help.

**This is a regression:** version **1.4.3 runs fine and stable**, but **1.4.32 and 1.4.33 crash** on the same machine.

## Environment
- Affected versions: 1.4.32.0, 1.4.33.0 (crash). Last known good: **1.4.3** (stable)
- OS: Windows 11 Pro, build 26200 (verbld=26200, ubr 8457)
- RAM: 64 GB

## Crash signature (Windows Event Viewer / WER)
- Faulting module: ntdll.dll (10.0.26100.8328)
- Exception code: 0xc0000374 (heap corruption)
- Faulting offset: identical on every crash (0x117175)
- WER bucket: ca73297130f9a1744468adeee883d1a4

## What I've ruled out
- **Not GPU-related:** crashes the same with --disable-gpu, --disable-gpu-compositing, --no-sandbox, --disable-software-rasterizer.
- **Not a corrupt config:** wiped %APPDATA%\orca and %APPDATA%\orca\daemon, fresh reinstall — same crash.
- **Not an injected 3rd-party DLL:** the WER loaded-module list is clean — only Windows DLLs plus Orca's own native modules. No AV/overlay DLLs present.

## Likely culprit
The only non-Windows modules loaded at crash time are Orca's native addons:
- resources\app.asar.unpacked\node_modules\node-pty\build\Release\conpty.node
- resources\app.asar.unpacked\node_modules\cpu-features\build\Release\cpufeatures.node

The crash coincides with PTY/daemon init. Earlier launches logged:
Failed to start daemon PTY provider, falling back to local: Daemon exited during startup with code 1

Looks like a node-pty / ConPTY heap corruption during startup on recent Windows 11 builds (26200), introduced between 1.4.3 and 1.4.32.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Install Orca 1.4.32 or 1.4.33 on Windows 11 build 26200
2. Launch
3. App opens, then crashes within seconds with c0000374

## Workaround
Downgrading to 1.4.3 resolves it.

I can provide the full WER report, the .dmp, or stderr logs if useful.
payload.title: [Windows] Crash on startup since 1.4.32 — heap corruption (c0000374) in ntdll during native module init (regression, 1.4.3 works)

payload.author: kenlin8827
payload.body:
## Problem

When working with many tabs open (terminals, browsers, editors, etc.), important tabs easily get lost in the crowd or get accidentally closed. There is currently no way to "pin" critical tabs, making tab management difficult in multi-tab workflows.

This is especially painful when you have long-running processes (dev servers, watch tasks, Docker logs) that you absolutely do not want to close by mistake, but they get buried among dozens of other tabs.

## Proposal

Add a **Pin Tab** feature, similar to browser pin-tab behavior:

### Core Behavior
1. **Right-click context menu** — Add "Pin Tab" option
2. **Pinned tabs**:
   - Shrink to icon-only form, aligned to the leftmost side of the tab bar
   - **Cannot be closed** — close button is hidden or disabled to prevent accidental closure
   - Cannot be drag-reordered
   - When new tabs are opened, pinned tabs stay in place
3. **Unpin** — Right-click menu adds "Unpin Tab" to restore a tab to normal state

### Keyboard Shortcut
- `Ctrl+Shift+P` (or configurable) — Toggle pin state of the current tab

### Visual Differentiation
- Pinned tabs display as compact, icon-only (no text title)
- Optional: subtle background color or border to distinguish pinned tabs

## Use Cases

- 🖥️ **Long-running terminals** (dev servers, watch processes) — prevent accidental closure
- 📌 **Always-needed tool tabs** (Git status, Docker logs) — quick access, always visible
- 🔄 **Frequent switching** — pinned tabs stay leftmost for one-click access

## References

Similar functionality exists in:
- **Chrome / Edge** — Pin Tab
- **VS Code** — Pinned Tabs
- **iTerm2** — Pin Session

---

This would be a huge UX improvement for power users who work with many tabs. Thanks for considering! 🙏
payload.title: Feature: Pin tabs to prevent accidental closure and keep important tabs visible

After downloading the Orca AppImage, it then sets up the CLI/bin at `$HOME/.local/opt/stably-orca/resources/bin/orca`.

This is primarily an issue for people using Orca on Linux via the AppImage who want their agents to use the Orca CLI (ie for reading other terminals' pty/stdin and stdout and things of that nature).

The theoretical workaround would be to set a shortcut to launch from the installed binary but this should already be done for the user.

payload.author: tmchow
payload.body:
## Summary
Quick Open filters and sorts the entire file list on every keystroke

**Category:** performance  ·  **Severity:** high  ·  **Confidence:** high  ·  **Affects:** macOS, Linux, Windows

## Impact
Quick Open re-filters and re-sorts the entire file list on every keystroke with no debounce, causing visible input lag in large repositories.

## Location
`src/renderer/src/components/QuickOpen.tsx:24-56` (line numbers as of `main` at filing)

## Reproduction
Open Quick Open on a worktree with a very large file list, such as a monorepo or remote SSH checkout with 100k+ files. Type a common character like `t`. The renderer must scan every path and sort all matches before it can update results, causing visible input lag or stalls.

## Suggested fix
Precompute normalized searchable fields when files are loaded, and replace full-result sorting with a bounded top-k selector for the first 50 results. For very large lists, debounce and/or move matching to a Web Worker so keystrokes remain responsive.

**Minimum fix scope:** Limit the change to QuickOpen search preparation/ranking: cache lowercase filename/path data, use top-k selection, and keep the rendered API unchanged.

## Why existing tests miss it
No QuickOpen performance or large-list tests were included with this feature, and ordinary functional tests usually use tiny file arrays that do not expose renderer-thread stalls.

## Suggested regression test
Add a QuickOpen ranking test or benchmark with 100k synthetic paths that asserts filtering returns within a small budget and does not sort the full match set before applying the result limit.
payload.title: [Bug]: Quick Open filters and sorts the entire file list on every keystroke

payload.author: tmchow
payload.body:
## Summary
Re-registering SSH handlers strands existing port forwards

**Category:** performance  ·  **Severity:** high  ·  **Confidence:** high  ·  **Affects:** macOS, Linux, Windows

## Impact
Re-registering SSH IPC handlers (e.g. on macOS window reactivation) orphans live port forwards, leaking listeners and blocking rebind/removal of the same port.

## Location
`src/main/ipc/ssh.ts:63-63` (line numbers as of `main` at filing)

## Reproduction
Connect an SSH target, add a local port forward, close all windows on macOS so the app remains alive, then reactivate Orca. registerSshHandlers runs again. ssh:listPortForwards now reads the new empty manager, ssh:removePortForward cannot remove the old id, and ssh:disconnect does not close the old listener. Attempting to add or restore the same local port fails because the old server is still bound.

## Suggested fix
Make SSH registration preserve or explicitly dispose session-owned state across window reactivation. The smallest safe direction is to keep a single portForwardManager/connectionManager for the process lifetime and update a current getMainWindow reference used by callbacks, rather than replacing managers while activeSessions exist. If replacement is required, first dispose/detach active sessions and await old port-forward teardown.

**Minimum fix scope:** src/main/ipc/ssh.ts registration lifecycle plus a focused SSH IPC regression test.

## Why existing tests miss it
ssh.test.ts covers connect, disconnect, removeTarget, resetRelay, and relay-loss behavior, but it does not create a port forward and then call registerSshHandlers a second time. register-core-handlers.test.ts only proves core handlers are guarded once; SSH handlers are registered from attach-main-window-services on each window attachment and have their own re-registration path.

## Suggested regression test
In src/main/ipc/ssh.test.ts, connect a target, add a mocked forward, call registerSshHandlers again, then assert either the forward remains listed/removable through IPC or the old manager's removeAllForwards/dispose path was invoked before replacement. Also assert disconnect after re-registration closes the original forward manager.
payload.title: [Bug]: Re-registering SSH handlers strands existing port forwards

payload.author: tmchow
payload.body:
## Summary
Eager PTY buffer trimming is quadratic and can exceed its cap

**Category:** performance  ·  **Severity:** high  ·  **Confidence:** high  ·  **Affects:** macOS, Linux, Windows

## Impact
Per-chunk array shifting is O(n^2), and a single large chunk bypasses the cap entirely — freezing the renderer and growing memory unboundedly on noisy PTY output.

## Location
`src/renderer/src/components/terminal-pane/pty-dispatcher.ts:162-165` (line numbers as of `main` at filing)

## Reproduction
Register an eager buffer for a PTY and deliver more than 512 KiB as many one-byte pty:data chunks before attaching the pane. After the cap is reached, every further chunk shifts a roughly 512k-element array. Alternatively, deliver one multi-megabyte chunk; the while condition cannot trim it because buffer.length is 1, so the eager buffer stores the whole payload.

## Suggested fix
Replace the string array plus shift trimming with a bounded deque/ring buffer or a start-index queue that trims without reindexing. Enforce the cap for a single oversized chunk by slicing the tail of that chunk or splitting chunks before enqueueing.

**Minimum fix scope:** Change registerEagerPtyBuffer's internal buffering implementation and add focused tests for cap enforcement and many-chunk trimming.

## Why existing tests miss it
Existing eager-buffer tests cover replay routing, attention suppression, and clear-before-replay behavior, but they do not stress many small chunks or one oversized chunk to verify time complexity and the actual memory cap.

## Suggested regression test
Add a pty-dispatcher or pty-transport test that feeds an eager buffer one oversized chunk and many small chunks, then verifies flush output is capped to the newest 512 KiB without using Array.shift-like behavior.
payload.title: [Bug]: Eager PTY buffer trimming is quadratic and can exceed its cap

payload.author: tmchow
payload.body:
## Summary
Short stream chunks silently zero-fill remote file reads

**Category:** data-loss  ·  **Severity:** high  ·  **Confidence:** high  ·  **Affects:** macOS, Linux, Windows

## Impact
A short or missing stream chunk resolves a remote file read with zero-filled bytes instead of erroring — silent corruption of read data.

## Location
`src/main/ssh/ssh-filesystem-stream-reader.ts:129-143` (line numbers as of `main` at filing)

## Reproduction
Stub mux.request('fs.readFileStream') to return { streamId: 1, totalSize: STREAM_CHUNK_SIZE * 2, isBinary: true, resultEncoding: 'base64' }. Emit fs.streamChunk seq 0 with STREAM_CHUNK_SIZE bytes, emit fs.streamChunk seq 1 with one byte, then fs.streamEnd. The promise resolves even though only STREAM_CHUNK_SIZE + 1 bytes arrived, returning a Buffer-equivalent with zero-filled missing bytes.

## Suggested fix
Track decoded byte count and validate exact coverage before resolving. Reject any non-final chunk whose decoded length is not STREAM_CHUNK_SIZE, reject a final chunk whose decoded length is not totalSize - offset, and reject streamEnd unless bytesReceived === totalSize.

**Minimum fix scope:** src/main/ssh/ssh-filesystem-stream-reader.ts plus the streaming provider test file.

## Why existing tests miss it
The existing stream tests cover out-of-order chunks, totalSize caps, stream errors, and chunk count mismatch, but not short chunks that keep the expected chunk count.

## Suggested regression test
Add a readFileViaStream/SshFilesystemProvider streaming test where metadata declares two chunks but the second chunk is shorter than the declared remaining bytes; assert the read rejects with StreamProtocolError instead of resolving with zero padding.
payload.title: [Bug]: Short stream chunks silently zero-fill remote file reads

payload.author: tmchow
payload.body:
## Summary
Clone abort can recursively delete an unowned destination path

**Category:** data-loss  ·  **Severity:** high  ·  **Confidence:** high  ·  **Affects:** macOS, Linux, Windows

## Impact
Aborting a clone can recursively delete a pre-existing, user-owned destination directory that the clone never created.

## Location
`src/main/ipc/repos.ts:624-635` (line numbers as of `main` at filing)

## Reproduction
In a unit test, make gitSpawn return an EventEmitter that does not emit close. Register repo handlers, call handlers.get('repos:clone') without awaiting it using { url: 'file:///tmp/source/.', destination: '/Users/alice/projects' }, then call handlers.get('repos:cloneAbort'). activeClonePath is set to join('/Users/alice/projects', '.') and cloneAbort calls rm('/Users/alice/projects', { recursive: true, force: true }).

## Suggested fix
Validate the derived clone directory name and reject '.', '..', empty names, and any path segment that normalizes outside args.destination. Before spawning git, record whether clonePath already exists and only cleanup a path that this clone created. Prefer creating a unique temporary clone directory and renaming after success, or use an ownership marker so abort cleanup cannot target user-owned paths.

**Minimum fix scope:** src/main/ipc/repos.ts clone name validation plus clone cleanup ownership tracking; add focused tests in src/main/ipc/repos-remote.test.ts or a repos-clone-abort test file.

## Why existing tests miss it
The included repos clone tests cover successful clone creation and folder-to-git dedupe, but there is no cloneAbort test and no coverage for dot-segment URLs or cleanup ownership.

## Suggested regression test
Add a repos:cloneAbort test with a pending mocked gitSpawn and url 'file:///tmp/source/.'; assert rm is not called on the destination parent and the handler rejects the URL before setting activeClonePath. Add a second test where clonePath already exists before spawn and abort does not remove it.
payload.title: [Bug]: Clone abort can recursively delete an unowned destination path

payload.author: tmchow
payload.body:
## Summary
Discard can delete files outside the worktree through symlink parents

**Category:** data-loss  ·  **Severity:** high  ·  **Confidence:** high  ·  **Affects:** macOS, Linux, Windows

## Impact
Discarding a path under a symlinked parent deletes files OUTSIDE the worktree via the rm fallback — data loss beyond the repository.

## Location
`src/main/git/status.ts:1087-1108` (line numbers as of `main` at filing)

## Reproduction
In a repo at /repo, create /tmp/orca-outside/keep.txt and ln -s /tmp/orca-outside /repo/link. Call discardChanges('/repo', 'link/keep.txt') in a case where git ls-files --error-unmatch -- link/keep.txt fails. The function accepts /repo/link/keep.txt as inside the worktree, then rm removes /tmp/orca-outside/keep.txt. bulkDiscardChanges('/repo', ['link/keep.txt']) has the same behavior.

## Suggested fix
Before any fs.rm fallback, resolve the real parent/target safely and prove it remains inside the real worktree root, or refuse discard for paths that traverse symlinked directories. For missing leaf paths, realpath the nearest existing parent and validate that parent is inside the real worktree before removal.

**Minimum fix scope:** Update discardChanges and bulkDiscardChanges path validation for the untracked rm fallback, plus add regression coverage for symlink-parent paths.

## Why existing tests miss it
The existing discard tests cover normal tracked/untracked paths and lexical ../ traversal, but they do not create an in-worktree symlink to an outside directory and then discard a child path through it.

## Suggested regression test
Add an integration-style discard test with a real temporary repo, an in-repo symlink to an outside temp directory, and an outside file. Verify discardChanges and bulkDiscardChanges reject the symlink-child path and the outside file still exists.
payload.title: [Bug]: Discard can delete files outside the worktree through symlink parents

## Summary
Worktree removal force-deletes unpublished branch commits

**Category:** data-loss  ·  **Severity:** high  ·  **Confidence:** high  ·  **Affects:** macOS, Linux, Windows

## Impact
Removing a worktree force-deletes its branch with `git branch -D`, permanently destroying commits that were never pushed or merged.

## Location
`src/main/git/worktree.ts:457-469` (line numbers as of `main` at filing)

## Reproduction
Create a repo, add a linked worktree on branch `feature/test`, make and commit a change in that worktree without pushing or merging it, then call `removeWorktree(repoPath, worktreePath, false)`. The worktree is clean so preflight passes, `git worktree remove` succeeds, and `git branch -D feature/test` deletes the local ref for the unpublished commit.

## Suggested fix
Before deleting the branch, verify its tip is safely reachable from an upstream/base ref or require an explicit discard-branch choice. At minimum, use a non-force deletion path (`git branch -d`) or a reachability check and preserve the branch when Git reports unmerged/unpublished commits.

**Minimum fix scope:** Change `removeWorktree` branch cleanup to a safe deletion helper that checks publish/merge reachability before deleting; mirror the same behavior in the SSH relay worktree removal path because the local code comments require parity.

## Why existing tests miss it
The existing removal tests mock the happy path and assert `git branch -D` is called. They do not model a branch that is ahead of its upstream, unmerged into the base, or otherwise contains commits that would become unreachable.

## Suggested regression test
Add a real-git or mocked removeWorktree test where the removed worktree's branch has a commit not reachable from its upstream/base. Assert the worktree can be removed but the branch is preserved, or that removal reports a discard-required error before branch deletion.
payload.title: [Bug]: Worktree removal force-deletes unpublished branch commits

## Summary
fs.rename silently overwrites an existing destination

**Category:** data-loss  ·  **Severity:** high  ·  **Confidence:** high  ·  **Affects:** macOS, Linux, Windows

## Impact
Renaming onto an existing path destroys the destination's contents with no warning, including over the SSH relay file handler.

## Location
`src/relay/fs-handler.ts:205-208` (line numbers as of `main` at filing)

## Reproduction
On macOS or Linux, create old.txt with 'new' and existing.txt with 'keep', then call fs.rename with oldPath=old.txt and newPath=existing.txt. The request succeeds and existing.txt now contains 'new'; the original 'keep' content is lost.

## Suggested fix
Make FsHandler.rename no-clobber by default: check the destination and return an EEXIST-style error before renaming, and keep the destination content untouched. If overwrite is truly needed, require an explicit overwrite flag from a confirmed caller.

**Minimum fix scope:** Change FsHandler.rename and add relay fs-handler coverage for existing-file and existing-directory destinations.

## Why existing tests miss it
The current rename test only verifies the happy path where the destination does not exist; there is no test for an existing destination or content preservation.

## Suggested regression test
Add an fs-handler test that creates both source and destination files, calls fs.rename to the existing destination, expects an EEXIST-style rejection, and verifies the destination content remains unchanged.
payload.title: [Bug]: fs.rename silently overwrites an existing destination

## Summary
Missing write content is coerced to an empty string and written

**Category:** data-loss  ·  **Severity:** high  ·  **Confidence:** high  ·  **Affects:** macOS, Linux, Windows

## Impact
A write request with missing or non-string content silently truncates the target file to empty instead of erroring — silent data loss.

## Location
`src/main/runtime/rpc/methods/files.ts:33-38` (line numbers as of `main` at filing)

## Reproduction
Dispatch files.write with { worktree: 'id:wt-1', relativePath: 'src/index.ts' } or content: null. The schema parses content as '', then the handler calls runtime.writeFileExplorerFile(..., '').

## Suggested fix
Change write payload schemas to require the field to be present and string-typed without defaulting invalid values to ''. Use a custom/string schema that accepts '' only when the caller explicitly supplied a string. Apply the same rule to contentBase64 for files.writeBase64 and files.writeBase64Chunk, and consider base64 validation where appropriate.

**Minimum fix scope:** src/main/runtime/rpc/methods/files.ts write-content schemas plus focused RPC validation tests.

## Why existing tests miss it
The included tests are computer CLI/spec tests and do not exercise file RPC write validation. The provided package test command would not catch this unless a negative files.write/files.writeBase64 validation case exists.

## Suggested regression test
Add RPC dispatcher tests asserting files.write, files.writeBase64, and files.writeBase64Chunk reject omitted/null content fields and do not call the runtime, while explicit content: '' still succeeds for the text write path if empty files are supported.

## Summary
`orchestration.reset` wipes all orchestration state when no reset scope is provided

**Category:** data-loss  ·  **Severity:** high  ·  **Confidence:** high  ·  **Affects:** macOS, Linux, Windows

## Impact
A caller passing empty or ambiguous params silently wipes ALL tasks and messages — total loss of orchestration state with no confirmation.

## Location
`src/main/runtime/rpc/methods/orchestration.ts:139-143` (line numbers as of `main` at filing)

## Reproduction
Create a task and message, then call the RPC method directly with `{}`: `orchestration.reset {}`. The handler reaches the final `db.resetAll()` branch and returns `{ reset: 'all' }`, clearing all orchestration state despite no explicit reset scope.

## Suggested fix
Require exactly one reset scope. Reject `{}` with an invalid-argument error, and reject multiple scopes instead of applying the first truthy branch. If a no-flag CLI shortcut is desired, make the CLI pass `all: true` explicitly after its own confirmation/intent handling.

**Minimum fix scope:** Change `ResetParams`/handler validation in `src/main/runtime/rpc/methods/orchestration.ts` and update the orchestration reset RPC tests.

## Why existing tests miss it
The visible reset tests cover `{ all: true }`, `{ tasks: true }`, and `{ messages: true }`, but not the empty-params path or contradictory multi-scope input.

## Suggested regression test
Add an `orchestration.reset` RPC test that seeds a task/message, calls the method with `{}`, expects an invalid-argument error, and verifies the task/message remain. Add another test for `{ tasks: true, messages: true }` rejecting without mutation.

payload.author: michael-hewitt
payload.body:
## Description

Keyboard shortcuts are bound to physical key positions (QWERTY layout) rather than the logical characters they produce. On a Dvorak keyboard layout, this means every shortcut fires from the wrong key.

For example:
- **Cmd+W** (Close Active Tab) fires when pressing the physical W key, which produces `,` on Dvorak
- **Cmd+,** (Open Settings) fires when pressing the physical `,` key, which produces `w` on Dvorak

The result is that Cmd+W opens Settings and Cmd+, closes the tab — exactly backwards from what's expected.

## Attempted workaround

Swapping the bindings in `~/.orca/keybindings.json` does not help because the override values are also interpreted by physical position. No matter which way the bindings are configured, they remain swapped on Dvorak.

## Expected behavior

Shortcuts should map to the logical character produced by the key, not the physical key position. This is the standard behavior in macOS applications — `Cmd+W` should mean "Cmd + the key that types W in the active layout."

## Environment

- **Orca version:** 1.4.27
- **OS:** macOS (Darwin 25.3.0)
- **Keyboard layout:** Dvorak

## Notes

This likely affects all non-QWERTY layouts (Colemak, AZERTY, etc.), not just Dvorak. Related: #1205 (Polish diacritics issue — different symptom but also a non-standard keyboard handling problem).
payload.title: Keyboard shortcuts map to physical key positions instead of logical characters on Dvorak layout

payload.author: erikd234
payload.body:
## Summary

Let each Orca workspace run on its own dedicated cloud machine, with a **warm pool** of pre-booted instances so new workspaces are instant. Make the backend pluggable so users can bring their own infra (Daytona, Fly Machines, Firecracker, EC2, GCP, etc.).

## Motivation

Today every workspace shares the local laptop's CPU/memory/disk. As soon as you have multiple parallel agents working in parallel worktrees — exactly Orca's pitch — they all fight over the same host:

- builds (Go, native iOS, Expo) contend for CPU
- node_modules / DerivedData / Xcode caches contend for disk
- multi-agent loops contend for tokens *and* RAM (each agent + its sub-agents)
- everything slows the IDE itself

The obvious answer is "throw it on a big cloud machine," but **a single beefy multi-tenant cloud machine isn't always great either**: noisy-neighbor problems between workspaces, blast radius when one agent runs `rm -rf` or fills the disk, hard to snapshot/clone, hard to give different workspaces different specs (GPU vs CPU vs ARM). Per-workspace cloud instances solve all of that — at the cost of cold-start latency, which is exactly what warm pooling fixes.

## What I'm asking for

1. **Per-workspace machine model**: each Orca workspace can be backed by its own cloud machine instead of (or in addition to) running on the host.
2. **Warm pool**: configurable N pre-booted machines kept hot so `worktree create` returns in under a second instead of waiting on boot + clone + dep install.
3. **Pluggable backend**: the machine provider is an interface, not hardcoded. First-class targets I'd love to see — Daytona, Fly Machines (Firecracker), AWS EC2 / Fargate, GCP, generic SSH+systemd.
4. **Self-hostable**: I'm happy to bring my own infra and pay my own cloud bill. The Orca app would just need the backend protocol documented (gRPC / HTTP / SSH — whatever) so I can point it at my own warm-pool controller.

## Why I'm offering to self-host

- Don't want to wait on Stably to ship a managed offering before getting the workflow.
- Already have cloud spend committed; would prefer a BYO-infra path even when a managed version exists.
- Believe enough Orca users are infra-comfortable that supporting BYO would unlock a lot of value cheaply for you (you ship the protocol + a reference provider; the community ships adapters).

## Rough shape of the integration I'd build

```
orca worktree create --backend daytona --pool dev-warm
  → controller hands back a hot machine (already has repo cloned, deps installed, agent CLIs warm)
  → Orca SSH'es / WebSocket-tunnels into it
  → terminals, file edits, browser automation all route to the remote machine
  → on workspace close: snapshot or recycle back into the pool
```

The pieces I think you need to expose:

- Backend protocol (so I can implement the Daytona/Firecracker provider).
- Hooks for workspace lifecycle (`on_acquire`, `on_release`, `on_snapshot`).
- Network plumbing for terminals + file sync + browser automation that already works locally.

## Happy to help

I can prototype a Daytona-backed provider against any protocol you publish, and feed back design issues from doing it for real. Reply here or DM and I'll get started.
payload.title: Feature request: per-workspace cloud machines with warm pooling (self-hostable)

payload.author: dragonfire1119
payload.body:
## Bug Report

Hostname resolution fails in newly-spawned Orca terminals because the long-lived Orca daemon loses access to the macOS system resolver (mDNSResponder) over its lifetime. PTYs it spawns afterward cannot resolve hostnames.

**Behavior:**
- `ping google.com` → `cannot resolve google.com: Unknown host` in a newly-spawned Orca terminal
- `ping 1.1.1.1` works (network is fine, only name resolution breaks)
- `dig` / `nslookup` still work (they hit a nameserver directly over UDP, bypassing the system resolver)
- Affects any tool using the system resolver: ping, curl/git over https hostnames, package managers
- Terminals that were spawned earlier in the session keep working; only newly-spawned ones break
- Quitting and relaunching Orca does NOT fix it

**Diagnosis:**
In a broken (newly-spawned) terminal:
- `scutil --dns` → `No DNS configuration available`
- `dscacheutil -q host -a name google.com` → no output
- `dig google.com` → resolves fine

The PTY parent for both working and broken shells is the same daemon process:

```
/Applications/Orca.app/Contents/Frameworks/Orca Helper.app/Contents/MacOS/Orca Helper \
  .../out/main/daemon-entry.js --socket .../orca/daemon/daemon-v7.sock --token .../daemon-v7.token
```

That daemon runs with **PPID 1 (detached from the GUI login session)** and outlives the app. Shells it spawns early still resolve DNS; shells spawned later (identical env / PATH / PPID / `/bin/zsh -l`) cannot. The daemon appears to lose its mDNSResponder / SCDynamicStore connection over its lifetime, and every PTY spawned after that inherits the broken state.

`buildPtyEnv` env construction is not the cause — no DNS/resolver env vars are touched.

**Workaround that fixes it:** kill the daemon and relaunch Orca so a fresh daemon spawns:

```
kill $(pgrep -f 'daemon-entry.js --socket')
```

After that, newly-spawned terminals resolve DNS correctly.

**Environment:**
- macOS 26.5 (25F71), Apple Silicon
- Orca 1.4.28-rc.4 (also reproduced on 1.4.28-rc.0)
- App not quarantined; no sandbox entitlements on the binary
payload.title: PTY terminals spawn outside gui/$UID launchd domain — system DNS resolution fails

payload.author: Jeet-Chugh
payload.body:
## Feature Request

Extend Orca automations so that a scheduled run can be **gated by a deterministic shell command**. Today every cron firing unconditionally runs the agent with the configured prompt. For many automations, the agent only needs to run *occasionally* — when some external condition is true. Without a gate, the only options are (a) waste agent runs on no-op invocations or (b) push the conditional logic into the agent prompt itself, which is slow, expensive, and non-deterministic.

A simple `--precheck` shell command, gated by exit code, would let users front a deterministic preflight check before the agent fires.

## Current Behavior

`orca automations create` supports a scheduled trigger (preset / cron / RRULE) plus a fixed `--prompt` handed to a `--provider`. When the cron fires, the agent **always** runs:

```
orca automations create \
  --name "Daily PR review" \
  --trigger daily --time 09:00 \
  --provider claude \
  --prompt "Review any open PRs assigned to me and leave inline comments"
```

There is no way to say *\"only run this if there is actually a PR to review.\"* The agent spins up, looks around, finds nothing, and exits. That's wasted tokens, wasted time, and noisy run history.

I searched closed + open issues (`exit code`, `conditional`, `gate`, `guard`, `predicate`, `precheck`, `automation script/bash/command`) and didn't find an overlapping proposal. #1807 covered the broader Automations tab spec but did not address conditional execution.

## Proposed Behavior

Add an optional **`--precheck`** flag to `orca automations create` (and the corresponding UI field once #1807's tab lands). When set, Orca runs the precheck shell command first; the agent only runs if the command exits **0**. Any non-zero exit code skips the run.

### CLI

```
orca automations create \
  --name \"Daily PR review\" \
  --trigger daily --time 09:00 \
  --provider claude \
  --precheck \"gh pr list --search 'review-requested:@me' --state open --json number -q '.[0].number'\" \
  --prompt \"Review any open PRs assigned to me and leave inline comments\"
```

Semantics:

| Precheck exit code | Behavior | Logged as |
|---|---|---|
| `0` | Run the agent with the configured prompt | `ran` |
| non-zero | Skip the agent run entirely | `skipped: precheck exit <N>` |

The precheck command runs in the same worktree/working directory the agent would have run in (or a sensible default for workspace-mode automations), inherits a shell-like environment, and is killed if it exceeds a reasonable timeout (suggest 60s default, configurable via `--precheck-timeout`).

### YAML / config parity

Whatever config file backs CLI-created automations (and `orca.yaml` for repo-committed ones) gains a sibling field:

```yaml
automations:
  - name: Daily PR review
    trigger: daily
    time: \"09:00\"
    provider: claude
    precheck: |
      gh pr list --search 'review-requested:@me' --state open --json number -q '.[0].number'
    prompt: |
      Review any open PRs assigned to me and leave inline comments
```

### Run history

A skipped run should still show up in `orca automations runs` so the user can see *the schedule fired but the precheck said no*. Suggested columns: timestamp, outcome (`ran` / `skipped` / `precheck-error`), precheck exit code, precheck stdout/stderr tail (truncated). This is essential for debugging \"why didn't my automation fire?\" — without it, skips are invisible.

### Distinguishing skip vs. broken precheck (optional follow-up)

The minimal contract is **exit 0 = run, anything else = skip**. If a precheck command itself is broken (e.g. typo, missing binary, command not found → exit 127), it will silently skip forever, which is its own footgun. Two ways to address, both can be deferred:

- Surface precheck stderr prominently in the runs view so a broken precheck is debuggable.
- Optionally, treat exit 127 (or a configurable \"error code set\") as `precheck-error` distinct from `skipped` so it can alert.

I'd ship the simple
