payload.body:
## Summary
When opening a newly created worktree, the File Explorer can render an incomplete directory list (missing files/folders) until a manual refresh or later reload.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Create/open a new worktree.
2. Immediately switch to the Explorer panel.
3. Observe the tree while background directory reads are still settling.

## Actual behavior
Explorer sometimes shows a partial tree for the worktree root or expanded folders.

## Expected behavior
Explorer should consistently reflect the latest directory state and not be overwritten by stale async responses.

## Suspected root cause
`useFileExplorerTree` allows overlapping `loadDir()` requests to race. Older async responses can complete after newer ones and overwrite `dirCache` with stale children.

## Proposed fix
Gate directory-load completion writes with session/revision guards so only the latest in-flight request for a directory (within the current tree reset session) can mutate cache/error state.
payload.title: Explorer can show incomplete file tree right after opening a new worktree

payload.author: BradleyGoulding
payload.body:
### Operating system

macOS

### Orca version

previous release before 1.4.5 - 1.4.2/3?

### Details

## Summary

When the Orca client stays disconnected from the remote for longer than the relay daemon's `--grace-time 300` (i.e. >5 minutes), the daemon exits cleanly on its own, killing every pseudoterminal it was managing and all the processes inside those ptys. When Orca later reconnects (whether automatically or by user clicking reconnect), tabs are restored as UI elements showing green/connected, but the pty session inside each tab is brand new — prior shells have exited, scrollback is gone, any running tool (e.g. an interactive process like `claude`, `vim`, a build) is dead.

This isn't an error — the daemon's exit is documented behaviour of `--grace-time`. The bug is that the daemon's grace-time is shorter than common disconnect durations (Mac sleep, lid close, network drop while moving between locations, etc.), and there's no recovery path that survives.

## Why this matters

The disconnect trigger is *user-routine*: closing the laptop lid, sleeping the Mac, walking from one office to another, switching WiFi. Any of these can cross the 5-minute threshold trivially. The cost is "all the in-progress work in every Orca terminal" each time — measured in minutes-to-hours of re-doing things.

## What's actually broken

The disconnect itself isn't the bug — disconnects are fine, they happen. The bug is that the relay's failure mode for "client disconnected for a while" is **exit cleanly and SIGHUP everything**, with no mechanism by which a returning client can re-attach to existing ptys.

A tmux-style daemon that kept ptys alive across client absences, or a longer/configurable grace-time, or detaching pty children from the daemon process group, would all solve this. Any of those would convert the user pain from "lose all work" to "click reconnect."

## Environment

- Orca remote-helper version: `0.1.0+8ed91fb74fa0` (post-update, current)
- Remote: Ubuntu Noble (24.04), aarch64
- Client: macOS, Orca app version current as of 2026-05-18
- Disconnect mechanism in reproduction: Mac sleep via lid close on battery + drive between locations (~28 minutes elapsed)

## Reproduction steps

Concrete repro path — anyone with Orca + a remote can run this:

```
1. In Orca, connect to a remote you control.
2. Open a new terminal tab.
3. Start something with visible state — easiest is to print
   distinctive output:
      echo "==== before disconnect ===="
      date
      sleep 36000     # any long-running thing
   Or start `claude` / `vim` / a build / anything with internal state.
4. SSH to the remote in a SECOND, SEPARATE terminal (NOT through Orca):
      ssh user@remote
   Note the running processes:
      pgrep -af relay.js
   You'll see one `relay.js --detached --grace-time 300 ...` daemon
   and one `relay.js --connect ...` client. Save those pids.
5. Disconnect Orca for >5 minutes. Multiple ways:
      a. Sleep the Mac for >5min:
            sudo pmset schedule wake "$(date -v+7M "+%m/%d/%y %H:%M:%S")"
            sudo pmset sleepnow
      b. Kill the network on the Mac side for >5min.
      c. Force-quit Orca and wait >5min before reopening.
   Any one suffices.
6. From the SECOND ssh session (outside Orca), confirm what happened
   to the daemon:
      pgrep -af relay.js
   You should see NOTHING after about 5 min of Orca being away.
      cat ~/.orca-remote/relay-*/relay.log
   The last line will be:
      [relay] Process exiting with code 0
7. Reconnect Orca (auto or manual click — same outcome).
8. Look at the tab from step 3.
```

## Expected behaviour

- Tab is restored *with its prior pty session*. The output from step 3 is still in the scrollback. The `sleep 36000` (or `claude`, or `vim`, or your build) is still running. You can interact with it.

## Actual behaviour

- Tab is restored as a *new* pty.
- Prior process is gone (the shell that hosted it received SIGHUP when the daemon exited and the controlling terminal went awa
payload.title: [Bug]: ssh terminal state lost after >5min Orca disconnect

payload.body:
### Details

## Security Concern: Preventing Malicious Pull Requests

Hi team 👋

First of all, great work on Orca — it's an impressive project.

I wanted to raise a **security question** that I think is important for a tool like this, which runs with elevated privileges on users' machines and integrates deeply with AI agents and code execution.

### The concern

Orcas's open-source nature means that **anyone can submit a Pull Request**. This opens the door to potential **supply-chain attacks** or **malicious contributions**, where a bad actor could:

- Inject malicious code into core execution paths
- Introduce backdoors in agent integrations or terminal/shell runners
- Smuggle data-exfiltration logic into networking or API-related modules
- Gradually escalate privileges through seemingly innocent incremental PRs

These kinds of attacks are well-documented (e.g., the [xz utils backdoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XZ_Utils_backdoor), event-stream npm incident, etc.) and are particularly dangerous for tools that:
- Execute code locally
- Have access to the filesystem
- Communicate with external APIs or AI backends

### My questions

1. **What is your current PR review process?** Do you have a checklist or policy for reviewing contributions from unknown/new contributors?
2. **Do you use any automated security scanning** on PRs (e.g., CodeQL, Dependabot, Semgrep, Socket.dev for supply-chain risks)?
3. **Do you enforce signed commits** or any form of contributor identity verification?
4. **Is there a SECURITY.md** or responsible disclosure policy in place?
5. **Do you have branch protection rules** that require reviews from specific trusted maintainers before merging?

### Suggestion

I'd strongly recommend:
- Publishing a `SECURITY.md` with a clear vulnerability disclosure process
- Enabling **GitHub's dependency review** and **secret scanning**
- Requiring **at least 2 maintainer approvals** for PRs touching sensitive areas (agent execution, networking, auth)
- Running **SAST tools** (CodeQL / Semgrep) automatically on every PR via GitHub Actions
- Considering a **CODEOWNERS** file to assign mandatory reviewers per module

Given that Orca is an AI-powered tool that executes code and interacts with the filesystem, the attack surface is significant. I'd love to understand your current security posture and how the community can help keep this project safe.

Thanks for your time and for maintaining this project!
payload.title: [Security Question]: How do you prevent malicious or supply-chain attack PRs from being merged?

## Summary
Make Linux packaging explicitly use the Orca app logo in build config so AppImage and `.deb` icon behavior is deterministic.

## Current state
Linux artifacts currently include `orca-ide` icons in package output, but the icon source is implicit via electron-builder defaults.

## Problem

Set the Linux icon path explicitly in `config/electron-builder.config.cjs`:

- `pnpm build:linux` succeeds.

### Operating system

macOS

### Orca version

1.4.4

### Details

**Short summary:**
Image paste into a terminal pane writes a host-local temp file path (e.g. `/var/folders/17/.../T/orca-paste-1779070188893.png`) into the terminal. In a **Remote Project** (SSH), the agent runs on the remote host and can't read that path — the file is on the local Mac — so tools like Claude Code or Hermes that accept pasted images fail with "file does not exist."

This is a follow-up to #490, which added clipboard-image paste by saving the image to a temp file on the local machine and pasting its path. The local-project case works; the Remote Project case doesn't.

**What happened?**

Pasting an image into a terminal in a Remote Project inserts a local Mac path. The agent on the remote tries to read it and reports the file doesn't exist.

**How can we reproduce it?**

1. Open a Remote Project in Orca (SSH'd into a remote host)
2. Run an agent in the terminal that accepts pasted images (e.g. Claude Code)
3. Copy an image to the clipboard on the local Mac
4. Cmd+V into the terminal
5. The pasted path is something like `/var/folders/17/.../T/orca-paste-*.png` — a local Mac path the remote agent can't see

**Anything else that might help:**

*Why it happens:* the fix from #490 writes the image to a temp file on the host (local) filesystem and pastes the local path. For a local project this works because the agent process shares the filesystem. For a Remote Project, the agent process lives on the remote and has no access to `/var/folders/...` on the Mac.

*Possible directions:*

- **Push the file across to the remote** when the pane belongs to a Remote Project — write to `/tmp` (or equivalent) on the remote via the existing SSH channel and paste that remote path
- **OSC / iTerm2-style inline image protocol** — encode the image inline as an escape sequence; works only for agents that understand it (doesn't help agents that strictly want a file path)
- **base64 + here-doc on paste** — paste something like `cat > /tmp/orca-paste-X.png <<EOF ... EOF` followed by the path; crude but no out-of-band channel needed
- **At minimum**, detect Remote Project and surface a notification that image paste isn't supported yet, rather than silently pasting a dead path

*Related:*

- #490 — original feature that added image paste via local temp-file path
- #326 — SSH access to remote projects
- #1921 — Start work from SSH
payload.title: [Bug]: Image paste broken in Remote Projects — temp file is on local Mac, agent runs on remote

payload.author: leynier
payload.body:
### Problem or use case

The Source Control panel currently uses a fixed group order: `Changes`, `Staged Changes`, then `Untracked Files`.

That order is useful because unresolved conflicts are assigned to the `Changes` area, so they stay near the top. However, the panel is also commit-oriented: the commit controls sit directly above the file list, and staged files are the files that will actually be committed.

Different users may reasonably prefer different workflows:

- Commit review workflow: `Staged Changes`, `Changes`, `Untracked Files`
- Conflict/change-first workflow: `Changes`, `Staged Changes`, `Untracked Files`
- Cleanup workflow: maybe `Untracked Files` earlier

A fixed order makes one workflow feel optimized and the others secondary.

### Proposed solution

Add a setting to configure the Source Control group order.

The default can remain the current order to preserve existing behavior:

1. `Changes`
2. `Staged Changes`
3. `Untracked Files`

Users who prefer a commit-oriented panel could change it to:

1. `Staged Changes`
2. `Changes`
3. `Untracked Files`

Important constraint: unresolved conflicts should remain highly visible regardless of the configured order. A good implementation could keep conflict entries pinned above the normal groups, or otherwise ensure conflict visibility is not degraded when `Staged Changes` is configured first.

### Alternatives or additional context

A simpler alternative would be to change the default order to `Staged Changes`, `Changes`, `Untracked Files`, but that may not fit every workflow and could reduce conflict visibility.

Related Source Control work:
- #1658 added the Source Control tree view.
- #1670 added the Stage Files primary button.
- #1407 improved Source Control section actions.
payload.title: [Feature]: Make Source Control group order configurable

payload.body:
## Versions

- **Mobile (iOS):** v0.0.7 (latest on App Store)
- **Desktop (macOS):** v1.4.1
- **Remote relay:** `0.1.0+04be5c83b2f5`

## Setup

- MacBook running Orca desktop v1.4.1
- iPhone (iOS) paired to the MacBook desktop, reachable to the Mac via private network
- An SSH-remote Linux dev VM connected from the desktop, with multiple `git` worktrees under `~/workspace/<repo>/.worktrees/...`
- Pairing on the phone reports the desktop as reachable; relay handshake to the SSH host repeatedly logs `Handshake OK`. Transport is healthy.

## Symptom 1 — Mobile does not show SSH-remote host worktrees

The mobile app shows a host labeled **"Host 1"** with a worktree list. The worktrees listed under "Host 1" are the ones on the **local Mac**. The **SSH-remote VM and its worktrees are not visible at all from mobile** — there is no second host entry, no remote-host picker, and no way to navigate to worktrees that exist on the SSH host the desktop is connected to.

The docs at https://www.onorca.dev/docs/mobile state the mobile app lets you "Monitor every worktree, its agent, and its current status." In practice that appears to mean "every local worktree" — remote-host worktrees defined by the paired desktop are excluded.

See attached `IMG_0698.png` (mobile) and `Screenshot 2026-05-17 at 12.26.26 PM.png` (desktop, for the same session).

### Expected

When the paired desktop has one or more SSH-remote hosts connected, the mobile app should:

1. Surface each remote host as its own entry (named after the configured SSH host, not `Host 1`).
2. List the worktrees defined under each remote host alongside local worktrees.
3. Allow the same monitor/reply actions the docs already describe for local worktrees.

## Symptom 2 — Create Workspace on mobile fails with `spawn git ENOENT`

In the mobile "Create Workspace" flow (repo selected, name filled, agent Claude), submitting surfaces a red error: **`spawn git ENOENT`**. See attached `IMG_0698.png`.

On the SSH-remote VM, `git` is installed at `/usr/bin/git` and `/usr/bin` is on `PATH` in a normal interactive shell — `which git` resolves cleanly. So the relay process is evidently spawning `git` without inheriting a `PATH` that includes `/usr/bin`, and the spawn ENOENTs.

### Likely fix

Either resolve `git` to an absolute path before `spawn` in the relay, or ensure the spawned child inherits a sane `PATH` (include `/usr/bin` + `/usr/local/bin` at minimum). This is the standard Node `child_process.spawn` PATH-inheritance pitfall when the relay starts from a non-login context.

## Repro

1. Pair iOS mobile v0.0.7 with macOS desktop v1.4.1.
2. From desktop, connect to an SSH-remote host that has a repo cloned with multiple worktrees under `.worktrees/`.
3. On mobile, open the host list:
   - **Observed:** only local Mac worktrees appear under "Host 1". The SSH host and its worktrees are absent.
4. Tap **Create Workspace**, pick the repo, fill a name, tap Create.
   - **Observed:** `spawn git ENOENT` error.

## Screenshots

- `IMG_0698.png` — Mobile, "Host 1" view + Create Workspace dialog with `spawn git ENOENT`
- `Screenshot 2026-05-17 at 12.26.26 PM.png` — Desktop session for the same setup

## Notes

- Mobile is the current App Store build (`v0.0.7`).
- Desktop just updated to `v1.4.1`.
- Restarting the desktop, force-reconnecting the SSH host, and refreshing the mobile app did not surface remote-host worktrees.
- `mobile-v0.0.7` and recent mobile changelogs don't mention SSH-remote worktree surfacing — this feature may simply not be wired up on the mobile yet despite the docs implying it.
payload.title: [Bug][Mobile]: SSH-remote host worktrees not visible; 'spawn git ENOENT' on Create Workspace

payload.author: Sharpek
payload.body: ### Problem or use case Orca already has a runners concept (e.g. the per-project runner dropdown in the top bar), but it appears limited to a fixed set of predefined runner types. In day-to-day work on a single project I routinely need to launch several different commands that aren't a clean fit for any built-in type — for example: - `npm run android` / `npm run ios` (Expo / React Native) - `npm run dev` for a web frontend - `uv run pytest tests/` or `pytest -k some_test` for backend tests - `docker compose up` for local infra - arbitrary project scripts like `./scripts/seed-db.sh` or `make lint` Right now each of these means dropping into a terminal, recalling the command, and rerunning it manually. IntelliJ-based IDEs solve this with Run/Debug Configurations: you define a named runner once (command + args + working dir + env vars), pin it to the top bar, and launch it with a click or shortcut. The dropdown becomes the single source of truth for "how do I run this project." I'd love the same in Orca. ### Proposed solution Add a generic "Shell command" runner type that integrates with the existing runner dropdown. Per-runner fields: - Name (shows in the dropdown) - Command (the shell command to execute, e.g. `npm run android`) - Working directory (default: project root) - Environment variables (key/value list, with support for `${...}` interpolation from project/user-level vars) - Optional: shell to use (sh / bash / zsh / project default) - Optional: "Before launch" steps — chain another runner first (e.g. build before run), mirroring IntelliJ's behavior - Optional: input/output handling — show output in a dedicated tool window/tab, with the ability to stop/restart the process Storage & sharing: - Store runner definitions in the project (e.g. `.orca/runners.json` or similar) so they can be committed and shared across the team — same pattern as IntelliJ's `.idea/runConfigurations/`. - Allow user-level runners too, for things that aren't project-specific. UX: - Existing runner dropdown lists all configured runners (built-in + user-defined shell runners) together. - Keyboard shortcut to run the currently selected runner, and a "Run…" picker (fuzzy search across all runners) similar to IntelliJ's Run Anything. - Re-running a runner reuses the same output tab rather than spawning a new one (configurable). This effectively turns Orca's runner bar into a project-aware command palette for execution — which is one of the things IntelliJ users miss the most when switching editors. ### Alternatives or additional context _No response_

### Operating system

Windows

### Orca version

v1.4.3

### Details

**Short summary:**
On Windows, Orca fails to detect Claude Code when `claude.exe` is installed by the official Anthropic native installer at `C:\Users\<name>\.local\bin\claude.exe`, even though `where.exe claude` resolves it correctly from a terminal.

**What happened?**
- Installed Claude Code via the official Windows native installer (v2.1.143), which places `claude.exe` in `~/.local/bin`.
- `~/.local/bin` is on my user-level PATH; `where.exe claude` from PowerShell returns `C:\Users\033\.local\bin\claude.exe`.
- Orca, launched from the Start Menu, does not detect Claude Code.
- After fully quitting Orca and re-launching it via `Start-Process` from a PowerShell session (which has the full merged PATH), detection works.

**How can we reproduce it?**
1. Install Claude Code on Windows using the official native installer (it installs to `C:\Users\<name>\.local\bin\claude.exe`).
2. Make sure `~/.local/bin` is on the *user-level* PATH but NOT on the *system-level* PATH (this is the installer's default — it only edits user PATH).
3. Launch Orca from the Start Menu (not from a terminal).
4. Orca reports Claude Code as not installed / not detected.

**Root cause (from code reading):**
In `src/main/codex-cli/command.ts`, the function `getVersionManagerDirectories` Windows branch (around lines 100–103) only probes:
- `AppData\Roaming\npm`
- `AppData\Local\pnpm`
- `AppData\Local\Yarn\bin`

The macOS/Linux branch probes `~/.local/bin`, but the Windows branch does not — even though Anthropic's official Windows native installer for Claude Code uses exactly this location. So when the PATH lookup misses (e.g., GUI launch with a stripped PATH), the fallback also misses.

**Suggested fix:**
Add `join(homePath, '.local', 'bin')` to the Windows branch in `getVersionManagerDirectories`. This is the documented Windows location for Anthropic's native Claude Code installer.

**Anything else that might help:**
- Orca version: 1.4.3
- Claude Code version: 2.1.143 (official native installer)
- Node: v22.21.1
- OS: Windows 11 Pro for Workstations
- Workaround until fixed: add `C:\Users\<name>\.local\bin` to **system-level** PATH, or fully quit and relaunch Orca after any user-PATH change.

Happy to send a PR for this if you'd like.
payload.title: [Bug]: Windows: claude.exe in ~/.local/bin not detected by Orca when launched from Start Menu

payload.body:
### Operating system

macOS

### Orca version

1.4.2

### Details

Short summary:
When creating a new worktree/session from an existing branch whose name contains slashes, Orca preserves the selected branch as the base ref, but also copies that ref into the workspace name. The workspace name is then sanitized for the new worktree branch, so a selected branch like `feature/something` becomes a new branch like `feature-something`.

What happened?
- In the new workspace composer, selecting an existing branch calls `handleSmartBranchSelect(refName)`.
- That stores `refName` as `baseBranch`, which is correct.
- If the workspace name is empty or auto-generated, the same handler also does `setName(refName)`.
- Worktree creation derives the new branch from `name`, and `sanitizeWorktreeName()` replaces `/` with `-` because `/` is outside its allowed character set.
- Result: starting from `feature/something` creates the worktree from that base ref, but the new local branch becomes `feature-something` instead of preserving the branch hierarchy/name shape users expect.

How can we reproduce it?
1. Open the new workspace/session composer.
2. Select an existing branch whose name contains slashes, for example `feature/something`, from the branch picker / Start from flow.
3. Leave the auto-filled workspace name unchanged.
4. Create the worktree.
5. Inspect the branch created in the new worktree.

Expected behavior:
Starting from `feature/something` should not unexpectedly flatten the branch name to `feature-something`. The flow should either preserve the selected branch name for the new branch when that is the intended default, or use a safer explicit naming rule that is visible to the user before creation.

Actual behavior:
The selected branch ref is copied into the workspace name and then normalized as a worktree name, so `/` is replaced by `-`.

Code path observed:
- `src/renderer/src/hooks/useComposerState.ts`: `handleSmartBranchSelect` sets both `baseBranch` and, when auto-naming, `name` from `refName`.
- `src/main/ipc/worktree-logic.ts`: `sanitizeWorktreeName()` replaces characters outside letters/numbers/`.`/`_`/`-` with `-`.
- `src/main/ipc/worktree-remote.ts` and `src/main/runtime/orca-runtime.ts`: creation computes the new branch from the sanitized workspace name.

Anything else that might help:
This differs from the base ref behavior: the base branch itself is preserved, but the newly created branch name is flattened because it is derived through the workspace-name sanitizer. This is confusing for users who expect branch names with path components to remain recognizable.
payload.title: [Bug]: Starting from a branch with slashes creates a flattened branch name

payload.author: slashdevcorpse
payload.body:
# Feature Request: AI-Generated Session Naming Tokens for Agent Tabs

## Summary

When running multiple agent sessions, tab titles are volatile and non-descriptive. They flicker with spinners, show raw commands, or display identical agent names ("Claude", "Claude", "Claude"). This makes multi-agent orchestration, which is Orca's core use case, difficult to navigate.

**Proposal**: Add an opt-in setting (`tabAutoGenerateTitle`, disabled by default) that generates a short, stable, descriptive title from the agent's first prompt. This title slots between user-set names and live PTY titles in the display priority chain. Users can still manually rename tabs at any time, and manual names always take precedence.

---

## Problem

### Current title priority (what the tab bar shows):

```
1. customLabel (user-renamed via double-click)
2. label (live PTY title from OSC escape sequences)
3. "Terminal N" ordinal fallback
```

### What goes wrong:

1. **Flickering titles**: Agent CLIs emit rapidly-changing OSC titles during execution. Claude cycles braille spinners (`⠋⠙⠹⠸⠼⠴⠦⠧⠇⠏`), and Gemini updates on every keystroke. `normalizeTerminalTitle()` handles known patterns but does not cover all edge cases.

2. **Indistinguishable sessions**: With 4 to 8 concurrent agent tabs, the tab bar shows "Claude", "Claude", "Claude", "Gemini", or worse, spinner characters. There is no way to tell which session is doing what without clicking into each one.

3. **No semantic identity**: There is no concept of "what is this session working on." The only stable identifier is the tab UUID (meaningless to humans) or `defaultTitle` ("Terminal 3", equally meaningless).

4. **Fragile on failure**: Per #1158 (hydration wipes titles) and #2005 (agent identity lost on reattach), the live PTY title is the weakest link. A persisted semantic name would survive these failures.

### Related issues:
- #480: No programmatic tab creation with names
- #1158: Silent data loss wipes tab titles
- #2005: Agent name lost after pane reattachment
- #1933: Phantom tab auto-creation

---

## How Other AI Environments Solve This

| App | Approach |
|-----|----------|
| **ChatGPT** (chatgpt.com) | Auto-generates a 3 to 6 word conversation title after the first exchange using a lightweight model call |
| **Claude.ai** | Generates conversation titles from the first message; updates if the topic shifts significantly |
| **OpenCode** | Dedicated `titleModel` config with 80 max tokens, separate from the main agent model |
| **Cursor / Windsurf** | Tab titles derived from file context and task description, stable once set |
| **T3 Code / VSmux** | Priority hierarchy: user-set, then AI-generated, then first-prompt, then placeholder. Never overwrites user intent |
| **Claude Code** | Manual only (`/rename`, `--name` flag). Functional but poor default experience |

The industry consensus is clear: auto-generate a short descriptive title from context, but never override a user-set name.

---

## Proposed Solution

### New title priority chain:

```
1. customLabel (user-renamed)            : sacred, never overwritten
2. generatedTitle (AI-derived)           : NEW - stable semantic name from prompt
3. label (live PTY title / agent name)   : current behavior
4. defaultTitle ("Terminal N")            : ordinal fallback
```

### Setting (disabled by default):

Add to `GlobalSettings`:

```typescript
tabAutoGenerateTitle?: boolean  // default: false
```

When **disabled** (default): existing behaviour is unchanged. Tabs show live PTY titles as they do today.

When **enabled**: after the first agent hook payload arrives with a `prompt` field, a short title is derived and stored as `generatedTitle`. This title is stable and does not flicker with agent execution state.

### Generation strategy:

**Heuristic extraction from prompt** (no model call needed):
- Take the user's first prompt from `AgentStatusIpcPayload.prompt` (already available, max 200 chars)
- Strip filler words ("please", "can you", "I wan

payload.body:
## Bug: Not all supported CLI agents appear in the Agents tab

### Description

When running certain CLI tools inside Orca terminal panes, they do not appear in the **Agents tab** in the sidebar. This affects tools that Orca ostensibly supports or should be able to detect, but which are missing from the agent detection registry.

For example, running `kiro chat` in a pane produces no entry in the Agents tab — no status dot, no agent row, nothing. Meanwhile, tools like Codex, Claude Code, and Gemini appear correctly.

This also extends to the **worktree agent indicators** — if the agent isn't detected, it's invisible across the entire sidebar, not just the Agents tab.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Orca
2. Launch a terminal pane and run a CLI agent that isn't in the detection registry (e.g., `kiro chat`, or other newer tools)
3. Observe the Agents tab in the sidebar — no entry appears
4. Compare by running `claude` or `codex` in another pane — those appear correctly

### Expected Behavior

All CLI agents running in Orca terminal panes should be detected and visible in the Agents tab, with appropriate status indicators (running/idle).

### Actual Behavior

Only agents explicitly listed in `agent-kind.ts` and matched by `agent-detection.ts` appear. Any agent not in this allowlist is completely invisible to the Agents tab and sidebar worktree indicators.

### Root Cause

The agent visibility pipeline is gated by a hardcoded allowlist:

1. `src/shared/agent-kind.ts` — defines a finite set of known agent types
2. `src/shared/agent-detection.ts` — pattern-matches process names/command lines against that set
3. If no match → no `AgentKind` assigned → `agent-status` store gets no entry → Agents tab has nothing to render

Additionally, `useWorktreeAgentRows.ts` requires the pane to belong to a registered worktree. Agents running in non-repo directories are invisible even if they ARE detected (related to #1774).

### Affected Agents (non-exhaustive)

- Kiro (`kiro chat`, `kiro-cli`)
- Amp
- Cline
- Cursor Agent
- Any other CLI tool not explicitly in the registry

### Proposed Fix

**Short-term:** Add missing agent entries to `agent-kind.ts` and corresponding detection patterns to `agent-detection.ts`.

**Long-term:** Support user-defined agent detection in `orca.yaml` (aligns with #480) so new tools don't require code changes:

```yaml
customAgents:
  - kind: kiro
    displayName: "Kiro"
    detect:
      processName: "kiro"
      commandPattern: "kiro\\s+(chat|code)"
  - kind: amp
    displayName: "Amp"
    detect:
      processName: "amp"
```

**Sidebar worktree dependency:** The Agents tab should also show agents running in panes that aren't bound to a registered worktree (standalone sessions). Currently these are silently dropped by `buildActivityEvents()`.

### Environment

- Orca version: latest
- OS: Windows / macOS / Linux (all affected — this is a registry-level issue, not platform-specific)
payload.title: Bug: Not all supported CLI agents appear in the Agents tab

payload.author: slashdevcorpse
payload.body:
## Feature Request: Fork Existing Agent Sessions

### Summary

Add the ability to **fork** (branch) an existing agent session — creating a new parallel session that inherits the full conversation context up to the fork point, then diverges independently. Think "right-click → Fork" on any active or completed agent session.

### Motivation

Orca already excels at parallel agent orchestration via git worktrees, but currently there's no way to **branch an existing conversation context**. Common scenarios where this is needed:

1. **Exploring alternatives** — An agent is halfway through implementing auth with JWT; you want to fork and try OAuth2 without losing the JWT progress
2. **Splitting a complex task** — An agent has built up rich context about a codebase; you want to fork that context into multiple specialized subtasks
3. **Recovering from dead ends** — An agent went down a wrong path; fork from an earlier point rather than starting fresh
4. **Review + iterate** — Fork a completed session to ask follow-up questions or request changes without polluting the original

### Proposed Implementation

Since Orca is agent-agnostic and wraps CLI agents via PTY, forking could work at multiple levels:

#### Level 1: Orca-native context fork (indirect)
- Serialize the terminal scrollback/conversation history of the source session
- Create a new worktree (or reuse current)
- Launch a new agent session, injecting the serialized context as initial prompt/context file
- This works with ANY agent CLI — it's passing context through Orca's orchestration layer

#### Level 2: Agent-native fork passthrough
- For agents that support forking natively, Orca could invoke the agent's fork mechanism directly
- Map Orca's fork action → agent-specific fork command

#### Level 3: Full fork (folder-mode projects / no git)
- For workspaces or directories without a git repo, forking creates a **copy-on-write directory clone** (`cp --reflink` on APFS/btrfs, full copy fallback)
- Respect `.orcaignore` or `.gitignore` patterns to skip `node_modules`, build artifacts, etc.
- Register the copied directory as a new folder-mode project linked to the parent
- `orca fork rm` removes the copy and deregisters the project

### `orca fork` CLI Command

```
orca fork [--message <uuid>] [--terminal <handle>] [--name <label>] [--activate] [--no-copy-files]
orca fork list [--worktree <selector>] [--json]
orca fork show <fork-id>
orca fork diff <fork-id-a> <fork-id-b>
orca fork rm <fork-id>
```

**Flags:**
- `--message <uuid>` — Fork agent session at this specific message/checkpoint (truncates after this point). Without this, forks from current end of session.
- `--terminal <handle>` — Which agent terminal's session to fork. Defaults to active terminal.
- `--name <label>` — Label for the fork. Used as branch name suffix (git) or directory suffix (folder-mode).
- `--activate` — Switch the UI to the forked worktree/project immediately.
- `--no-copy-files` — Fork only the agent session, not the workspace files. Useful for retrying a prompt without duplicating the directory.

**Examples:**
```bash
# Fork from current state
orca fork --name "try-redis-approach"

# Fork from a specific message in the agent conversation
orca fork --message msg_a1b2c3d4 --name "before-refactor"

# List forks of current worktree
orca fork list
```

### UX Mockup

```
Sidebar:
├── 🟢 auth-feature (main session)
│   ├── 🟡 auth-feature/fork-1 (trying OAuth2)
│   └── ⚪ auth-feature/fork-2 (trying Passport.js)
├── 🟢 api-refactor
```

**Right-click context menu** on any session → "Fork from here" → pick a message/checkpoint as the fork point.

### Non-Git Workspace Support

For projects without a `.git` directory, forking still works:

```
$ pwd
/home/user/scratch/prototype

$ orca fork --name "approach-b"
Forked: approach-b
  Session: forked at current state
  Path:    /home/user/scratch/prototype-approach-b
  Copy:    reflink (instant)
```

The directory is cloned (CoW where supported), registered as a link
payload.title: Feature: Fork existing agent sessions (context branching)

## Problem or use case

The File Explorer can surface files ignored by git, but users do not have a quick way to switch between a complete filesystem view and a cleaner repo-focused view.

In large projects, ignored directories such as build outputs, caches, generated files, or dependency folders can add noise when the user wants to focus on source-controlled work. At other times, those ignored files still need to be inspected from the File Explorer.

## Proposed solution

Add a File Explorer toolbar toggle that lets users show or hide files ignored by git:

- Default to showing gitignored files so existing behavior remains unchanged.
- Only show the toggle for projects that are git repositories, not regular folders.
- When hidden, filter gitignored files and descendants of gitignored folders out of the File Explorer tree.
- Persist the preference in app settings.
- Request ignored paths from git only when the user hides gitignored files.
- Preserve local, runtime, and SSH-backed worktree support.

## Alternatives or additional context

This is separate from the File Explorer collapse/uncollapse work in #2017.

Related context: #1941 added gitignored File Explorer visibility/decoration. This issue is specifically for adding a user-controlled show/hide toggle.

Implementation notes:

- Use `git status --porcelain=v2 --ignored=matching` only when the toggle needs ignored-path data.
- Keep ignored paths separate from normal git status entries so source-control badges remain unchanged.
- Match ignored descendants by normalized relative paths without confusing sibling prefixes such as `dist` and `dist2`.
- Add regression coverage for git status parsing, local/runtime/SSH propagation, settings persistence, filtering behavior, and toolbar visibility for non-git folders.
payload.title: [Feature]: Add File Explorer toggle for gitignored files

payload.author: leynier
payload.body:
### Problem or use case

I often open a parent folder in Orca that contains multiple projects or repositories. That parent folder is not always a Git repository itself; it is just the directory where I organize my work.

Today, if I find a child folder in the File Explorer that I want to add as its own Orca project, I have to copy or remember the folder path, open Add Project, choose Browse folder, and select the same folder again from the native picker.

This makes the workflow slower when using Orca from a parent “projects” folder.

### Proposed solution

Add a File Explorer context-menu action for directories in folder-mode projects, for example:

- `Add as Project...`

When selected, Orca should show a confirmation step with the selected folder path. After confirmation, it should follow the same behavior as Add Project > Browse folder, but with the folder already selected.

Expected behavior:

- The action is available when right-clicking a folder in the File Explorer for a non-Git/folder-mode project.
- The confirmation clearly shows which folder will be added.
- If the selected folder is a Git repository, Orca adds it as a normal Git project and continues to the existing setup step.
- If the selected folder is not a Git repository, Orca uses the existing “Open as Folder” confirmation/flow.
- The existing Add Project flow remains unchanged.

### Alternatives or additional context

This is related to the existing Add Project flow, but the goal is not to replace Browse folder. It is a shortcut for the case where the user is already looking at the target folder inside Orca’s File Explorer.

Related issues:

- #763 added an easier way to create a new repo/folder.
- #766 renamed Add Repo to Add Project because not all folders are Git repos.
- #1602 discusses broader multi-repository organization.
- #1846 discusses per-project paths.

This issue intentionally scopes the first version to folder-mode projects. Showing the action inside Git repositories may need stricter repo-root detection to avoid accidentally adding arbitrary subfolders from an existing repository as separate projects.
payload.title: [Feature]: Add project from File Explorer folder context menu

payload.author: leynier
payload.body:
## Problem or use case

The File Explorer currently lets users expand and collapse individual folders, but it lacks fast controls for collapsing the current expanded tree or recursively expanding/collapsing a folder subtree.

When working in deeply nested projects, users have to manually close many expanded folders one by one or repeatedly expand each nested folder to inspect a subtree. This makes navigation slower in large repos and long-lived worktrees.

## Proposed solution

Add File Explorer controls for folder collapse/uncollapse workflows:

- Add a toolbar "Collapse All" action that collapses all expanded directories in the active worktree.
- Add a folder context-menu action that switches between:
  - "Collapse Folder" when the folder is currently expanded.
  - "Uncollapse Folder" when the folder is currently collapsed.
- "Collapse Folder" should collapse the selected folder and all expanded descendants.
- "Uncollapse Folder" should recursively expand the selected folder subtree.
- Recursive uncollapse should avoid following symlink directories to prevent cycles across local and SSH-backed filesystems.
- Keep expanded directory state scoped per worktree.

## Alternatives or additional context

This is intended as a focused File Explorer navigation improvement. It is separate from any future option to show or hide files ignored by git.

Implementation notes:

- Use existing File Explorer toolbar and context-menu patterns.
- Use existing path utilities so behavior remains cross-platform.
- Preserve SSH support by using the existing directory-read abstraction rather than assuming local filesystem access.
- Add regression coverage for collapse-all, subtree collapse, recursive uncollapse, and symlink directory handling.
payload.title: [Feature]: Add collapse and uncollapse actions to File Explorer folders

payload.author: timothyjlaurent
payload.body:
## Symptom

After an SSH relay channel drops (SSH session stays alive but the relay multiplexer dies), the target's UI status doesn't visibly distinguish itself from a healthy state. Clicking actions that require the SSH git provider (e.g. **Create worktree**) produces an opaque error to the user:

```
Error invoking remote method 'worktrees:create': Error: No git provider for connection "ssh-<id>"
```

The string `No git provider for connection` is the internal exception message from `src/main/ipc/worktrees.ts:528` (and 4 other call sites). It doesn't tell the user **what to do** — the actual fix is "click Reconnect on the SSH target."

## Repro

1. Connect to a remote target (especially via a `proxyCommand` like `coder ssh --stdio` where channel flakiness is common).
2. Let the relay channel drop (idle long enough for grace period, or kill the `--connect` bridge process on the remote).
3. SSH session stays up, but `watchMuxForRelayLoss` at `src/main/ssh/ssh-relay-session.ts:411` fires → `teardownProviders('connection_lost')` → `unregisterSshGitProvider` → state goes `disposed` per `ssh-relay-session.ts:401`.
4. UI still surfaces the target as if usable.
5. Click **Create worktree** on a repo bound to that target.
6. Get the opaque error above.

Manual reconnect re-runs `registerProviders()` → providers re-register → action works.

## Root cause

There's a clean state→capability gap:
- `SshRelayConnection.state` is `disposed`/`idle` after `_onRelayLost`.
- Git provider is unregistered.
- But the renderer's view of the target doesn't update — it doesn't subscribe to provider-availability changes, only to higher-level connection state, and the visual signal for `disposed` isn't strong enough to stop the click.

## Proposed fix (pick one or both)

**A) Surface the dropped state in the UI loudly.** When state transitions to `disposed` or `idle` post-`_onRelayLost`:
- Show the target with a red/amber indicator + a "Reconnect" CTA inline
- Disable (grey out) every action on repos bound to that target until reconnect succeeds
- Cover: worktrees:create, worktrees:remove, filesystem reads, the git operations in `orca-runtime-git.ts:43-100`

**B) Replace the opaque exception text with a user-actionable error.** In each of the 5 call sites that throw `\`No git provider for connection "${...}"\``, replace with something the user can act on:

```ts
throw new Error(
  'Remote connection dropped. Click Reconnect on the SSH target before retrying.'
)
```

Files to touch:
- \`src/main/runtime/orca-runtime.ts:5959\`
- \`src/main/ipc/worktrees.ts:528\`
- \`src/main/ipc/filesystem.ts:540, 561, 585\`
- Any other \`getSshGitProvider\` call site that throws

A central helper would be DRYer:

```ts
function requireSshGitProvider(connectionId: string): SshGitProvider {
  const provider = getSshGitProvider(connectionId)
  if (!provider) {
    throw new Error('Remote connection dropped. Click Reconnect on the SSH target before retrying.')
  }
  return provider
}
```

A) is the real fix (prevents the click); B) is the cheap defensive layer for when the UI subscription lags.

## Why it matters more for proxyCommand-backed targets

`coder ssh --stdio` and similar proxyCommand setups are inherently more failure-prone than direct SSH:
- Coder workspace can scale down mid-session
- Network blips between Coder's gateway and the workspace
- The proxy process itself can crash

These setups will continue to drop the relay channel periodically. Without A or B above, every drop produces a confusing error and the user has to learn to reconnect by trial and error.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] After relay channel drop, target's UI status visibly differs from healthy state (color + label)
- [ ] Actions requiring the git provider are disabled while state is not \`ready\`
- [ ] If an action somehow does fire (race), the error message tells the user to reconnect
- [ ] Reconnect button is one click away
payload.title: UX: surface relay-channel-loss state instead of opaque 'No git provider for connection' error

payload.author: prateek
payload.body:
# Floating terminal auto-creates tab after user closes the last one

## Symptom

When the floating terminal has a single tab open and the user clicks the X button to close it, the panel auto-creates a new terminal tab instead of closing the panel. The user has to close the panel manually via the minimize button or by closing the newly created tab again.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open the floating terminal (Cmd+Alt+T on Mac / Ctrl+Alt+T on Windows/Linux)
2. The panel opens with one auto-created terminal tab
3. Click the X button on that tab to close it
4. **Expected**: Panel closes cleanly
5. **Actual**: Panel stays open with a fresh auto-created tab

## Root cause

The `closeTab` callback used for the X button triggers the auto-create effect (lines 102-108 in `FloatingTerminalPanel.tsx`) that spawns a tab whenever the panel is open with zero tabs. The panel never closes because a replacement tab is created before the close check can run.

Additionally, `closeOthers` and `closeToRight` context menu actions had stale closure bugs—they read `tabs.length` from the captured array in `useCallback` dependencies instead of pulling fresh state via `useAppStore.getState()`, causing these callbacks to operate on outdated tab lists.

## Expected behavior

- Clicking X on the last terminal tab should close the floating panel (symmetric with the auto-create on open)
- The panel should remain open if a PTY exits so the user can see exit status
- Multi-tab operations (`closeOthers`, `closeToRight`) should operate on current state, not stale captures

## Why it matters

The asymmetry breaks user expectations: the panel auto-creates a tab on open (hotkey press), but closing that tab doesn't reverse the action. Users expect the X button on the last tab to dismiss the panel, not spawn an orphaned replacement.

## Environment

- All platforms (macOS, Linux, Windows)
- Floating terminal feature introduced in recent releases
payload.title: Floating terminal auto-creates tab after user closes the last one

## Summary

AI commit messages should support the local agents Orca can invoke safely in non-interactive mode, with model handling that matches each CLI instead of assuming a single provider shape.

## Supported agents

Users can enable AI commit messages and choose from these built-in agents:

- Claude Code
- Codex
- OpenCode
- Pi
- Gemini
- Amp
- Cursor
- Kimi
- GitHub Copilot

## Model behavior

- Dynamic model discovery is used when the agent CLI exposes a model list: Codex, OpenCode, Pi, and Cursor.
- Static catalogs are maintained for agents whose CLIs do not expose a reliable model endpoint for this workflow: Claude Code, Gemini, Amp, Kimi, and GitHub Copilot.
- GitHub Copilot lists the hosted Copilot CLI catalog while still allowing account and organization policies to determine which selections actually run.
- Gemini uses the model aliases and preview IDs accepted by its headless CLI execution path.
- Kimi uses its provider-qualified model ID and keeps the user config default available.
- Model selections and discovered catalogs are scoped by execution host so local and SSH worktrees do not share incompatible state.

## Acceptance criteria

- AI commit messages can be generated with each supported built-in agent that provides a non-interactive execution mode.
- Dynamic model discovery refreshes model lists without leaking host-specific catalogs between local and SSH worktrees.
- Static model catalogs reflect the agent-specific model IDs accepted by the corresponding CLI.
- The settings UI exposes agent, model, and thinking-effort controls where supported, with refresh controls for dynamic catalogs.
- Commit message generation remains read-only/non-destructive for built-in agents.
- Missing CLIs, unavailable models, invalid credentials, and auth/policy failures are surfaced as user-facing errors.

## Summary

Add support for importing cookies from [Comet](https://comet.perplexity.ai/) — Perplexity's Chromium-based browser — alongside the existing Chrome / Edge / Arc / Brave / Firefox / Safari sources.

## Why

Comet adoption is growing among power users (AI-native browser). Users moving from Comet to Orca currently have no way to bring their logged-in sessions across, forcing manual re-login on every site.

Comet is Chromium-based, so it reuses the same cookie DB layout (`<Profile>/Network/Cookies`) and the same Safe Storage keychain encryption pattern as Chrome/Edge/Brave. The import pipeline should already work — only the browser registration is missing.

## Platform support

Comet ships **macOS and Windows only** as of 2026-05-15. No official Linux build. Orca on Linux will gracefully skip Comet detection (existing `browserRootPath()` returns `null` when `linuxRoot` is undefined).

## Changes required

1. **`src/main/browser/browser-cookie-import.ts`** — add a `CHROMIUM_BROWSERS` entry:
   - `family: 'comet'` (new discriminator — see open question)
   - `label: 'Comet'`
   - `keychainService: 'Comet Safe Storage'` (verify on macOS Keychain)
   - `keychainAccount: 'Comet'`
   - `macRoot: 'Perplexity/Comet'` (verify — likely `~/Library/Application Support/Perplexity/Comet`)
   - `winRoot`: verify path under `%LOCALAPPDATA%`
   - `linuxRoot`: omit (no Linux build)

2. **`src/shared/types.ts`** — `BrowserSessionProfileSource.browserFamily` union currently: `'chrome' | 'chromium' | 'arc' | 'edge' | 'firefox' | 'safari' | 'manual'`. Add `'comet'` discriminator (do not fold into `'chromium'` — that slot is already overloaded with Brave).

3. **`src/shared/constants.ts`** — add `comet: 'Comet'` to `BROWSER_FAMILY_LABELS`.

4. **UI labels** — `BrowserPane.tsx` description ("import cookies from Chrome, Edge, or other browsers") updated to mention Comet.

5. **Tests** — extend `src/main/browser/browser-session-registry.test.ts` and `src/main/runtime/rpc/methods/browser.test.ts` with a Comet fixture. Add a `browser-cookie-import.test.ts` for detection coverage.

## Open questions

- Exact Safe Storage keychain service name on macOS — needs verification on a machine with Comet installed.
- Exact data dir paths on macOS and Windows.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Comet appears in the browser picker on Settings → Browser → Session & Cookies (when running on a platform that supports Comet)
- [ ] Profiles enumerate from Comet's `Local State` `profile.info_cache`
- [ ] Cookies decrypt and import on **macOS** and **Windows**
- [ ] On Linux, Comet is silently absent from the picker (no errors)
- [ ] SSH use case still works (no local-only assumptions)
- [ ] Tests cover the new browser family

## Implementation plan

See `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-15-comet-browser-cookie-support.md` in branch `timothyjlaurent/Comet-browser-cookie-support`.

## Symptom

Desktop terminal session unexpectedly renders at phone-sized dimensions (narrow column count, fewer rows). Typing into the pane appears to do nothing. There is no obvious indicator on the desktop explaining why.

## Reproduction (loose — encountered organically)

1. Open the desktop app with an active terminal session.
2. From the iOS app, connect to that same session — the relay PTY gets resized to the phone viewport via the mobile-presence lock (see [`docs/mobile-presence-lock.md`](./docs/mobile-presence-lock.md)).
3. Quit / background the iOS app.
4. Return focus to the desktop app and the affected terminal pane.

Expected: the desktop user immediately understands why the terminal is squished and how to recover.

Actual: the existing presence-lock banner DID render — it's a 4-pixel grey strip glued to the top of the pane in roughly the same colour as the empty terminal background, easy to miss especially when the user is focused on the prompt below. The desktop user's keyboard input is silently dropped (the documented presence-lock behaviour) and the cause is not obvious.

## Evidence

The current banner — the thin grey strip across the top of the terminal:

![current-banner](https://github.com/prateek/orca/blob/6ae5035e3965e705e180e55f59bc99c2505124f5/02-mobile-driving.png?raw=true)

## Root cause

This is a **UX visibility** bug, not a state-machine bug. The mobile-presence lock state machine is working correctly:
- The fit override is set when mobile subscribes.
- The driver flips to `mobile{clientId}` when the phone takes the floor.
- The held-at-phone-fit state persists indefinitely after the phone disconnects (per [`docs/mobile-fit-hold.md`](./docs/mobile-fit-hold.md), `mobileAutoRestoreFitMs` defaults to `null`).
- The banner is the documented escape hatch with a working `Restore` button.

The bug is that the banner's visual treatment is ineffective at communicating any of the above to the user.

## Fix

PR #1899 replaces the banner with a full-pane overlay (loud) that the user can collapse to a corner chip if they want to keep watching live mobile output. Adds e2e regression coverage for the mount/dismiss state transitions.
payload.title: Desktop terminal can get stuck at phone dimensions with no visible explanation

payload.author: Sharpek
payload.body:
### Problem or use case

Copying short snippets in Orca currently requires the full select → Ctrl+C → focus target → Ctrl+V dance, even for tiny, repetitive paste operations (IDs, paths, names, error codes, etc.).

In many tools — Linux terminals, most Linux browsers, tmux, xterm, GTK/Qt apps — selecting text automatically places it into a "primary selection" buffer, and a middle-click (pressing the mouse wheel as a button) pastes it at the cursor. This is a separate channel from the regular Ctrl+C/Ctrl+V clipboard, so it doesn't clobber whatever you already have copied. It's a meaningful productivity boost once you're used to it, and its absence in Orca breaks muscle memory for users coming from those environments.

### Proposed solution

Add primary-selection-style middle-click paste:

1. When the user selects text anywhere in Orca, store the selection in a dedicated primary buffer (separate from the OS clipboard — Ctrl+C/Ctrl+V remain untouched).
2. A middle-click (mouse wheel button press) inside any editable field/text area pastes the current primary buffer at the click position.
3. Make it togglable in Settings → Input/Editing, with a sensible per-platform default:
   - Linux: enabled by default (matches platform convention).
   - macOS / Windows: disabled by default (users there typically don't expect this and middle-click is often bound to other actions).
4. No paste if the buffer is empty or the target isn't editable — fail silently rather than intercepting the click.

Nice-to-haves (not required for v1):
- Visual hint (subtle cursor change) over editable areas when a primary buffer is non-empty.
- Respect existing middle-click bindings (e.g. open-link-in-new-tab) and only act on editable surfaces.

payload.author: nwparker
payload.body:
## Context

PR #1737 attempted to honor user `ZDOTDIR` for XDG-style zsh setups, but was reverted in #1864 because the implementation sourced the user `.zshenv` inside a wrapper function. That can change normal zsh scoping behavior for common startup-file patterns, for example `typeset -U path` followed by `path=(...)`, because `typeset` becomes function-scoped.

We still need to support users who set `ZDOTDIR` from `.zshenv`, but the fix must preserve zsh startup-file semantics.

## Goal

Find and land a safer implementation that lets Orca discover/honor `ZDOTDIR` without sourcing user `.zshenv` in a context that changes variable scoping or other shell semantics.

## Acceptance criteria

- XDG-style zsh users who set `ZDOTDIR` in `~/.zshenv` get their intended rcfiles.
- Common `.zshenv` patterns using `typeset`, `path`, `fpath`, exports, aliases/functions, and early `return` behave as they would under normal zsh startup.
- Add regression tests covering at least `ZDOTDIR`, early `return`, and `typeset -U path` / `path=(...)` behavior.
- Validate both daemon shell-ready and local PTY shell-ready paths.

## Links

- Original PR: #1737
- Revert PR: #1864
payload.title: Support zsh ZDOTDIR without changing .zshenv evaluation semantics

### Problem or use case

Right now it is hard to keep the project setup clean when each project needs its own set of local worktree I use Orca as an IDE for multiple separate projects/repositories.

Each project has its own parent folder and may have its own parent-level instructions, for example AGENTS.md. I want Orca to understand the project’s parent path and create/find Git worktrees in a path configured for that specific project.

The main use case:

- Project A has its own parent folder and instructions.
- I want worktrees for Project A to be created in something like `../worktrees` relative to that project parent/repository path.
- Project B is a different repository with a different parent folder and possibly different instructions.

## Summary
Orca's Explorer currently only supports selecting one file or folder at a time. It stores a single `selectedPath`, so modifier-click gestures replace the current selection instead of extending it.

## Expected behavior
The Explorer should support standard file-tree multi-select gestures:

- `Shift` + click selects a contiguous range between the anchor item and clicked item.
- `Cmd` + click on macOS, or `Ctrl` + click on Windows/Linux, toggles individual files/folders in the selection.
- Context-menu actions and drag/drop should operate on the selected set when the clicked/dragged row is part of the selection.
- Single click without modifiers should keep the existing one-item behavior.

## Current behavior
Clicking any row calls the Explorer click handler and replaces the selection with that row. `Shift`-click and `Cmd/Ctrl`-click do not add, remove, or range-select rows.

## Implementation notes
Likely areas:

- `src/renderer/src/components/right-sidebar/FileExplorer.tsx`
- `src/renderer/src/components/right-sidebar/useFileExplorerHandlers.ts`
- `src/renderer/src/components/right-sidebar/FileExplorerRow.tsx`

The current state appears to be centered on a single `selectedPath`; multi-select will likely need a selected-path set plus an anchor path/index for range selection. Keep platform handling cross-platform: use `metaKey` on macOS and `ctrlKey` on Windows/Linux.

## Why this matters
Users expect Explorer-style file trees to support selecting multiple files for operations like delete, move, copy path, and future batch actions.

payload.author: slashdevcorpse
payload.body:
## Feature Request

Add an **Automations** tab to the left sidebar (below Search, above Workspaces) that lets users view, create, and edit scheduled and event-triggered agent tasks from a single surface.

## Current Behavior

Orca's automation system today lives entirely in `orca.yaml` and the Settings > Worktree Hooks pane:

```yaml
scripts:
  setup: |
    pnpm worktree:setup
  archive: |
    echo "Cleaning up before archive"
issueCommand: |
  Complete {{artifact_url}}
```

The Settings pane provides:
- "When to Run Setup" policy (ask / run by default / skip by default)
- Custom GitHub Issue Command field (uses `{{artifact_url}}` for the linked issue/PR URL)
- Detection of whether `orca.yaml` exists in the repo

This works, but:
- There is no scheduled/recurring automation support (cron-style "run X every N hours")
- There is no unified view of all hooks across repos and workspaces
- Creating or editing hooks requires manually writing YAML or navigating per-repo settings individually
- There is no run history or status tracking
- Workspaces without repos have no automation path at all

## Proposed Behavior

### Automations Tab (Sidebar)

A dedicated tab showing all configured automations in one list.

| Column | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| Name | User-defined automation name |
| Provider | Agent CLI logo (icons already exist in Orca) |
| Trigger | Schedule (cron), worktree create, issue linked, manual |
| Target | Repo or workspace this automation belongs to |
| Status | Active / Paused / Errored |
| Last Run | Timestamp of most recent execution |

Groupable by: name, schedule, repo, workspace, provider.

### Create and Edit (Form UI)

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| Name | Human-readable label |
| Trigger type | Schedule/cron, worktree create, issue linked, manual |
| Prompt | The instruction passed to the agent |
| Provider | Which CLI agent to target |
| Target | Repo or workspace |
| Session reuse | Toggle: reuse same session across runs (see below) |

### Session Reuse (Per-Automation)

Automations can optionally reuse the same agent session across runs, preserving semantic memory and context. This is configurable per automation because different tasks have different needs (email/drafts checking benefits from accumulated context, a linting pass does not). Session reuse ties into each CLI's resume capability. Automations targeting agents without resume support always start fresh.

### Automation Scopes

| Scope | Location | Use case |
|-------|----------|----------|
| Repo-committed | `orca.yaml` in repo root | Shared team automations, version-controlled |
| Workspace-level | `.orca/automations.yaml` (local) | Personal automations, workspace-only setups, repos without git |

Both scopes are required. Workspace-level automations are necessary for users running Orca without repos. Without this, those users have no automation path.

### CLI Support

The Orca CLI must support automation CRUD so agents themselves can register automations:

```
orca automations list
orca automations create --name "..." --trigger "..." --prompt "..." --provider "..."
orca automations edit <id>
orca automations remove <id>
```

This means a user can ask any agent inside Orca to "set up a daily code review automation" and the agent calls `orca automations create` to register it. The CLI writes to the same config the UI reads.

### Defaults

Disabled by default. Users opt in via Settings.

## Benefits

- Makes existing `orca.yaml` hook functionality discoverable without reading docs
- Adds scheduled/recurring capability that does not exist today
- Workspace-level automations support repo-less setups
- Session reuse preserves context for tasks that benefit from continuity
- CLI parity means agents can self-register automations on behalf of the user
- Provider-agnostic: any CLI agent works as the execution target
- Builds on the existing hook system rather than replacing it
payload.title: feat: Automations tab in sidebar for managing scheduled and event-triggered agent tasks

payload.author: slashdevcorpse
payload.body:
## Problem

When a worktree is slept, `dropAgentStatusByWorktree` wipes all agent status rows. No record of the running agent survives: agent type, session ID, last prompt, and resume command are all lost. The user wakes the worktree, sees terminal scrollback, but has zero affordance to resume the agent conversation they were in. They must manually remember which agent was running, find the session ID, and type the resume command themselves.

Similar ADEs have resolved this by storing simple metadata and cache locally so the user can start where they left off. The agents themselves already persist their sessions (Claude via `--resume`, Codex via `resume --last`, Kiro via `--resume-id`). The ADE only needs to store a pointer, not duplicate the conversation.

## Proposed Solution

Store a lightweight agent session record (agent type, session ID, resume command, last prompt summary, ~500 bytes per agent) at sleep time, before the agent status is dropped. On wake, offer a one-click resume that executes the stored command.

Not all CLIs support session resume. Each agent needs to be checked for resume capability. Agents without it should be clearly marked as incompatible in the UI rather than silently failing.

The UI needs clear visual separation between:
1. **Active agents** (running now)
2. **Sleeping, resumable agents** (conversation preserved, can be woken)
3. **Sleeping, non-resumable agents** (CLI lacks resume support, current behavior)

This differentiation is required so users are not confused about what can and cannot be resumed.

## Settings

- Disabled by default. Must be explicitly enabled by the user.
- Global toggle: enable/disable agent session persistence on sleep
- Per-workspace override: `inherit` / `always` / `never` (follows existing per-repo settings pattern in `RepoHookSettings`)
- Auto-resume on wake: optional setting for zero-click resume

## Cleanup / Retention

- Configurable per-workspace: `permanent` (never prune) or N days (default: 30)
- Records cleared on explicit worktree remove (not sleep)
- If the agent's own session is gone, the resume command fails gracefully on the agent side

## Benefits

- One-click resume instead of manual session archaeology
- No duplication of agent data (agents own history, Orca stores a pointer)
- Minimal storage footprint
- Per-workspace control so users opt in only where it matters
- Disabled by default, zero overhead for users who do not want it
- Prepares metadata layer for future mobile sync without coupling to it now

## Notes

- Not all CLI agents support session resume. Each agent needs to be checked. Incompatible agents must be clearly indicated in the UI.
- Happy to work on this for the desktop version.
- Mobile (iOS/Android) is a separate effort but this lays the groundwork.
payload.title: feat: persist agent session metadata on sleep for one-click resume on wake

payload.author: slashdevcorpse
payload.body:
## Problem

The Activity page (bell icon → agent thread list) renders zero threads when the workspace has no registered repo, even if agents are actively running in terminals.

## Root Cause

`buildActivityEvents()` in `ActivityPrototypePage.tsx` builds a `tabContext` map by iterating `worktreeMap.values()`:

```ts
for (const worktree of args.worktreeMap.values()) {
  const tabs = args.tabsByWorktree[worktree.id] ?? []
  for (const tab of tabs) {
    tabContext.set(tab.id, { worktree, tab })
  }
}
```

Later, every agent status entry is looked up against this map:

```ts
const context = tabContext.get(tabId)
if (!context) continue // silently dropped
```

No repo → no worktrees → empty `tabContext` → every agent event is dropped → empty Activity page.

The same pattern affects `WorktreeCardAgents` (sidebar inline agents) and `useWorktreeAgentRows`, which both key off `tabsByWorktree[worktreeId]`.

## Expected Behavior

Agents running in a repo-less workspace should still appear in the Activity view. The status pipeline shouldn't require a git repo to function.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Orca with a workspace that has no repos added
2. Launch an agent (Claude, Codex, etc.) in a terminal
3. Open Activity page (bell icon in sidebar)
4. Observe: "No activity yet" despite agent running

## Environment

- Orca v1.3.51 (latest stable)
- Windows

## Related

#1727 (merged) fixes CLI-spawned terminals lacking `paneKey` env attribution, but that fix still requires a worktree to exist — it doesn't address the no-repo case.

cc @brennanb2025 — wanted to flag this as a potential gap. The paneKey fix in #1727 is great but the activity pipeline still hard-depends on worktrees existing. Might already be on the radar or planned for a later stage, but figured it's worth tracking.
payload.title: [Feature]: Activity view should show AI activities even when there is no repo

payload.author: prateek
payload.body:
## Summary

When Orca spawns a zsh PTY that needs to wait for shell-ready (agent launch, attribution shim, anything routed through `getShellReadyLaunchConfig` or `getAttributionShellLaunchConfig`), it pins `ZDOTDIR` to a wrapper dir under `<userData>/shell-ready/zsh/` (e.g. `~/Library/Application Support/orca/...` on macOS, `~/.config/orca/...` on Linux). The wrapper's `.zshenv` sources `~/.zshenv`, but the wrapper has already committed to a value for `ORCA_ORIG_ZDOTDIR` (the path the rest of the wrapper uses to find the user's `.zshrc`/`.zprofile`/`.zlogin`). So for users whose `~/.zshenv` follows the canonical XDG idiom

```zsh
export ZDOTDIR="${ZDOTDIR:-$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/zsh}"
```

the wrapper's downstream rcfiles source `$HOME/.zshrc` (typically a stub or absent) instead of `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/zsh/.zshrc` (the real config). User functions, aliases, and PATH edits silently disappear inside the affected PTYs.

## Repro

1. `~/.zshenv`:

   ```zsh
   export ZDOTDIR="${ZDOTDIR:-$HOME/.config/zsh}"
   ```

2. `~/.config/zsh/.zshrc`:

   ```zsh
   hello() { echo "from xdg .zshrc"; }
   ```

3. `~/.zshrc`: empty / absent.

4. Launch Orca with no inherited `ZDOTDIR` (Spotlight, Dock, Finder, or a Linux desktop launcher — the GUI launch path inherits nothing from a shell).

5. From the orca CLI, spawn a PTY that goes through shell-ready, e.g. an agent launch or:

   ```
   orca terminal create --worktree active --command hello
   ```

   The shell-ready wrapper sources `~/.zshrc` instead of `~/.config/zsh/.zshrc`, so the `hello` function defined in step 2 never gets loaded.

6. Observed: `zsh: command not found: hello`.

   Expected: `from xdg .zshrc` — the function would resolve in any normal zsh session.

## Root cause

The `zshEnv` template inside `ensureShellReadyWrappers()` in `src/main/providers/local-pty-shell-ready.ts` writes this into the wrapper dir:

```zsh
export ORCA_ORIG_ZDOTDIR="${ORCA_ORIG_ZDOTDIR:-$HOME}"
case "${ORCA_ORIG_ZDOTDIR%/}" in
  */shell-ready/zsh) export ORCA_ORIG_ZDOTDIR="$HOME" ;;
esac
[[ -f "$ORCA_ORIG_ZDOTDIR/.zshenv" ]] && source "$ORCA_ORIG_ZDOTDIR/.zshenv"
export ZDOTDIR='<wrapper dir>'
```

`ORCA_ORIG_ZDOTDIR` is set in the spawn env from `resolveOriginalZdotdir()`, which reads `process.env.ZDOTDIR` from the Electron main process. On a GUI launch this is `undefined`, so the spawn env passes `ORCA_ORIG_ZDOTDIR=$HOME`. The user's `~/.zshenv` does run and *does* set `ZDOTDIR=~/.config/zsh`, but two things happen next:

- The very next line overwrites `ZDOTDIR` with the wrapper dir.
- `ORCA_ORIG_ZDOTDIR` was already pinned to `$HOME` before `.zshenv` ran, so the downstream wrapper rcfiles (`.zprofile`, `.zshrc`, `.zlogin`) all use `$HOME` as `_orca_home` and source the wrong files.

The daemon mirror in `src/main/daemon/shell-ready.ts` has the same bug. Both code paths flow through the same wrapper files, so this affects both `getShellReadyLaunchConfig` (startup-command PTYs) and `getAttributionShellLaunchConfig` (attribution-shim PTYs that don't emit a ready marker but still need user config to resolve). SSH PTYs are also affected because they run the daemon on the remote host.

## Why this matters

XDG-style zsh is a documented zsh-supported pattern — `man zshall`'s `STARTUP/SHUTDOWN FILES` section names `ZDOTDIR` as the lookup root for everything except `.zshenv` itself. It's the recommended layout for Arch Linux's zsh package, prezto's installer, xdg-ninja, and most "clean `$HOME`" dotfile setups. For these users, *every* feature that goes through shell-ready runs against an empty config: agent launches, the attribution overlay, and any `--command` startup invocation.

Bash users hit a different shape of the same problem only if their `~/.bash_profile` is unusual; the wrapper's bash startup chain (login files → `.bashrc` via the user's own profile) follows the standard contract, so vanilla bash setups are unaffected.

## Proposed fix

Let the user's `.zshenv` compute its preferred `ZDOTDIR` first, *
payload.title: shell-ready zsh wrapper drops user's ZDOTDIR before sourcing .zshenv (XDG layout broken)

payload.author: prateek
payload.body:
## What's wrong

Each worktree card in the sidebar renders an `▾ AGENTS (n)` header with a chevron that toggles the inline agent list open or closed for that one workspace. It's a second control on top of one we already have, and it sits inside the click target users actually want to hit.

Two concrete problems:

1. **Redundant.** Whether the inline agent list shows up at all is already controlled globally by the `inline-agents` view option in the sidebar header. If a user doesn't want agent rows on their cards, they turn that off — for every workspace, in one place. The per-workspace chevron just lets them flip the same decision card by card, with no value over the global toggle.
2. **Misclick magnet.** The header sits roughly one row-height above the agent it's meant to label. Aiming for the agent row and hitting the chevron instead collapses the section the user wanted to interact with.

## Proposed fix

Remove the toggle entirely. Always render agents inline when the global `inline-agents` view option is on; never render them when it's off. Drop the matching per-worktree collapse state from the UI store along with it.

Drop the header section as a whole rather than keeping a static "AGENTS (n)" label. There are usually only one or two agents per worktree, the agent rows already self-identify with the spark icon, and removing the header gives the agent rows a touch more breathing room above. Keep a `role="group"` + `aria-label="Agents"` on the wrapper so screen-reader users still get a labeled region.
payload.title: Sidebar: drop the per-workspace AGENTS toggle

## Bug Report

Orca hits Anthropic API rate limits during normal usage.

**Behavior:** API calls accumulate faster than expected mid-session, causing rate limit errors that interrupt workflow.

**Diagnosis:** Blocking Anthropic IPs via Lulu firewall (macOS) eliminated rate limit errors entirely — confirming the source is background API calls, not user-triggered requests. Likely culprit: polling, telemetry, keepalive, or context-refresh calls firing independently of user actions.

**Expected behavior:** Anthropic API calls should only fire on user-initiated actions.

**Proposed fix:** Make background API call frequency user-configurable with interval options (e.g. 5 min, 15 min, 30 min), similar to how OpenUsage handles polling intervals. Default to a conservative interval, not continuous polling.

### Operating system

macOS

### Orca version

1.3.50

### Details

## Short summary:
Orca fetches GitHub Issues in a repo-scoped way, so gh can infer the repo’s host from the checkout. GitHub Projects calls are made as global, hostless gh api graphql calls, so gh falls back to its globally active/default host instead.
In multi-host setups, Orca ends up checking auth/scopes against the wrong GitHub instance and shows the misleading project-scope message.

## What happened
* Issues work because those calls run with cwd=repoPath, so gh resolves the repo host from the git remote.
* Projects fail because listAccessibleProjects, resolveProjectRef, and the shared project GraphQL/REST helpers do not pass a host.
* The auth error is misleading because diagnoseGhAuth() also reads gh auth status globally and picks the globally active account, not the account for the repo’s host.
* Paste-to-add is also single-host biased: project URL parsing currently only accepts https://github.com/..., so GHES-style project URLs are not handled correctly.

## How to reproduce

  1. Authenticate gh to at least two hosts, for example:
   * github.com
   * a GHES/GHE-hosted instance
  2. Make sure the repo opened in Orca belongs to the non-default host.
  3. Give the correct host token the project scope.
  4. In Orca:
   * open the repo
   * confirm GitHub Issues load
   * open GitHub Projects
  5. Orca shows:
   * Your gh token is missing the project scope... even though the correct host already has that scope, because Orca is checking/calling the wrong host.

## Expected behavior

Project discovery, project view fetches, and auth diagnosis should target the same host as the repo/project, not gh’s global active host.
payload.title: [Bug]: GitHub Projects uses the wrong gh host in multi-host setups and incorrectly reports missing project scope
