payload.author: Jinwoo-H
payload.body:
## Context

Today the SSH relay deploy runs `npm install node-pty` on the remote host at first connect. This requires:

- npm + node on the remote (we already deploy node)
- Either a matching node-pty prebuild on the registry OR build tools (python3, make, g++) on the remote
- Network access to the npm registry from the remote

This has been the source of multiple bugs:

- #1660 reconnect loop (root cause was unrelated, but the fix made the install dir name contain `+` which broke npm-init — see commit 963f56d7 on `Jinwoo-H/ssh-typing-lag`)
- npm 11 / Node 26 strict semver name validation rejects `+` in package names derived from dir basename
- A remote without compilers can't install node-pty at all → relay degrades to fs/git/preflight without PTY (graceful but confusing to users)
- Transient registry failures during install can leave a partially-installed dir that requires manual cleanup

## How VS Code does it

VS Code's remote server (`vscode-reh`) is a fully pre-built tarball, generated on their CI per platform (`vscode-server-linux-x64.tar.gz`, `...-linux-arm64`, `...-darwin-x64`, `...-darwin-arm64`, plus Alpine variants). The tarball already contains `node_modules/node-pty/` with the right prebuild for that platform.

Their remote-install flow:

1. `prereqs.rs::verify()` detects glibc/glibcxx/musl on the remote → picks the matching tarball (or returns `PrerequisitesFailed` if requirements aren't met)
2. Download the tarball
3. Extract via `decompress_tarball` (Rust gunzip + tar reader, no `tar` binary required on remote)
4. Done — no `npm install`, no compiler needed, no `package.json` ceremony

Source files in the VS Code repo: `cli/src/util/prereqs.rs`, `cli/src/util/tar.rs`, `resources/server/bin/code-server-linux.sh`, `resources/server/bin/helpers/check-requirements-linux.sh`.

## Proposed approach for Orca

Update `config/scripts/build-relay.mjs` to additionally fetch node-pty's prebuilds (via `npm install node-pty` in a temp dir, then copy the right `prebuilds/<platform>/` subdir) and include them in `resources/relay/<platform>/node_modules/node-pty/`. Then in `src/main/ssh/ssh-relay-deploy.ts`:

- `installNativeDeps` becomes a no-op (or, more precisely, it just `chmod +x` the spawn-helper since SFTP doesn't preserve execute bits)
- Remove the SFTP package.json write and `npm install node-pty` exec
- Drop the post-install probe (the bundle is shipped, so it's there or our build broke)

Build-system changes:
- Add a step in CI that fetches node-pty prebuilds for each of our 4 platforms (linux-x64, linux-arm64, darwin-x64, darwin-arm64)
- Bake them into `resources/relay/<platform>/` alongside `relay.js` and the bundled node binary
- Update the upload size accounting (probably +1-2 MB per platform for node-pty native + JS)

## Benefits

- Eliminates the entire "node-pty install failed on remote" failure class
- No build tools required on remote (matches VS Code's UX)
- Faster first-connect (no npm registry round-trip)
- Deterministic — what shipped is exactly what's on the remote
- Fewer remote process spawns (no npm)

## Tradeoffs

- Larger relay tarball per platform
- Build pipeline must be updated to fetch prebuilds (similar to how `build-relay.mjs` already handles per-platform output dirs)
- We need to track node-pty version bumps in our build, not the remote's npm

## Pointers

- Reference comment in code: `src/main/ssh/ssh-relay-deploy.ts` near `installNativeDeps` (added in this PR)
- VS Code reference: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/cli/src/util/prereqs.rs

## Out of scope here

This is being deferred from PR #1679 (`Jinwoo-H/ssh-typing-lag`). That PR ships the runtime bypass-npm-init fix (hardcoded package.json) which is the minimum to unblock the immediate bug, but does not change the architectural model.

Made with [Orca](https://github.com/stablyai/orca) 🐋
payload.title: SSH relay: pre-bundle node-pty per platform (VS Code-style) to eliminate npm install on remote

payload.body:
### Operating system

Linux

### Orca version

v1.3.45

### Details

- Human description:

While updating Orca, the download process failed. After that when opening again Orca it crashed. I’ve used Claude to analyze the source code and provide more context on the failure below...

- Claude Code description:

**Operating system:** Linux (Pop!_OS)
**Orca version:** v1.3.45 packaged AppImage (reproducible against `main` source — `package.json` reports `1.3.46-rc.0`)

## Short summary

After an auto-update on Linux, the previous Orca process can survive past the new instance being spawned. While it lives, it holds the singleton lock — and every subsequent launch of `~/Applications/orca-linux.AppImage` fails the lock and crashes with `TypeError: Object has been destroyed` instead of focusing the existing window or exiting silently. Orca becomes unrelaunchable until the lingering process is killed and `~/.config/orca/SingletonLock` is removed.

The lock-survival is the trigger; the crash is a latent bug in the lock-failure path.

## What happened

Sequence (from `journalctl --user`):

1. `[autoUpdater]` downloaded v1.3.45. Differential download failed (`HttpError: 501` from Fastly/Varnish), fell back to full download which completed.
2. `[autoUpdater] Install on explicit quitAndInstall` → `[autoUpdater] Install: isSilent: false, isForceRunAfter: true` → `Executing: /home/doctor/Applications/orca-linux.AppImage`.
3. The original process **did not exit**. `ps aux` showed it still alive long after, holding the lock:
   ```
   ~/.config/orca/SingletonLock -> pop-os-105447
   ```
4. The auto-respawned instance, plus every subsequent manual launch, crashed with the same trace. No window ever appeared.

## Crash trace

```
/tmp/.mount_orca-XXXXXXX/resources/app.asar/out/main/index.js:43753
    throw error;
    ^

TypeError: Object has been destroyed
    at BrowserWindow.<anonymous> (/tmp/.mount_orca-XXXXXXX/resources/app.asar/out/main/index.js:46626:17)
    at BrowserWindow.emit (node:events:521:24)

Node.js v24.15.0
```

The `throw error` site at `:43753` is `installUncaughtPipeErrorGuard` in `src/main/startup/configure-process.ts:22-34`, which rethrows everything that isn't `EIO`/`EPIPE`. The actual fault originates in an unguarded `BrowserWindow` event handler at `:46626`.

## Reproduction

Reliable, in <30 seconds, on a working install:

1. Launch packaged Orca (process A) — it acquires the singleton lock.
2. While A is running, run `~/Applications/orca-linux.AppImage` again from a shell. (Or any second-instance trigger: double-click, `gtk-launch orca`, etc.)
3. The second instance prints the trace above and exits instead of routing focus back to A.

Confirmed locally — running the installed AppImage while the original process held the lock produced the trace verbatim.

## Root cause

In `src/main/index.ts:134-145`:

```ts
const hasSingleInstanceLock = is.dev ? true : acquireSingleInstanceLock(app, focusExistingWindow)
if (!hasSingleInstanceLock) {
  if (is.dev) {
    console.log(
      '[single-instance] Another Orca instance is already running against this userData path — focusing existing window.'
    )
  }
  app.quit()
}
```

There is no `return` after `app.quit()`. The comment a few lines below claims:

> // Why: when the lock is held by another process, we've already called
> // app.quit() above. Skip every remaining file-writing side effect so this
> // transient process never touches userData, and let handler registration
> // below happen — those handlers only fire after whenReady, which app.quit()
> // prevents from ever dispatching.

But `app.quit()` is asynchronous, and `app.whenReady().then(…)` is registered unconditionally at `src/main/index.ts:425`. On Linux this race can fire **before** the deferred quit takes effect. When it does:

- The bootstrap runs in full: `new Store()`, services, `openMainWindow()`.
- A `BrowserWindow` is created and listeners attached — `'closed'` (`src/main/index.ts:257`), `webContents.on('did-
payload.title: [Bug]:  Linux relaunch crash-loops with "Object has been destroyed" when singleton lock is held

payload.body:
### Details

Hi, I’m running into an issue with symlinks in a remote SSH workspace.

My remote workspace is opened at a path like:

```text
<remote-workspace-path>
```

Inside this workspace, I have a symlink pointing to another directory outside the workspace:

```text
<remote-workspace-path>/<symlink-name> -> <external-project-path>
```

For example, the actual layout is conceptually like this:

```text
/workspace/project-link -> /external-storage/project
```

When I try to open files through this symlink in Orca, the file fails to load.

## Environment

- Client OS: macOS
- Remote connection type: SSH
- Remote OS: Linux
- Remote workspace path: `<remote-workspace-path>`
- Symlink target path: `<external-project-path>`

## Reproduction

1. Connect to a remote server through Orca SSH.
2. Open a remote workspace, for example:

```text
<remote-workspace-path>
```

3. Create a symlink inside the workspace that points to a directory outside the workspace:

```bash
ln -s <external-project-path> <remote-workspace-path>/<symlink-name>
```

4. In Orca’s file explorer, open the symlink.
5. Try to open a file inside the symlinked directory.

## Actual behavior

Orca shows an error similar to:

```text
Error loading file: Error: Error invoking remote method 'fs:readFile': Error: Path outside authorized workspace: <external-project-path>
```

The symlink itself is visible in the file explorer, but files under the symlink cannot be opened because the resolved real path is outside the authorized workspace.

## Expected behavior

It would be helpful if Orca supported one of the following:

1. Allow opening symlinks whose link entry is inside the authorized workspace.
2. Provide a way to add extra trusted remote paths, for example:

```text
<remote-workspace-path>
<external-project-path>
```

3. Show a clearer message explaining that the symlink resolves outside the current workspace and that the target path needs to be added as another trusted workspace root.
4. Allow adding the resolved symlink target as an additional authorized workspace folder.

## Why this matters

On remote servers, HPC environments, and container-based development setups, it is common to keep code, datasets, checkpoints, model files, and project storage under different mount points.

A common layout looks like:

```text
/workspace
/external-storage
/shared-data
/model-storage
```

Developers often use symlinks to connect these directories into one project workspace. Currently, Orca can show the symlink, but cannot open files under it if the resolved path is outside the original workspace root.

## Notes

I understand that this may be a security boundary to prevent reading files outside the authorized workspace. If so, a trusted-path allowlist or “add symlink target as workspace root” option would make this workflow much easier while keeping the security model explicit.

Hi, I’m experiencing noticeable typing latency in Orca’s remote SSH terminal.

The same remote server feels responsive when I connect with native OpenSSH from my local terminal, but typing inside Orca’s remote SSH terminal has visible per-keystroke delay.

## Environment

- Remote glibc: 2.35
- Remote Node.js: v20.19.6
- Remote workspace path: `<remote-workspace-path>`
- Orca remote relay path: `<orca-remote-relay-path>`

## Reproduction

1. Connect to a remote server through Orca SSH.
2. Open a remote terminal.
3. Run:

```bash
cat >/dev/null
```

4. Type several characters quickly, for example:

```text
adadadad
```

The characters appear with visible delay.

For comparison, if I connect to the same server using native OpenSSH from my local terminal, typing is much smoother.

## What I checked

I tested with a clean bash environment:

```bash
env -i HOME="$HOME" TERM=xterm-256color PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin bash --noprofile --norc
```

The typing delay still happens, so it does not seem to be caused by my shell config, conda initialization, prompt rendering, git prompt, or startup files.

The remote machine is almost idle:

```text
CPU idle: about 99.8%
Orca relay node process: about 0.3% CPU
Memory: sufficient
```

The remote relay process is running:

```text
node relay.js --detached --grace-time 300 --sock-path <relay-socket-path>
node relay.js --connect --sock-path <relay-socket-path>
```

`node-pty` also works correctly on the remote host. From the Orca remote relay directory, this test succeeds:

```bash
node - <<'NODE'
const pty = require('node-pty');
console.log('REQUIRE_NODE_PTY_OK');
const p = pty.spawn('/bin/bash', ['-lc', 'echo NODE_PTY_SPAWN_OK && tty'], {
  name: 'xterm-256color',
  cols: 80,
  rows: 24,
  cwd: process.env.HOME,
  env: process.env
});
p.onData(d => process.stdout.write(d));
p.onExit(e => process.exit(e.exitCode || 0));
NODE
```

Output:

```text
REQUIRE_NODE_PTY_OK
NODE_PTY_SPAWN_OK
/dev/pts/<n>
```

The relay log shows:

```text
ORCA-RELAY v0.1.0 READY
[relay] File watcher not available, fs.changed events disabled
```

## DevTools logs

I noticed this in DevTools during SSH restore / terminal reconnect:

```text
[terminals-hydration] remoteSessionIdsByTabId: {"<tab-id>":"<pty-id>"}

[filesystem-watch] failed to watch worktree
Error invoking remote method 'fs:watchWorktree': Error: Multiplexer disposed

[ssh-restore] Polled state for <ssh-connection-id>: status=connected

[reconnect-terminals] worktree=<worktree-id>::<remote-workspace-path> connectionId=<ssh-connection-id> sshStatus=connected supportsDeferredReattach=true

[pty-connection] SSH tab=<tab-id> connectionId=<ssh-connection-id> pendingSessionId=<pty-id> isDeferredTarget=false

[pty-connection] Reattach result for tab=<tab-id>:
{sessionExpired: undefined, replay: true}
```

The terminal session seems to reattach successfully, but the filesystem watcher reports `Multiplexer disposed`.

## Expected behavior

Typing in Orca’s remote SSH terminal should feel close to native OpenSSH when the remote host and relay are idle.

## Actual behavior

Typing in Orca’s remote SSH terminal has visible per-keystroke latency, while native OpenSSH to the same server is responsive.

## Notes

This does not seem to be caused by remote CPU load, memory pressure, missing `node-pty`, shell configuration, conda initialization, or prompt rendering.

Could this be related to Orca’s remote terminal input path, relay IPC, reconnect/reattach logic, or the filesystem watcher / multiplexer state?

## Summary

Whenever the remote host I'm SSH'd into reboots, **the entire Orca app exits to the desktop** — not just the affected workspace tab. Reproducible 100% of the time across multiple distinct remote hosts.

## Repro

1. SSH-connect Orca to a remote workspace (any of my Linux LXCs — repro'd on three different ones over the last few weeks)
2. From a separate shell, reboot the remote host (e.g. `sudo reboot` over a different SSH session, or `pct reboot <vmid>` from the Proxmox host)
3. Within seconds of the SSH transport going dead, the Orca app quits

## Expected behavior

The affected SSH workspace should disconnect and show a "remote unreachable, retrying…" state (similar to VS Code Remote-SSH on connection loss). Other workspaces / local windows / the dashboard should remain intact. The app process should not exit.

## Actual behavior

The whole app process exits. No window remains. Re-opening Orca from the dock starts it fresh.

## Diagnostics

- **No macOS crash dialog** — the app exits silently
- **No `Orca-*.crash` in `~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/`**
- **No fault-level entries in the unified log** (`log show --predicate 'process == \"Orca\"' --last 1h | grep -iE 'fault|crash|abort|terminate|signal'` returns nothing)

This pattern (clean exit, no SIGSEGV) suggests the main process is calling `app.quit()` (or letting the last window close trigger quit) in response to the relay/IPC channel for the dead SSH workspace throwing — instead of catching the error and scoping it to that workspace.

## Hypothesis

An unhandled rejection from the relay-side IPC handler when the SSH socket dies is propagating to the main process top-level error handler, which then exits the app. Looking at this from the outside, scoping the error to the specific workspace's lifecycle (and showing a reconnect UI) would match the pattern in #985.

## Environment

- **Orca**: 1.3.45 (Apple Silicon)
- **macOS**: 26.3.1 (arm64)
- **Remotes**: Debian 13 trixie LXCs, SSH on default port, key-based auth
- **Workspace path**: absolute paths (since the `~/`-as-workspace bug from issue #326 / #911 era)

## Related

- #985 — feature request to persist/restore SSH connections across **app** restarts. If the app stops *needing* to restart on remote reboot, that becomes much less urgent.
- #1158 — silent data loss when workspace session hydration fails (different code path but same general theme of remote-state failures bubbling up too far).

## Cooperation

Happy to attach more diagnostics if there's a debug log mode I should enable before triggering a repro.

Made with [Orca](https://github.com/stablyai/orca) 🐋

payload.author: braianj
payload.body:
### Problem or use case

## Summary

Allow users to group multiple repositories together in Orca and have Orca prepare a local working environment with all of them, similar to how Workspaces worked in VS Code.

## Use case

This would be especially helpful when working on features that require changes across multiple repositories. Instead of manually cloning each repo, creating branches one by one, and keeping them organized separately, Orca could automate the setup and keep the repositories grouped under the same package.

Today, when a feature spans multiple repos, the user has to:

- Manually clone each repository.
- Create or check out the working branch in each one.
- Track which folders belong to the same logical change.
- Re-do this setup every time, on every machine.

There is no first-class concept in Orca for "this set of repos that I work on together as a unit".

### Proposed solution

Add a new concept called **Packages** — a named group of repositories that Orca clones, organizes, and branches together as a single working unit.

> Since Orca already has the concept of Workspaces, this new feature is called **Packages** to avoid confusion.

## Proposed behavior

1. The user can create a new group of repositories (a Package).
2. The user can select multiple repositories to include in that group.
3. Orca clones each selected repository.
4. Orca creates a dedicated folder inside the Orca directory for that group.
5. Inside that folder, Orca places all selected repositories.
6. Orca creates or checks out a branch for each selected repository.
7. The user can then work across all repositories as part of the same grouped context.

## Example folder structure

```
Orca/
  Packages/
    my-package/
      repo-a/
      repo-b/
      repo-c/
```

## Expected outcome

A user should be able to:

- Create a Package.
- Select multiple repositories.
- Have Orca automatically clone them into a dedicated folder.
- Have Orca create or check out the required branch for each repository.
- Work across all repositories as part of the same grouped context (open files, run agents, search) without manual setup.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] User can create, rename, and delete a Package.
- [ ] User can select N repositories (from accessible orgs/accounts) to include in a Package.
- [ ] User can specify (or accept a default of) the branch name to create / check out for each repository in the Package.
- [ ] On creation, Orca clones each selected repository into `Orca/Packages/<package-name>/<repo>/`.
- [ ] On creation, Orca creates the branch in each repo if it doesn't exist, or checks it out if it does.
- [ ] User can re-open a Package later without re-cloning (Orca detects existing local copies).
- [ ] User can add or remove repositories from an existing Package.
- [ ] Errors per-repo (auth failure, missing branch, dirty working tree) are surfaced clearly without aborting the whole Package setup.

### Alternatives or additional context

## Alternatives considered

1. **Reuse the Workspaces concept.** Could overload "Workspace" to mean a multi-repo group, but Workspaces already has a meaning in Orca / VS Code — overloading it would be confusing. A new name (Packages) keeps the mental model clean.
2. **Manual scripts per developer.** Each user writes a shell script to clone + branch a set of repos. Works today, but is not shareable and not first-class in Orca's UI.
3. **Submodules / monorepo conversion.** Heavy, invasive, and not always feasible across organizations or teams.

## Additional context

- A Package definition (name, list of repos, default branch name) could be exported / imported as a small JSON or YAML file, making it easy for teams to share standard Package setups.
- Could later support "open this Package" deep links and per-Package agent contexts (so an agent run knows about all repos in the Package).
- Each repository inside a Package should still behave like a normal Orca repo (commits, PRs, agents) — Packages are a groupin
payload.title: [Feature]: Add support for grouping multiple repositories into Packages

What happened?
A toast notification appears in the top-right corner:

Anything else that might help:

When Orca resolves the canonical path through this pointer via `fs:readDir`, it crosses outside the worktree root directory boundary — triggering the "Access denied" check. payload.body:
## Description

When opening a git worktree in Orca IDE, the file tree fails to load with the following error toast:

> Could not load files for this worktree: Error invoking remote method 'fs:readDir': Error: Access denied: path resolves outside allowed directories. If this blocks a legitimate workflow, please file a GitHub issue.

## Environment

- Orca IDE (latest)
- Claude Code v2.1.89
- macOS

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have a primary git repository open in Orca (e.g. \`~/Desktop/work/my-repo\`)
2. Create a git worktree inside the project: \`git worktree add .worktrees/my-branch feat/my-branch\`
3. Open the worktree in Orca via the WORKSPACES panel
4. Observe the error toast in the top-right corner

## Expected Behavior

The file tree for the worktree loads normally.

## Actual Behavior

The error toast appears and the file tree is empty. The worktree appears in the WORKSPACES list but its files cannot be browsed.

## Root Cause Analysis

In a git worktree, the \`.git\` entry is a **file** (not a directory) that contains a pointer to the main repo's \`.git/worktrees/<name>/\` directory. When Orca calls \`fs:readDir\` and resolves the canonical path via this pointer, the resolved path falls outside the worktree's root directory — triggering the "Access denied: path resolves outside allowed directories" security check.

This is a known behavior of git worktrees and needs to be handled specially when resolving allowed directory boundaries.
payload.title: Cannot load files for git worktree: fs:readDir Access denied outside allowed directories

payload.body:
## Issue: TUI Rendering Artifacts — Black Boxes on Scroll (Linux)

### Environment
- **OS:** Ubuntu 26.04 (Resolute Raccoon)
- **Orca Version:** 50.1.2
- **Display Server:** Wayland
- **GPU:** Intel Corporation Arrow Lake-P [Arc Pro 130T/140T]

### Description
When using Orca's integrated terminal with TUI applications (e.g., `pi`, `htop`, `nvim`), the screen develops black rectangular artifacts while scrolling. Individual letters/glyphs become obscured by these black boxes, making the interface unusable over time.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Open Orca terminal
2. Launch any TUI application with scrollable content (e.g., `pi` agent, `htop`, file manager)
3. Scroll up/down using mouse or keyboard
4. Observe black boxes appearing over characters

### Expected Behavior
Clean scroll with no visual artifacts; previous screen buffer properly cleared.

### Actual Behavior
Black rectangular artifacts accumulate on scroll. Characters become unreadable. Issue compounds with continued scrolling.

### Key Findings

#### Shortcut Behavior (Session-Dependent)
| Location | Ctrl+Shift+R | Effect |
|----------|--------------|--------|
| Settings panel | Works | Refreshes/reloads as expected |
| Terminal/TUI view | **Intermittent** | Sometimes captured by terminal, sometimes works globally |

**Note:** After Orca restart, `Ctrl+Shift+R` now works in terminal views. The shortcut interception appears to be **session-specific** rather than consistent behavior.

#### Agent-Specific Behavior
- **Pi, Claude Code, Codex:** Functional after hard refresh
- **OpenCode:** **Crashes/freezes on hard refresh** — becomes unresponsive (no scroll, no input)

#### Attempted Fixes
- [x] Hard refresh (`Ctrl+Shift+R`) — Works after restart, but breaks OpenCode specifically
- [x] Window resize — No effect
- [x] Orca restart — Resolves shortcut issues, recreates OpenCode freeze on refresh

#### Working Solution
**Disabling GPU acceleration** (`Settings → Appearance → GPU Acceleration → OFF`) immediately resolves all rendering artifacts.

### Impact
- **Severity:** High (renders TUI applications unusable)
- **Workaround:** Yes (disable GPU acceleration)
- **Regression:** Unknown if this breaks other features

### Related
Possibly related to GPU driver + Wayland interaction. Intel Arc GPUs on Wayland may have different buffer clearing behavior than NVIDIA/AMD.

### Attachments
- [ ] Screenshot of black box artifacts (if reproducible)
- [ ] Output of `orca --version`
- [ ] GPU info: `lspci | grep -i vga` or `nvidia-smi` / `radeontop`

payload.author: Jinwoo-H
payload.body:
## Background

PR #1539 pinned `zod` to `~4.3.6` to unblock mobile + CLI users after #1526's opportunistic bump to `4.4.3` silently broke a large family of RPC param schemas. This issue tracks the proper fix so we can move zod forward again.

## The bug

zod 4.4 changed how `.transform(...).pipe(z.X().optional())` interacts with `z.object` field validation. When such a field's key is **omitted** from the parsed object, zod 4.4 reports:

> Invalid input: expected nonoptional, received undefined

…instead of treating the missing key as the inner schema's `.optional()` case. The dispatcher rejects the call with `invalid_argument` before the handler runs.

Reduced repro:

```ts
import { z } from 'zod' // 4.4.x
const OptionalFiniteNumber = z.unknown()
  .transform((v) => (typeof v === 'number' && Number.isFinite(v) ? v : undefined))
  .pipe(z.number().optional())

z.object({ limit: OptionalFiniteNumber }).safeParse({})
// 4.3.6: { success: true, data: {} }
// 4.4.3: { success: false, error: 'expected nonoptional, received undefined' }
```

The fix is to put `.optional()` **outside** the pipe and make the piped target a union with `undefined`:

```ts
const OptionalFiniteNumber = z.unknown()
  .transform((v) => (typeof v === 'number' && Number.isFinite(v) ? v : undefined))
  .pipe(z.union([z.number(), z.undefined()]))
  .optional()
```

## Affected sites (13 total)

`src/main/runtime/rpc/schemas.ts` — 5 helpers used widely:
- [ ] `OptionalFiniteNumber`
- [ ] `OptionalPositiveInt`
- [ ] `OptionalString`
- [ ] `OptionalPlainString`
- [ ] `OptionalBoolean`

Local copies of the same idiom in method files:
- [ ] `src/main/runtime/rpc/methods/terminal.ts` — `TerminalSplit.direction`
- [ ] `src/main/runtime/rpc/methods/worktree.ts` — `WorktreeCreate.setupDecision`
- [ ] `src/main/runtime/rpc/methods/browser-schemas.ts` — `Scroll.amount`, `Screenshot.format`, `TabSwitch.index`, `TabClose.index`, `Wait.timeout`, `InterceptEnable.patterns`

## Real-user impact (when zod is bumped past 4.3.x without the fix)

- mobile `worktree.ps` → home page shows '0 worktrees', host detail screen never loads
- `worktree.list` / `worktree.set` / `worktree.create` reject callers omitting any optional field
- `terminal.split` (omit direction), `terminal.create` (omit title etc.)
- `browser screenshot` / `scroll` / `wait` / `tab switch` / `tab close` / `intercept enable` whenever an optional field is left off

## Why this shipped to main without anyone noticing

The bug is invisible to:
- TypeScript (the schemas still type-check; the breakage is runtime-only)
- Existing unit tests (the RPC test suite doesn't exercise the dispatcher with payloads that omit optional fields — it always passes well-formed objects)
- Local desktop dev (Electron CLI passes params explicitly via commander)

It only fires on the mobile/external RPC path where callers naturally omit fields they don't need.

## Suggested fix

1. Update the 5 schema helpers in `schemas.ts` (one-line change each — move `.optional()` out of the pipe and union the inner schema with `z.undefined()`).
2. Apply the same pattern to the 8 inline copies in method files.
3. Add a dispatcher-level test that walks every registered RPC method and asserts `safeParse({})` doesn't reject with `expected nonoptional` for fields that shouldn't be required. This guards against future regressions.
4. Bump zod back to latest 4.x.

## References

- PR #1539 — the temporary pin
- PR #1526 — original opportunistic bump that introduced the regression
- PR #1532 — the mobile-fit-hold work that surfaced this during manual testing

Made with [Orca](https://github.com/stablyai/orca) 🐋
payload.title: zod: schemas using `.pipe(z.X().optional())` break on missing keys in zod 4.4+

payload.author: maco222
payload.body:
### Problem or use case

Multi-pane workflows where content types are pinned to specific regions of the layout — e.g. editor in top-left, terminals in bottom-left, browser tabs in a right-side group. Today this works manually if a user does drag-and-drop on first session and lets the layout persist. But it falls apart for:

1. **`orca.yaml scripts.setup`** — setup scripts run before the user has a chance to arrange anything; whatever they spawn lands in whichever pane is "active" at start-up.
2. **CLI automation** — `orca terminal split --direction vertical --command "..."` splits the *active* terminal. There is no `--group` or `--position` flag, so a dashboard launcher can't say "open this in bottom-left" deterministically.
3. **`orca tab create --url`** for browser tabs has the same gap — no way to say "this tab goes into the right-side group".
4. **Multi-developer repos** — each dev currently re-arranges the layout once on their box. There's no committed-to-repo answer for "this is the canonical layout for our project".

Concrete shape (our monorepo):

- top-left: editor / files
- bottom-left: terminals (one running our TUI dashboard, others ad-hoc shells)
- right: browser tabs (frontend SPA, Mailpit, Horizon, etc.)

We can build this manually once. We can't reproduce it from `orca.yaml` or CLI, and that's the friction.

### Proposed solution

Two complementary surfaces:

**1. Declarative groups + rules in `orca.yaml`:**

```yaml
layout:
  groups:
    editor:   { position: left-top,    kind: editor }
    terminal: { position: left-bottom, kind: terminal }
    browser:  { position: right,       kind: browser }
  rules:
    new-editor-tab:  editor
    new-terminal:    terminal
    new-browser-tab: browser
```

`groups` defines regions and what kind of content lives there. `rules` maps "what just got created" → "which group". Existing CLI calls without an explicit `--group` consult the rule table.

**2. CLI overrides for explicit placement:**

```
orca terminal create --group terminal --command "make dashboard"
orca tab create --url http://localhost:3000 --group browser
orca editor open --group editor src/main.rs
```

`--group` resolves to the declared group from `orca.yaml`; without an `orca.yaml` declaration, an inline `--position <left-top|...>` fallback is enough for ad-hoc use.

For first-time worktree provisioning, the layout config is materialized into the same persisted layout state that drag-and-drop would have produced — so reloads and subsequent sessions don't re-run the rule engine, they just hit the persisted shape.

### Alternatives or additional context

- **Manual layout + persistence** (current state) — works for a single dev who arranged their workspace once. Fails for setup scripts, multi-dev repos, and `orca worktree create` for fresh issues.
- **PR #1396 + #1397 (tab profile lifecycle)** got CLI to express *which session profile* a tab uses. The natural next axis is *which group* a tab/terminal lives in. Same shape, different field on the workspace model.
- **Prior art:** VS Code's `contributes.views.containers` lets extensions declare where their views live; Hyprland/i3/sway have window rules; tmux has named windows + targets. The pattern is well-trodden.

For TUI dashboard cockpits + SPA frontend + agent terminals all in one Orca workspace, this is the missing primitive that turns ad-hoc CLI scripting into a committed-to-repo workflow contract. #1498 would be a building block — once a tab can be focused, the next thing is "which group does it focus into".
payload.title: [Feature]: Declarative layout rules — pin content types to specific groups/regions

payload.author: maco222
payload.body:
### Problem or use case

Building a TUI dashboard that drives Orca's browser via CLI hits a wall: no verb both activates a tab AND surfaces the browser pane.

- `orca tab switch --page <id>` — flips `activeWebContentsId` in the bridge but never fires a renderer focus event. If the user is on terminal/editor, the pane stays put; the switch is invisible.
- `orca browser.goto --url <url>` — fires `notifyRendererNavigation` (load-indicator flickers on the target tab) but doesn't promote the pane either.
- `orca tab create --url <url>` — does surface the pane, but mints a new tab every call. Dedupe via close-then-create reshuffles the tab strip on every click — also bad UX.

Concrete use case: a dashboard cockpit (Textual TUI for our monorepo's dev stack) that opens registered service URLs (Mailpit, Horizon, Swagger, etc.). With ~10 services and frequent context switches, "open or focus existing" is the natural verb. There's no way to express it without either ghost-switching (tab moves, pane doesn't) or tab-strip shuffling (close + create).

### Proposed solution

A CLI verb or flag that does the analogue of #1451's `activateTabAndFocusPane`, for browser:

```
orca tab focus --page <id> [--worktree <selector>]
# or:
orca tab switch --page <id> --focus
```

Implementation hint from #1451: pattern is `setActiveTab(tabId)` + dispatch `FOCUS_<TYPE>_PANE_EVENT` on `requestAnimationFrame`. Same pattern, different pane type — either parameterize the existing helper, or add a sibling `FOCUS_BROWSER_PANE_EVENT`.

### Alternatives or additional context

Tried in my dashboard before reverting:

1. `tab switch` alone → "switched" toast lies; pane stays.
2. `tab switch` + `goto <existing-url>` → load-indicator flickers on the tab (proof goto fires the right hook for *navigation*, not pane focus); pane stays.
3. `tab close existing` + `tab create new` → works mechanically but the tab strip reshuffles on every Enter — a closed tab at index 2 reappears at index N.

Ended up reverting to `tab create` for "new tab" hotkey and `goto` for navigation, accepting that pane surfaces only if the user was already on it.

**Reproduction:**

```sh
# 1. Open Orca with a repo
# 2. orca tab create --url http://example.com --worktree path:<repo>
# 3. orca tab create --url http://example.org --worktree path:<repo>
# 4. Click into a terminal pane (renderer's active pane type → terminal)
# 5. orca tab switch --index 0 --worktree path:<repo> --json   # ok=true, but pane doesn't surface
```

Reference: bridge `tabSwitch` (visible in packaged `app.asar`) ends with `this.activeWebContentsId = wcId` + `activeWebContentsPerWorktree.set(...)` and returns — no renderer notification path.

Tested on `1.3.35-rc.4` and `1.3.36`.
payload.title: [Feature]: Surface browser pane on tab activation (analogue of #1451 for terminal panes)

### Problem or use case

The Source Control panel already supports staging, committing, and pushing, but writing the commit message itself is still 100% manual. After a long session — especially one driven by AI agents inside worktrees — users spend extra time eyeballing the diff just to summarize what changed. It is a small but constant friction point that breaks the "review → commit → push without leaving Orca" flow that the panel is designed for.

### Proposed solution

Add an opt-in **"Generate with AI"** action inside the commit area of the Source Control panel that drafts a commit message from the currently staged changes.

UX outline:

- A button appears next to the commit message textarea, but **only after the user opts in** (no surprise network or agent calls).
- Pressing it inspects the staged diff of the active worktree and fills the textarea with a draft message; the user is always in control of editing or discarding it.
- The button is enabled only when there are staged changes and the textarea is empty, so it never silently overwrites something the user has already typed.
- Works the same on local worktrees and on **SSH-connected** worktrees, so the experience is identical regardless of where the repo lives.

Configuration lives under **Settings → AI Commit Messages**:

- Choose which AI agent to use (extensible — ships with the agents already supported by Orca).
- Pick a model and an effort/quality level per agent.
- Optional custom prompt suffix to enforce repo conventions (Conventional Commits, ticket prefixes, language, etc.).
- Sensible low-cost defaults so users can try it immediately without tuning anything.

### Alternatives or additional context

- Reference: VSCode's "Generate Commit Message with Copilot" button in the SCM input box.
- Builds on top of the commit flow already shipped via #1170 / #1211 / #1373 — this issue covers only the **AI draft** step; the rest of the commit/push pipeline is unchanged.
- Out of scope (possible follow-ups): auto-committing without confirmation, multi-commit splitting, PR description generation.
payload.title: [Feature]: AI-generated commit messages from staged changes in the Source Control panel

payload.author: braianj
payload.body:
### Problem or use case

## Summary

Add a chat-style, user-friendly view for inspecting agent runs (e.g. Claude and other agents) inside Orca, while keeping full parity with the native Claude CLI capabilities.

## Problem / Motivation

Today, when an agent like Claude runs inside Orca, the output is rendered in a format that:

- Is dense and log-like, hard to scan visually.
- Mixes user prompts, agent reasoning, tool calls, tool results, and final answers in a way that breaks the natural flow of a conversation.
- Makes it difficult to follow long, multi-step agent runs (debugging, demos, support, stakeholder reviews).
- Underuses formatting that Claude already produces (Markdown, code blocks, tables, citations).

This affects multiple personas:

- **Developers** debugging agent behavior need to follow turns clearly.
- **PMs / non-technical users** reviewing runs need a readable artifact.
- **Support / QA** need to share or replay a run without parsing raw logs.

## User Stories

- As a **developer**, I want to skim an agent run in chat format so I can quickly identify where it went off track, without losing access to raw events.
- As a **PM**, I want to share a clean, readable transcript of an agent run with stakeholders.
- As a **power user**, I want to toggle back to the raw CLI view at any time so I do not lose any functionality I rely on today.
- As a **support engineer**, I want to expand only the failing tool call instead of scrolling through the whole log.

### Proposed solution

Introduce a **chat-style renderer** for agent runs as the default view, with a toggle to fall back to the raw/native CLI view.

## Core elements

1. **Conversation timeline**
   - Distinct bubbles/sections for: `user`, `assistant`, `tool_call`, `tool_result`, `system`.
   - Avatars/labels per role (e.g. "You", "Claude", tool name).
   - Timestamps and run duration per turn.

2. **Smarter text rendering**
   - Full Markdown rendering (headings, lists, bold, links).
   - Syntax-highlighted code blocks with copy button.
   - Collapsible sections for long outputs (tool results, large diffs, JSON payloads).
   - Pretty-printed JSON / YAML / diff blocks.
   - Inline citations and file links rendered as clickable references.

3. **Tool-call visibility**
   - Tool call shown as a compact card: tool name, arguments (collapsed by default), result (collapsed by default).
   - Status indicator (running / success / error).
   - "Show raw" toggle per tool call.

4. **Native Claude CLI parity (non-negotiable)**
   - All current CLI capabilities remain available: streaming output, interrupts, slash commands, tool approvals, exit codes, transcripts, hooks.
   - Toggle: `Chat view` ⇄ `Raw CLI view`.
   - Keyboard shortcuts and pipeable stdout/stderr for scripts must keep working.
   - The chat view is a presentation layer over the existing event stream — it must not drop, reorder, or summarize events.

5. **Navigation & sharing**
   - Jump to: latest message, errors, tool calls.
   - Copy-as-Markdown for any turn or the full run.
   - Shareable permalink to a specific run / turn.

## UX Concept (rough mockup)

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Run #482  ·  Claude Sonnet  ·  2m 14s   [Chat | Raw]   │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  🧑 You · 10:02                                          │
│  Refactor auth.ts to use the new token service.         │
│                                                          │
│  🤖 Claude · 10:02                                       │
│  I'll start by reading the current implementation.       │
│                                                          │
│  🛠  read_file  · auth.ts                ▸ expand        │
│  ✅  success · 312 lines                                  │
│                                                          │
│  🤖 Claude · 10:03                                       │
│  Here's the proposed change (diff with syntax highlight) │
│
payload.title: [Feature]: Chat-style UI for viewing agent runs (Claude, etc.) with smarter text rendering, preserving CLI parity

payload.author: perebusquets
payload.body:
### Problem or use case

### Problem Description
When using WSL2 as the primary development environment, Orca resolves external tools (GitHub CLI, Opencode, Claude, etc.) against the Windows host rather than the WSL2 VM. Because my development toolchain is installed inside the WSL environment and not on the Windows host, Orca fails to locate these tools.

### Environment & Context
- Primary OS: Windows 11 (host)
- Dev Environment: WSL2 (primary workspace)
- Tool Installation: All dev tools (GH CLI, Opencode, Claude, etc.) are installed inside the WSL2 VM, not on Windows

### Impact
This behavior breaks the core WSL2 workflow:
- WSL2 is designed to isolate project environments across different VMs/distros.
- Requiring tools to be installed on the Windows host forces duplicated setup and eliminates environment isolation.
- It becomes impossible to use project-specific tool versions or switch between WSL distros cleanly.

### Expected Behavior
When the workspace is running inside WSL2, Orca should resolve external tools from the WSL2 environment (i.e., the VM's PATH) rather than the Windows host.

### Proposed solution

1. WSL-aware Startup Flow
   On launch, Orca should detect the presence of WSL and prompt the user with:
   - A list of available WSL distributions/machines.
   - An option to run at the Windows host level.
   
   The user selects their target environment once per window
2. Transparent WSL Command Wrapping
   If a WSL environment is selected, Orca should transparently prefix all external system calls with wsl.exe -d <DistroName> (or the equivalent native WSL Windows command). This ensures tooling (GitHub CLI, Opencode, Claude Code, etc.) is resolved against the WSL VM's PATH and filesystem, not the host.
3. Multi-Window / Multi-Project Support
   Because Orca supports multiple windows, each window should independently remember its chosen environment. This enables a workflow where:
   - Window A targets WSL: Ubuntu for Project 1.
   - Window B targets WSL: Debian for Project 2.
   - Window C runs at the Windows host level for native tooling.

### Alternatives or additional context

_No response_
payload.title: [Feature]: External tools (GH CLI, Claude, Opencode) are resolved on Windows host instead of inside the WSL VM

payload.author: nengqi
payload.body:
## Problem or use case

Follow-up to #800 (which I filed) and #521. v1.3.32 added an env-var bridge in `src/main/rate-limits/claude-fetcher.ts` (`ensureProxyFromEnv`) that reads `HTTPS_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY/ALL_PROXY` and feeds them into `session.defaultSession.setProxy`. Thanks for landing that — but for users in regions where `api.anthropic.com` requires a proxy and who launch Orca by **double-clicking the dock/Launchpad icon** (the common case on macOS), this fix has zero effect.

**Why**: macOS GUI apps are launched by `launchd`, which does **not** inherit the user's terminal shell env. So even if `~/.zshrc` defines `PROXY_ADDR=127.0.0.1:7890` and a `proxy` alias, the Orca main process boots with no `*PROXY*` env var, and the `ensureProxyFromEnv` short-circuit at `claude-fetcher.ts:47` (`if (!proxyUrl) return`) skips `setProxy` entirely.

**Empirical evidence** on my machine (Orca v1.3.32, macOS Darwin 25, dock-launched):

```
$ ps eww $(pgrep -f '/Applications/Orca.app/Contents/MacOS/Orca') \
    | tr ' ' '\n' | grep -i proxy
(no output — main process has zero proxy env vars)

$ scutil --proxy
  HTTPEnable  : 0
  HTTPSEnable : 0
  SOCKSEnable : 0
  (system proxy is also off, so the OS-proxy fallback won't fire either)

$ lsof -nP -iTCP -p <orca-network-helper-pid> | grep -v LISTEN
Orca\ Helper ... TCP 10.x:56429 -> 30.100.0.221:443 (ESTABLISHED)
Orca\ Helper ... TCP 10.x:56993 -> 30.100.0.235:443 (ESTABLISHED)

$ dig +short onorca.dev
216.150.1.1
30.100.0.221
```

So Orca is connecting **directly** to `onorca.dev` with no proxy involvement. The same path will be taken for `api.anthropic.com` once OAuth usage polling is triggered — which in my region is GFW-blocked at the TLS handshake.

The current env-var path only works if the user (a) knows to launch Orca from a terminal that has `proxy` exported, or (b) runs `launchctl setenv HTTPS_PROXY ...` globally. Neither is discoverable, and (b) leaks the proxy to every other GUI app on the system.

## Proposed solution

Add a first-class **HTTP proxy field in Settings** (as originally requested in #521), persisted to user prefs and applied at app start before any `net.fetch`. Specifically:

1. **New Settings UI**: text field for proxy URL (e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:7890`), plus optional bypass list. Empty = use OS proxy / env vars (current default behavior preserved).
2. **Apply at boot**: in `main`, call `session.defaultSession.setProxy({ proxyRules })` with the configured value before any `net.fetch` is issued — covers updater (`updater-changelog`, `updater-nudge`, `updater-prerelease-feed`), Claude/Gemini/OpenCode usage fetchers, feedback IPC, etc.
3. **Inject the same proxy as env vars into spawned PTY children**: the bundled `claude` CLI runs as a PTY child of Orca's main process and currently inherits the GUI's empty proxy env. This means even users with working terminal-side proxy wrappers (e.g. a shell function that injects `HTTPS_PROXY` before `claude`) get unproxied `claude` calls when they run it from inside Orca. (This sub-item could reasonably be split into a separate issue if preferred.)

Suggested precedence: explicit Settings value > OS system proxy > env vars > DIRECT. (Today the code does OS > env > DIRECT, which is fine — just slot Settings on top.)

## Alternatives or additional context

- Workaround today: `launchctl setenv HTTPS_PROXY http://127.0.0.1:7890` before launching Orca. Works, but pollutes every GUI app on the system.
- Workaround #2: launch Orca from a terminal where the proxy env is already exported (`open -a Orca`). Works, but defeats the purpose of a GUI app.
- Related: #521 (closed, `collecting upvote`), #800 (closed, partially addressed by env-var bridge in v1.3.32).
- Code reference: `src/main/rate-limits/claude-fetcher.ts:15-57` — the comment at line 17-25 already acknowledges users in this exact situation, the fix just doesn't cover the GUI-launch case.
payload.title: [Feature]: Settings UI for HTTP proxy — env-var bridge in v1.3.32 doesn't cover GUI-launched app

### Is there an existing issue for this?

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

With the recent and awesome addition of Linear, Orca is proving to be a fantastic unified workspace. However, many enterprise and corporate environments rely heavily on the Microsoft ecosystem, specifically Azure DevOps. 

Currently, developers using Azure DevOps cannot track their work items (Bugs, Tasks, User Stories) or manage their Pull Requests directly from within Orca's UI, breaking the flow and forcing them to constantly context-switch to the browser.

### Describe the solution you'd like

I would love to see Azure DevOps added as a "Task Source" and "Source Control Provider", alongside GitHub and Linear. 

The ideal integration would allow users to:
1. **Azure Boards:** View, search, and manage Work Items assigned to them (Bugs, Tasks, etc.) from the Tasks pane.
2. **Azure Repos:** See Pull Requests, check CI pipeline status, and manage PR reviews/comments directly from Orca, just like the current GitHub integration.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

* Continuing to use the web browser for all Azure DevOps related tasks, which defeats the purpose of having a unified developer workspace.
* Using third-party syncing tools to mirror Azure DevOps work items into GitHub Issues, which is messy and prone to sync errors.

### Additional context

payload.author: leynier
payload.body:
### Problem or use case

Orca currently has a fixed layout: the worktree/repo manager lives on the **left** sidebar and the activity panel (Explorer, Search, Source Control, Checks, Ports) lives on the **right** sidebar. There is no way for the user to invert this arrangement.

Different users have different ergonomic preferences:

- Some come from VSCode/Cursor where the file explorer is traditionally on the **left**, and feel disoriented having it on the right in Orca.
- Left-handed users, or users with their mouse on the left, often prefer the navigation/management surface (worktrees) on the side closer to their dominant hand.
- Multi-monitor setups: depending on which screen Orca lives on and where the secondary monitor is, swapping sides reduces eye/cursor travel.
- Users who keep a chat/AI panel docked on a specific edge of their monitor benefit from being able to push Orca's "primary" sidebar to the opposite side.

Today the only workaround is "get used to it", which is a poor experience for a tool meant to be lived in all day.

### Proposed solution

Add a setting (e.g. `Swap sidebar sides` under **Settings → Appearance** or similar) that, when enabled, renders:

- The **worktrees/repos sidebar** on the right side of the window.
- The **activity panel** (Explorer, Search, Source Control, Checks, Ports) on the left side of the window.

The setting should be persisted alongside the rest of the layout preferences. Behaviour notes:

- Each sidebar keeps its own width independently — the width should travel with the *component*, not with the position, so toggling the setting doesn't reset the user's carefully resized panels.
- Resize handles, borders, the activity bar's `side` strip, and the toggle icons (`PanelLeft` / `PanelRight`) must mirror correctly when swapped.
- Toggle shortcuts (`⌘B` / `⌘L`) continue to toggle the same logical sidebar; only their tooltip labels ("Toggle left/right sidebar") update to reflect the current physical side.
- The collapsed-sidebar header behaviour in the top bar should keep working in either configuration.

### Alternatives or additional context

- **Full panel-level customization** (à la VSCode's "Move View" where any individual panel can be dragged to either sidebar or to the bottom) would be more flexible, but is a much larger refactor and is probably overkill for the most common request, which is simply *"flip the two sides"*.
- A quick survey of similar tools: VSCode, JetBrains IDEs, and Zed all let users move sidebars between left and right. Orca is currently the outlier in not offering this.
- Initial code investigation suggests this is a contained change: a new boolean in the editor store slice, parameterizing the "physical side" inside the left `Sidebar` and `RightSidebar` components (border, handle position, `deltaSign` in `useSidebarResize`, activity bar `'side'` orientation, toggle icon), and conditionally swapping the render order in `App.tsx`. The only point that needs design attention is the collapsed sidebar header that lives in the top bar.
payload.title: [Feature]: Add a setting to swap left and right sidebar sides

payload.author: leynier
payload.body: ### Short summary When the right sidebar is opened from the **landing screen** (no worktree selected) - and from the **settings** and **tasks** views - its column starts ~42px below the top of the window, sitting beneath the full-width titlebar instead of aligning with it. As soon as a worktree is selected (workspace view, with a terminal), the right sidebar snaps into the correct position: its own 42px header anchors at `y=0`, in line with the rest of the chrome. ### What I expected The right sidebar should anchor at the top of the window (its 42px header at `y=0`) regardless of whether the user is on the landing screen, settings, tasks, or workspace view - i.e., it should look like the workspace-view screenshot in every view. ### What actually happens On landing / settings / tasks, the full-width titlebar covers the top of the window across the whole window width - including over the right-sidebar column - so the right sidebar's own header is pushed down by 42px. ### Reproduction 1. Open Orca with no worktree selected (landing screen). 2. Click the right sidebar toggle in the top-right of the titlebar to open the right sidebar. 3. Observe: the right sidebar's icon row appears ~42px below the top of the window, with the dark titlebar visible above it. 4. Now select any worktree so a terminal opens. 5. Observe: the right sidebar suddenly aligns at `y=0`, with its own header replacing the titlebar on its side. ### Screenshots **Bug - landing view, right sidebar opens below the titlebar:** **Expected - workspace view with a terminal, right sidebar at the top:** ### Likely root cause In `src/renderer/src/App.tsx` (around lines 938–1078) the shell is built as a `flex-col` where the full-width `.titlebar` is rendered **above** the inner flex-row that hosts ``. Because the titlebar spans the entire window width, it sits over the right sidebar's column too, so the right sidebar's own 42px header (`src/renderer/src/components/right-sidebar/index.tsx:305` / `:319`) ends up at `y≈42px` instead of `y=0`. When `workspaceActive` (`App.tsx:535` - `activeView !== 'settings' && activeWorktreeId !== null`) becomes `true`, the full-width titlebar is dropped and each column gets its own 42px header strip, so everything aligns at `y=0`. That's why opening a worktree (which usually auto-spawns a terminal) appears to "fix" the layout. ### Environment - OS: macOS - Orca version: v1.3.30-rc.0 - Branch: `main`
payload.title: [Bug]: Right sidebar opens below the titlebar on landing / settings / tasks views

payload.author: leynier
payload.body:
## Summary

On Windows, every time Orca starts it (re)installs the Claude Code managed hook entry in `~/.claude/settings.json` using the raw `scriptPath` returned by Electron's `app.getPath('userData')` — i.e. with single backslashes:

```
C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Roaming\orca\agent-hooks\claude-hook.cmd
```

When Claude Code runs the hook it invokes the command through Git Bash (`/usr/bin/bash`). Bash interprets the single backslashes as escape characters, so `\U`, `\l`, `\A`, `\R`, `\o`, `\a`, `\c` are stripped and the resulting string is:

```
/usr/bin/bash: line 1: C:UsersleyniAppDataRoamingorcaagent-hooksclaude-hook.cmd: command not found
```

This breaks the `UserPromptSubmit`, `Stop`, `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `PostToolUseFailure` and `PermissionRequest` hooks for every Claude Code prompt on Windows. Manually editing the JSON to use `/` (or doubled `\\`) works, but Orca's `install()` runs again on the next start and overwrites the user's edit with the broken raw path.

## Reproduction

1. Run Orca on Windows. Open Claude Code in any terminal (inside or outside Orca).
2. Send any prompt.
3. Observe the hook errors:

```
❯ Hola
  ⎿  UserPromptSubmit hook error
  ⎿  Failed with non-blocking status code: /usr/bin/bash: line 1:
     C:UsersleyniAppDataRoamingorcaagent-hooksclaude-hook.cmd: command not found
● Hola, ¿en qué puedo ayudarte?
● Ran 2 stop hooks
  ⎿  Stop hook error: Failed with non-blocking status code: /usr/bin/bash: line 1:
     C:UsersleyniAppDataRoamingorcaagent-hooksclaude-hook.cmd: command not found
```

The same error occurs when Claude Code is launched from a regular terminal — it is purely a function of the value Orca writes into `settings.json`.

## Root cause

[`src/main/claude/hook-service.ts`](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/blob/main/src/main/claude/hook-service.ts#L50-L52):

```ts
function getManagedCommand(scriptPath: string): string {
  return process.platform === 'win32' ? scriptPath : `/bin/sh "${scriptPath}"`
}
```

On `win32` the function returns the raw path with backslashes. JSON serialization emits `"C:\\Users\\..."` (correct JSON), and `JSON.parse` returns a string with single backslashes. Claude Code then hands that string to bash unquoted, where backslashes are escape characters.

## Proposed fix

Emit forward slashes on Windows. They are accepted by Windows when invoking a `.cmd` file (Windows path APIs treat `/` and `\` interchangeably for file-system paths) and bash leaves them intact, so the same JSON value works through every shell layer with no extra quoting:

```ts
function getManagedCommand(scriptPath: string): string {
  return process.platform === 'win32'
    ? scriptPath.replaceAll('\\', '/')
    : `/bin/sh "${scriptPath}"`
}
```

The companion `createManagedCommandMatcher` in `installer-utils.ts` already normalizes paths with `replaceAll('\\', '/')` before substring-matching, so existing stale entries written with backslashes are still detected and swept on the next `install()` call (automatic migration).

## Relationship to #1308

Issue #1308 ("Managed hook runtime and PTY spawn env handling drift across layers") describes the same symptom but frames it as part of a broader cross-layer ownership refactor that also covers PTY env shaping and runtime-state isolation.

This issue is intentionally narrower: a single-line fix targeting only the path-escaping bug in `getManagedCommand`, with no architectural changes. The accompanying PR is intended to be a minimal, surgical change that can ship independently of any larger refactor and unblocks Windows users immediately, without prejudicing the wider redesign discussed in #1308.

## Scope

- Affects only Claude Code on Windows. The Codex/Cursor/Gemini hook services share the same `getManagedCommand` shape but their runtime invocation paths have not been verified to exhibit the same bash-escape behavior, so they are intentionally out of scope for this minimal fix.
- OpenCode is not affected: it ships a JS plugin via `OPENCODE_C
payload.title: Windows: Claude managed hook command path uses backslashes that bash strips, breaking every hook

payload.author: akapug
payload.body:
# Orca multi-instance race corrupts `orca-runtime.json` + `agent-hooks/endpoint.env` (no single-instance lock)

## Environment
- Orca **1.3.24** AppImage (build identifier `75d0d6fea22007497deabe192471b490`)
- Ubuntu 25.10 (questing), kernel `6.17.0-22-generic`
- Wayland / GNOME shell
- Filesystem under investigation: `/home/pug/.config/orca/`
- AppImage mounts under: `/tmp/.mount_orca-<token>/` (read-only squashfs, one mount per concurrent instance)

## TL;DR
Orca does **not** call `app.requestSingleInstanceLock()`. Every time the user launches the AppImage (Activities → Orca, `gtk-launch`, double-click, second `xdg-open`, etc.), a new Electron main process starts and unconditionally:

1. Opens a fresh Unix socket `o-<NEW_PID>-<runtimeId-prefix>.sock`
2. Atomically rewrites `~/.config/orca/orca-runtime.json` (tmp → rename) with the new pid / socket / runtimeId / authToken — **clobbering the previously-running instance's metadata**
3. Picks a new random port for the agent-hook HTTP server and rewrites `~/.config/orca/agent-hooks/endpoint.env` with the new port + token

The previously-running orca process keeps its socket + hook port alive, but the canonical metadata files no longer point at it. When the *latest* instance later quits or crashes (no `clearRuntimeMetadata()` call on `will-quit`), the metadata file is left pointing at a dead pid + a unix socket whose path was `rmSync`'d on stop. CLI calls then return `runtimeState: stale_bootstrap` even though older Orca instances are still running healthily.

This is the "drift to stale_bootstrap" the user reported. It is **not** a CLI write race — the CLI is read-only on this metadata. The writer is the Electron main process, and the trigger is "any extra app launch".

## Symptom (CLI output)

Healthy state with one orca running (pid 50926):

```
$ orca status --json
{
  "ok": true,
  "result": {
    "app":     { "running": true, "pid": 50926 },
    "runtime": { "state": "ready", "reachable": true,
                 "runtimeId": "2ad011b0-4915-4a7a-8f61-5d4356a66c5b" },
    "graph":   { "state": "ready" }
  }
}
```

Drifted state after a second launch quits (or any time `pid` in metadata is dead):

```
$ orca status --json
{
  "ok": true,
  "result": {
    "app":     { "running": false, "pid": null },
    "runtime": { "state": "stale_bootstrap", "reachable": false, "runtimeId": null },
    "graph":   { "state": "not_running" }
  }
}
```

The `stale_bootstrap` branch comes from `out/cli/runtime/status.js` — line 19 distinguishes "metadata file exists but pid not running" from "no metadata at all".

## Concrete repro steps (smallest reliable sequence)

Pre-req: a healthy Orca running (call this **Orca A**, pid `$PID_A`).

```bash
# 1. Capture baseline
cp ~/.config/orca/orca-runtime.json /tmp/orca-meta.before
cat /tmp/orca-meta.before    # note runtimeId, pid=$PID_A, socket o-$PID_A-XXXX.sock
orca status --json           # runtime.state == "ready"

# 2. Launch a SECOND orca app instance from the AppImage. Any of these works:
gtk-launch orca.desktop                                # Activities / launcher path
# or:
/path/to/Orca-1.3.24.AppImage                          # direct execve
# or just double-click the AppImage in Files
# (NOT `orca` — the CLI wrapper does NOT spawn a second app, it execs the
# CLI inside an existing AppImage mount in node mode.)

# 3. Watch metadata get clobbered within ~2s of the new window appearing
stat -c '%y' ~/.config/orca/orca-runtime.json          # mtime jumps
diff /tmp/orca-meta.before ~/.config/orca/orca-runtime.json
# All four of pid, transport.endpoint, runtimeId, authToken changed.
# `orca status --json` now reports the NEW pid (Orca B). Orca A is still
# alive and serving on its old socket but is now invisible to the CLI.

# 4. Quit Orca B from its window menu (File → Exit). Orca A stays open.
ps -p $PID_A                                           # still running
ls ~/.config/orca/o-*.sock                             # Orca A's socket
payload.title: orca v1.3.24: missing single-instance lock corrupts orca-runtime.json + endpoint.env on every relaunch — CLI sees stale daemon metadata

## Summary

While testing a recent branch locally, I ran into two problems that at first looked unrelated, but after tracing them through the codebase they seem to stem from the same cross-layer ownership drift:

1. managed hook runtime / launcher behavior is spread across multiple layers and can drift by platform or entrypoint
2. PTY spawn environment shaping is also split across layers, which makes local and daemon-backed behavior harder to reason about and keep aligned

Because I’m still relatively new to contributing here, I wanted to check the maintainers’ view on the problem framing and the proposed direction before assuming a larger refactor would be welcome.

## Problems observed

### 1. Managed hook launcher/runtime behavior can drift across layers

In local testing, I hit failures around the managed hook launcher path / invocation shape, including cases where the generated hook command was no longer invokable in the expected environment.

Visible example from local output:

```text
  ⎿  PreToolUse:mcp__serena__get_symbols_overview hook     ⎿  Failed with non-blocking status code: /usr/bin/bash:
     error                                                     line 1: C:UsersadminAppDataRoamingorca-devagent-hoo
                                                              ksclaude-hook.cmd: command not found
  ⎿  PostToolUse:mcp__serena__get_symbols_overview hook    ⎿  Failed with non-blocking status code: /usr/bin/bash:
     error                                                     line 1: C:UsersadminAppDataRoamingorca-devagent-hoo
                                                              ksclaude-hook.cmd: command not found
  ⎿  PreToolUse:Grep hook error                            ⎿  Failed with non-blocking status code: /usr/bin/bash:
                                                               line 1: C:UsersadminAppDataRoamingorca-devagent-hoo
                                                              ksclaude-hook.cmd: command not found
  ⎿  PostToolUse:Grep hook error                           ⎿  Failed with non-blocking status code: /usr/bin/bash:
                                                               line 1: C:UsersadminAppDataRoamingorca-devagent-hoo
                                                              ksclaude-hook.cmd: command not found
```

This seems related to the fact that:
- launcher registration and managed entry behavior are partly owned by agent-specific services
- runtime publication / endpoint discovery are owned elsewhere
- Windows/POSIX command behavior is not fully centralized

### 2. PTY startup env handling is split across multiple ownership boundaries

I also ran into PTY / shell startup behavior that appears to depend on env shaping happening in more than one place.

Visible example from local PowerShell testing:

```text
PS C:\Users\admin\OneDrive\workspace\@private\orca> claude --dangerously-skip-permissions
claude : 无法将“claude”项识别为 cmdlet、函数、脚本文件或可运行程序的名称。
...
PS C:\Users\admin\OneDrive\workspace\@private\orca> $env:PATH
C:\Users\admin\AppData\Roaming\orca-dev\orca-terminal-attribution\posix;C:\Users\admin\AppData\Roaming\orca-dev\orca-terminal-attribution\win32;C:\Users\admin\AppData\Roaming\orca-dev\cli\bin
```

From tracing the code, this seems to involve:
- partial env resolution happening outside a single orchestration boundary
- provider-side repair / fallback behavior obscuring the real contract
- local and daemon-backed PTY paths being easy to drift apart over time

## Why I think these are related

After digging through the branch, my current understanding is that both issues are symptoms of the same underlying problem:

- managed hook runtime publication, launcher registration, and endpoint discovery are not fully centralized
- PTY spawn env resolution is not owned by one clear boundary
- build-scoped runtime isolation (especially dev vs packaged) is easy to violate when runtime state is treated as globally shared

In other words, the issues show up di

payload.author: nwparker
payload.body:
## Summary
When creating a new worktree through the Orca app, the `setup-runner.sh` it generates is built from the `orca.yaml` of the **primary checkout**, not the `orca.yaml` at the tip of the **target worktree's branch**. If your primary checkout is on an older branch that predates an `orca.yaml` change, every new worktree you create — even off `main` — runs the stale setup script.

## Repro
1. On branch `main` (say at commit A), add a line to `orca.yaml scripts.setup`: `echo "new line"`. Merge to `main`.
2. Switch your primary checkout to any branch that predates that commit: `cd ~/projects/orca && git checkout some-old-feature-branch`.
3. From the Orca app, create a new worktree off `main`.
4. Expected: the new worktree's `orca.yaml` has the new line, and `.git/worktrees/<name>/orca/setup-runner.sh` includes it.
5. Actual: the new worktree's `orca.yaml` has the new line (git is correct), but `setup-runner.sh` contains only the pre-change version — because it was generated from the primary checkout's current HEAD yaml.

## Impact
- Any orca.yaml change rolled out via a PR is invisible to teammates until their primary checkout is on a branch that contains the change.
- Silent failure mode: yaml looks right on disk, setup script disagrees, no warning logged.
- Surfaces in practice when a team uses orca.yaml for environment bootstrap (e.g. populating secrets, agent skills, etc.) — teammates think their setup is broken when actually the runner is stale.

## Expected behavior
`setup-runner.sh` should be generated from the **target worktree's** `orca.yaml` (the file that git checked out into the new worktree), not the primary checkout's HEAD.

## Relevant code
`src/main/hooks.ts` — the `orca.yaml` parser and `createWorktreeRunnerScript`. The `loadHooks(repo.path)` call in `getSetup`/`getArchive` reads from the repo's primary path rather than the worktree path.

## Workaround
Keep primary checkout on `main` (or whatever branch has the canonical `orca.yaml`) when creating new worktrees. Brittle — easy to forget when in the middle of a feature branch.

Made with [Orca](https://github.com/stablyai/orca) 🐋
payload.title: orca.yaml setup hook reads from primary checkout, not target worktree

payload.body:
### Operating system

macOS 26.3.1

### Orca version

1.3.12 (Linear integration shipped in #1007, mergedAt 2026-04-23)

### Details

## Summary

When clicking **Use** on a Linear issue from the Tasks page, Orca creates a worktree against `primaryRepo = selectedRepos[0]` (`TaskPage.tsx:706, 1467`). For users with a single repo connected this is fine, but for multi-repo workspaces (mine has 3) the choice is silent and not user-visible: the issue gets a worktree on whichever repo happens to be first in the persisted `defaultRepoSelection`, with no per-issue override and no way to know which repo got picked until the workspace opens.

The repo filter UI (`RepoMultiCombobox`) is only rendered when `taskSource === 'github'`. On the Linear tab, the slot is occupied by `TeamMultiCombobox` — which filters Linear issues by team but does not influence repo resolution at all. So from the Linear tab there is no visible affordance to choose or even see the target repo.

The "..." menu next to **Use** only offers "Open in browser" — no repo picker, no "open in composer" shortcut.

## Repro

1. Connect Linear (Settings → Integrations).
2. Connect 2+ GitHub repos.
3. Tasks → Linear tab → pick any issue → click **Use**.
4. Worktree appears on whichever repo is first in your saved selection. No prompt, no choice.

## Why this matters

Linear issues are not tied to a repo (unlike GitHub issues, where `item.repoId` comes from the issue itself). Teams using Linear across multiple services (mobile / web / backend) routinely need a single Linear team to feed worktrees into different repos depending on the issue. The current "first selected repo" heuristic forces the user to either (a) only ever connect one repo, or (b) reorder/filter `defaultRepoSelection` manually before each Use — which can only be done from the GitHub tab.

## Possible directions

Three options, ordered by my read of cost/benefit. Happy to write a design doc and a PR once the team confirms direction:

**Option A — prompt at Use time when ambiguous**
Keep the current fast path when only one repo is selected. When `selectedRepos.length > 1`, route the Use click through `openComposerForLinearItem(issue)` (the existing fallback in `handleUseLinearItem`) so the user explicitly picks repo + agent + base branch. Cheapest to implement; preserves current behavior for single-repo users; makes the choice explicit when it actually matters.

**Option B — Linear team ↔ repo mapping in Integrations settings**
Add an optional mapping (e.g. `Platform → platform-core`, `Growth → growth-experiments`) saved alongside `defaultLinearTeamSelection`. `handleUseLinearItem` consults the mapping first, falls back to `primaryRepo`. More UX surface but eliminates the prompt for users with stable team→repo conventions.

**Option C — show `RepoMultiCombobox` on the Linear tab too**
Keep both filters visible (team and repo) when `taskSource === 'linear'`. Lowest UX risk but cluttered, and it doesn't really fit the mental model: on Linear you're filtering issues by team, not by repo.

My read: **A is the right default**, with **B as a follow-up** if multi-repo Linear users keep asking. Open to other reads.

## Notes

- All three live in `TaskPage.tsx` + the `defaultLinearTeamSelection` / `defaultRepoSelection` settings already persisted; no schema changes needed for A.

## Related

- #370 — original Linear integration request (still open after #1007 shipped). This issue is a natural follow-up for the multi-repo case the original ask didn't specify.
- #923 — same shape of problem for GitHub (Tasks picker repo selection for fork-vs-upstream). Different surface, but the underlying concern (give the user control over which repo Tasks targets) overlaps.
- #1099 — multi-repo *workspaces* (one workspace spanning several repos). Distinct feature; flagging here so this doesn't get conflated with that one. This issue is about which single repo a Linear-launched worktree lands in, not about workspaces hosting multiple repo
payload.title: [Feature]: Linear "Use" should let multi-repo users choose the target repo

## Summary

Support doc links (`[[document-name]]`) between Markdown documents in Orca's Markdown management section, so users can link notes together for note-taking workflows.

## Motivation

User feedback from [@kglead on Twitter/X](https://x.com/kglead) (Apr 28, 2026):

> Thank you, it would be great if it were possible to link between documents `[[ ]]` and also to create templates.

Orca is being evaluated as a note-taking tool alongside its terminal/dev capabilities. Strengthening the Markdown section with doc links would make it viable for this use case.

## Suggested behavior

- Parse `[[some-doc]]` syntax in Markdown files and render as a link to the matching document.
- Autocomplete for document names when typing `[[`.
- Clicking a doc link opens the target doc; broken links are visually distinct.

Help wanted — community contributions welcome.

### Operating system

macOS

### Details

**Short summary:**
Unable to type Polish (diacritic) characters in the console — keystrokes are silently swallowed and no character appears.

**What happened?**
When trying to type Polish characters (e.g. ą, ć, ę, ł, ń, ó, ś, ź, ż) in the main console input, nothing happens — the character is not inserted and there's no visible feedback. Interestingly, the same keystrokes work correctly in the Find dialog (CMD+F), so the issue seems specific to the console input field rather than a system-level input problem.

**How can we reproduce it?**

Open Orca on macOS.
Focus the main console input.
Try to type a Polish character using the standard macOS "Polish Pro" layout (e.g. Option+A for ą, Option+C for ć, Option+L for ł).
Observe that no character is inserted.
Open the Find dialog with CMD+F and type the same characters — they appear correctly.

**Anything else that might help:**

OS: macOS
Orca version: v0.14.2
Keyboard layout: Polish Pro (Option-based dead keys)
Regular ASCII input in the console works fine.
The bug appears to be isolated to the console input component — other input fields (Find, presumably others) handle the same input correctly.
payload.title: [Bug]: Unable to type Polish (diacritic) characters in the console — keystrokes are silently swallowed and no character appears.

payload.author: mralexsaavedra
payload.body:
## Problem or use case

The Source Control panel already shows staged/unstaged files, branch compare, and conflict resolution. However, it's missing the core git workflow actions that developers use dozens of times per day:

- **Commit**: no message input + commit button in the panel
- **Push / Pull / Sync**: no way to push or pull without opening a terminal

This forces users to context-switch to the terminal for basic git operations that should live in the Source Control panel itself.

## Proposed solution

1. **Commit area** — add a textarea for the commit message and a `Commit` button (+ `Commit & Push` shortcut) at the top/bottom of the Uncommitted section.
2. **Push / Pull / Sync** — add action buttons in the panel header bar, showing ahead/behind counts against the remote (similar to VSCode's sync button).

**Assignee:** @mralexsaavedra

## Alternatives or additional context

VSCode reference: built-in SCM panel with commit input + sync button.
The IPC layer (`window.api.git`) already has `stage`, `unstage`, `discard`, `branchCompare` — `commit` and `push/pull` follow the same pattern.

> **Note**: Git Graph (visual commit history) is tracked separately.
payload.title: [Feature]: Source Control panel — commit, push/pull, and sync
